findings.evidence: resizeKml (line 2192) and drawKml (3014) are declared inside the KML IIFE (2103-3293) and never exported. The collapse scripts guard with typeof, so they silently skip: `if(typeof resizeKml==='function') resizeKml();` (3396), `if(typeof drawKml==='function') drawKml();` (3398), same at 3513. showApp does `try{fitCanvas?.();resizeKml?.();window.DADS3DResize?.();window.DADSBFMResize?.();draw?.();drawKml?.()}catch(e){}` (3314): an optional call on an undeclared name still throws ReferenceError, so everything after fitCanvas is skipped. Verified in Chromium with the rebuilt original: typeof resizeKml/drawKml/aircraftPitchAtTrack === 'undefined'; after clicking the collapse buttons in KML the canvas stayed 646 px wide while clientWidth grew 646 -> 932 -> 1278.
findings.suggested_fix: Give the KML module a public API (window.DADSKML = {resize, draw} now; an exported module function after the refactor) and have the collapse code call it. Better: a ResizeObserver on each canvas so no module has to be told. Remove the typeof probes so a missing function is an error, not a silent no-op.

findings.note: 4052 3D code writes #kmlTennisReadout from its own rAF loop (4108) with a different solver
findings.title: 3D view overwrites the KML viewer's Tennis-ball readout every frame with a different, disagreeing calculation
findings.user_impact: With Tennis-ball mode on, the KML tab briefly shows its own verdict (OUT OF CONE / IN CONE / INTERCEPT with LOS angle and cone half-angle) and about two frames later the text is replaced by the 3D module's verdict (INTERCEPT / NO INTERCEPT, different wording, different numbers). This happens even when the 3D tab is not open, because the 3D loop never stops. The two engines give different answers for the same inputs, so a student can see two different intercept results depending on which module last drew.
findings.evidence: 3D draw3DDogfightArc writes into the KML panel element: `const readout=document.getElementById('kmlTennisReadout'); ... readout.innerHTML = `${hit?'INTERCEPT':'NO INTERCEPT'}...` (4052-4054), called from draw3D() inside `function loop(){ draw3D(); requestAnimationFrame(loop); }` (4108). Math differs from KML's getKmlTennisSolution (3140): KML shooter speed added horizontally `vx=dir.x*(sv+ballFps*Math.cos(pitch))`, `vz=ballFps*Math.sin(pitch)` (3163-3165), 3D puts shooter speed on the pitch axis `vfps=ballKts*1.68781 + (shooter.spdKt||0)*1.68781` (3987); KML cone is +/-coneDeg/2 (3168, 3190), 3D draws +/-coneDeg (4023); KML predicts the target in a straight line, 3D uses the real future track `a.getInterp(targetId,t+tt)` (4002). Browser test: right after a slider input the readout was `OUT OF CONE ... LOS angle 36.6° / cone ±3.0° ... Pitch 0.0° (native aircraft pitch)`, two animation frames later `NO INTERCEPT Shooter #2 → Target #1 ... Pitch 0.0° (estimated)`.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep one tennis-ball solver (pure function, tested against current KML behaviour first, per the flight-math rule) and have KML overlay, KML readout and 3D arc all call it. The 3D module must only write to its own elements (add a #threeDTennisReadout) and only while its tab is active.

findings.title: 3D module cannot see the KML module's aircraftPitchAtTrack, so its tennis arc ignores aircraft pitch and its attitude fallback is dead
findings.user_impact: In 3D Debrief the tennis-ball arc is always launched level (pitch = only the manual bias) even when the KML data has native or flight-path pitch, so the arc and its INTERCEPT test disagree with the KML view. For tracks without native pitch, the 3D aircraft models are drawn with 0 degrees pitch through climbs and descents instead of the flight-path estimate the KML module already computes (+/-30 deg over a 1.5 s window).
findings.evidence: aircraftPitchAtTrack is a function declaration inside the KML IIFE (2446) and is not on window, but the 3D block probes for it as a global: `const pitchInfo=(window.aircraftPitchAtTrack && a.getTracks?.()[shooterId]) ? aircraftPitchAtTrack(...) : {deg:0,source:'estimated'};` (3984) and `(tr && typeof aircraftPitchAtTrack==='function') ? aircraftPitchAtTrack(tr,t) : null` (3793); pitch then falls back to `p.pitchNative ... ?? 0` (3794). Verified in the browser: typeof aircraftPitchAtTrack === 'undefined'; the 3D readout printed `Pitch 0.0° (estimated)` while KML printed `(native aircraft pitch)`.
findings.suggested_fix: Expose pitch through the existing bridge, e.g. add getPitch(id,t) to window.DADS3DAPI (line 2113) and call that from the 3D block. Add a test pinning the pitch fallback before moving it.

findings.note: scan-bfm-patches#4 (adds: Turn Sim copy silently controls KML playback)
findings.title: 'Auto-hide panels' checkbox exists three times with the same id; the KML one does nothing and the Turn Sim one silently controls KML playback
findings.user_impact: Ticking 'Auto-hide panels' in the KML Viewer toolbar (or in the EM chart card, where a second copy also appears) has no effect when Play is pressed. Auto-hide during KML play is actually controlled by the hidden Turn Sim checkbox, so ticking the box on the Turn Sim tab makes the KML viewer collapse its panels, and unticking the box you can see in KML changes nothing.
findings.evidence: `const toolbars=[...document.querySelectorAll('.toolbar,.kmlToolbar')]; toolbars.forEach(tb=>{ ... label.id='autoHidePlaybackWrap'; label.innerHTML='<input type="checkbox" id="autoHidePanelsOnPlay"> Auto-hide panels'; tb.appendChild(label); })` (3417-3423) matches three elements: Turn Sim toolbar (604), .kmlToolbar (685) and the EM card's toolbar (691). `function autoEnabled(){ const cb=document.querySelector('#autoHidePanelsOnPlay'); return cb&&cb.checked; }` (3426) always returns the first (Turn Sim). Browser test: three #autoHidePanelsOnPlay elements (hidden Turn Sim, visible kmlToolbar, hidden EM card); ticking the visible KML one and pressing Play left body class empty (no collapse).
findings.suggested_fix: Create one checkbox per module with unique ids (autoHideSim / autoHideKml), read each from its own module's Play handler, and don't add it to the EM card toolbar. Better: put the option in the module markup, not a patch script that clones it into every .toolbar.

findings.title: Traffic Pattern Sim: the shell's '← MODULES' button sits on top of the sim's own '2D Map' / '3D' tab buttons
findings.user_impact: The 3D tab of the Traffic Sim cannot be clicked with a mouse: clicking where it is drawn leaves the module and returns to the launcher. 2D Map is 61 percent covered.
findings.evidence:
#trafficReturn is `position:absolute;z-index:5;right:14px;top:7px` above the iframe (416). The sim header right-aligns its tabs in the same spot: `.topTabs{margin-left:auto;...}` and `
` (traffic.html 11, 32). Measured at 1366x768: back button [1259,7,93,29], tab3D [1311,10,41,28] (95 percent covered), tab2D [1235,10,68,28] (61 percent covered); document.elementFromPoint at both tab centres returns #trafficReturn; a real mouse click on the 3D tab closed the embed (trafficEmbed display none, launcher display block).
findings.suggested_fix: Give the embedded apps a reserved shell bar (e.g. a 40 px strip above the iframe holding '← MODULES') so the overlay never lands on app UI, or move the back button to the left where the sim header has only the title. Apply the same pattern to SOF.

findings.title: Collapse rails ('Hide controls' / 'Hide metrics') float over the module launcher and do nothing on the 3D Debrief and Turn Fight tabs
findings.user_impact: The two round arrow buttons and their vertical labels appear on top of the SELECT MODULE screen (and overlap card edges on narrow windows), and on the 3D Debrief and Turn Fight tabs they toggle a hidden flag but no panel moves (button text flips to 'Show controls' with nothing collapsed). The hidden flag then carries into the next module: collapse in Turn Sim and the KML Viewer opens with its Load-KML controls already collapsed to a 44 px strip.
findings.evidence: `.sideCollapseRail { position:fixed; ... z-index:9998; ...}` (3363) ties with `#moduleLauncher{position:fixed;inset:0;z-index:9998; ...}` (299), and the rails are appended to body later (3383), so they paint above the launcher. The layout CSS only targets `main` and `#kmlApp` (3356-3362), never #threeDApp or #bfmApp. State is a body class (leftCollapsed/rightCollapsed), shared by every module. Browser test on the launcher: elementFromPoint at the ◀ button returns collapseLeftBtn; on the 3D tab pressing ◀ left the aside at 300 px (grid 300px 726px 340px) and the label read 'Show controls'; on Turn Fight the aside stayed 320 px.
findings.suggested_fix: Create the rails only inside apps that support collapsing (simApp, kmlApp) and store the state per app (class on #simApp / #kmlApp, not on body). Use one z-index scale for shell overlays.

findings.title: Global Tab-key handler steals keyboard navigation everywhere, including the launcher
findings.user_impact: Pressing Tab (or Shift+Tab) anywhere in the main page except inside an input, textarea or select toggles the side panels instead of moving focus. Keyboard users cannot Tab through the launcher cards, header tabs or toolbar buttons, and cannot Tab into the SOF or Traffic iframes until they click inside them. On the launcher, each Tab silently flips the hidden collapse flags, which then appear in the next module opened.
findings.evidence: `document.addEventListener('keydown',function(e){ if(e.key==='Tab' && !e.ctrlKey && !e.altKey){ const tag=...; if(tag==='input'||tag==='textarea'||tag==='select') return; e.preventDefault(); if(e.shiftKey){ ...toggle('rightCollapsed') } else { ...toggle('leftCollapsed') ...toggle('rightCollapsed') } sync(); } });` Browser test: focus on #play, press Tab: activeElement stayed 'play' and body became 'leftCollapsed rightCollapsed'; on the launcher one Tab produced the same body class.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the Tab hijack (it breaks basic accessibility). If a shortcut is wanted use a non-navigation key such as [ and ], only while the Turn Sim or KML tab is active and no dialog or overlay is open.

findings.note: traffic step() rAF unconditional (452-457); agent measured sim time advancing while hidden
findings.title: Traffic Pattern Sim keeps stepping and redrawing at 60 fps while hidden
findings.user_impact: After opening the Traffic Sim, starting it and pressing ← MODULES, the simulation clock keeps advancing and the canvas keeps redrawing behind the launcher, using CPU (and battery on a tablet). When the user returns, aircraft are wherever they drifted to rather than where they left them.
findings.evidence: `function step(ts){ ... if(playing){ ... t+=dt*mult; aircraft.forEach(...) } draw();updatePanels();requestAnimationFrame(step) } requestAnimationFrame(step);` runs unconditionally, and the shell only sets display:none on the wrapper (main.html 3334-3337). Chromium test: sim time 44.9 s -> 69.1 s while #trafficEmbed was display:none; requestAnimationFrame calls inside the frame kept running at about 60 per second (613 -> 1921 across the hidden period); script time about 14 percent of a core vs 0.8 percent baseline. draw() and updatePanels() also run every frame while paused.
findings.suggested_fix: Have the shell tell the sub-app when it is hidden (postMessage {pause:true}) or use document.visibilityState/IntersectionObserver inside the sub-app; skip draw/updatePanels unless something changed. Tear the iframe down (remove srcdoc) on ← MODULES if state need not be preserved.

findings.title: SOF Dashboard keeps about a dozen timers, a WebSocket and several third-party embeds alive after you leave it
findings.user_impact: Leaving SOF via ← MODULES only hides the iframe (it is loaded once and never unloaded). Weather, radar and traffic polling, per-second clocks, the Blitzortung WebSocket reconnect loop and the airplanes.live, Windy and metar.cloud embeds keep running for the rest of the session, draining battery/data on a tablet and slowing every other module.
findings.evidence: Active (not type=text/plain) timers: `setInterval(loadTraffic,10000);setInterval(loadWx,120000);setInterval(loadRadar,300000)` (757), `setInterval(tick,1000)` (784), `setInterval(refresh,300000)` (840), `setInterval(tickMooseJaw,1000)` (868), `setInterval(refresh,120000)` (892), radar/traffic cycle (976), `setInterval(refresh,30000)` (1008), `setInterval(()=>{mergePriority();update()},30000)` (1059), `setInterval(render,1800)` (1585), lightning `setInterval(...,15000)` plus `new WebSocket('wss://ws7.blitzortung.org/')` with `ws.onclose=()=>{...setTimeout(connect,5000)}` (1680-1686), `setInterval(clean,5000)` (1783), `setInterval(()=>refresh(false),5000)` (2049). Parent: `if(!frame.dataset.loaded){frame.srcdoc=window.__SOF_DOC__;frame.dataset.loaded='1';}` (3346) and the back handler only sets display:none (4310-4313). Chromium test after ← MODULES: the 1000 ms timer fired 36 -> 81 times in 15 s, the 1500/1800/5000 ms timers also kept firing; four nested iframes (mainGlobe, windyRadar, globeFrame, metarCloudFrame) stay loaded. (Sandbox had no network, so the 10 s/2 min/5 min polls were not observed firing.)
findings.suggested_fix: On ← MODULES either blank the iframe (frame.removeAttribute('srcdoc'); frame.src='about:blank') and clear dataset.loaded, or postMessage a pause that clears the intervals, closes the WebSocket and unloads the third-party embeds. In the refactor give each timer an owner and stop it on view deactivate.

findings.note: switchTab re-asserts KML playing (2171); no pause anywhere
findings.module: Turn Sim / KML playback / Turn Fight
findings.title: Simulations and playback keep advancing after you switch tabs or go back to the launcher
findings.user_impact: Start the Turn Sim, KML playback or the Turn Fight, then click another tab or ← MODULES: the animation continues invisibly and the state is different when you return (Turn Sim time, KML time slider and 3D time, Turn Fight time). KML playback keeps driving the 3D Debrief and EM chart too. A student can come back to a KML debrief that has silently played to the end.
findings.evidence: Nothing pauses on switchTab or the ← MODULES handler (`restoredSuiteNavigation`, 4294-4306): switchTab only toggles display (2165-2167) and even re-asserts KML playback (`if(playbackWasRunning) window.DADS3DAPI?.setPlaying?.(true)`, 2171). Turn Sim loop keeps calling stepSim while `running` (1975-1996); kmlLoop advances kmlT while kmlPlaying (3263); BFM `if(run)step(dt)` (4292). Chromium test: Turn Sim t 0.83 -> 3.88 s while the KML tab was showing; BFM 'T+0.8' -> 'T+3.9' while the Turn Sim tab was showing; KML time slider 300 -> 306 while on Turn Sim.
findings.suggested_fix: Introduce a view manager: showView(name) calls deactivate() on the old module (pause playback/sim) and activate() on the new one; keep the '3D shares KML playback' behaviour explicit only between KML and 3D.

findings.title: Three heavy animation loops run every frame in every module, visible or not
findings.user_impact: Once KML tracks are loaded, the 3D scene (ground grid, landscape, planes, trails, several innerHTML rewrites) and the EM chart redraw about 60 times a second even while the user is on the launcher, Turn Sim, SOF or Traffic, and the Turn Fight canvas redraws every frame too. That slows laptops and tablets and speeds up battery drain for no visible result.
findings.evidence: `function loop(){ draw3D(); requestAnimationFrame(loop); }` (4108) with `loop();` at load, no visibility check; draw3D rebuilds `threeDTracks` and `threeDLive` with innerHTML each frame (4092-4105). EM: `function loop(){try{draw()}catch(e){}requestAnimationFrame(loop)}` (4188) started at DOMContentLoaded even though its card is display:none. BFM: `...if(run)step(dt);draw();requestAnimationFrame(loop)` (4292). Chromium test (1366x768): five loops each fired about 295 callbacks in the same window on the launcher; script time on the launcher rose from about 0.8-1.5 percent of a core with no tracks to about 8 percent with the example flight loaded (Turn Sim tab and launcher alike).
findings.suggested_fix: Run each loop only while its view is active (start on activate, cancelAnimationFrame on deactivate) or redraw on demand (on playback tick or control change). Skip DOM writes when text is unchanged.

findings.title: Clicking the KML Viewer tab re-registers a block of unrelated listeners every time
findings.user_impact: Each visit to the KML Viewer tab adds another set of listeners on the VNC chart controls, so after N visits every nudge/scale/opacity slider movement redraws the map N times and the KML map gets progressively laggier. Those controls also do nothing until the KML tab has been clicked once.
findings.evidence: The onclick arrow function opened at 2174 (`el('kmlTab').onclick=()=>{switchTab('kml'); el('kmlEmbeddedVnc')?.addEventListener('change',...);`) is not closed until 2191 (`initKmlOverlayDropdown();}; el('threeDTab')?.addEventListener(...)`), so lines 2175-2190 (kmlEmbeddedVncOpacity 'input', kmlVncResetAlign 'click', kmlVncNudgeX/Y/Scale 'input') run on every click. Browser test: one dispatched input on #kmlVncNudgeX caused 1 canvas clear after the first visit and 5 after five visits.
findings.suggested_fix: Close the onclick after switchTab('kml') (line 2174) and register the VNC listeners once at load. Add a quick test that dispatching one input produces one redraw.

findings.title: EM diagram card's toolbar inherits the global .toolbar overlay style and covers the card title and top of the chart
findings.user_impact: When 'EM Diagram' is ticked, the 'Chart [Auto nearest altitude]', 'EM trail (60 sec)' and a stray 'Auto-hide panels' pill sit on top of the heading 'T-6 Energy-Maneuverability - Real KML Aircraft' (hiding most of it) and over the upper part of the EM chart image where the aircraft dots and trails are drawn.
findings.evidence: The card's controls row is `<div class="toolbar" style="margin-bottom:6px">` (691) and the global rule `.toolbar{position:absolute;top:10px;left:10px;right:10px;...z-index:5}` (14) applies. No override exists for `#kmlEmCard .toolbar`, while the sizing rules assume it is in flow: `#kmlEmCard>div[style*="aspect-ratio"]{height:calc(100% - 70px)...}` (194). Measured: h2 box [341,467,624,15] fully inside toolbar box [341,469,624,44]; toolbar overlaps 16,848 px^2 of the chart box; the screenshot shows the heading covered.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename the class in the EM card (e.g. emControls) or add `#kmlEmCard .toolbar{position:static;margin-bottom:6px}`. Do not reuse layout classes across modules; scope each module's CSS under its root id.

findings.title: KML Debrief Focus Points (DFPs) are stored under one global key and survive across flights and 'Clear'
findings.user_impact: Flags dropped on one flight appear in the list when you load a different flight. Pressing Go To clamps the old absolute time into the new flight's range and pans to the old flight's x/y, so the map jumps to a meaningless spot. 'Clear' on the track panel does not clear them.
findings.evidence: `function dfpStorageKey(){ return 'dadsEzDebrief_dfps_v1'; }` (2722) is the only key; entries hold absolute epoch time and local-frame coordinates: `dfps.push({id:Date.now(),label:...,t:kmlT,x:p.x,y:p.y,lat:p.lat,lon:p.lon,...})` (2745), and loadDfps() (2723) runs once at start. Browser test: after Load Example Flight + Add DFP + Clear, dfpList still showed 'DFP 1 18:19:04Z' and localStorage kept the record.
findings.suggested_fix: Key the store by a flight signature (file names + first timestamp + point count), or keep DFPs in memory and offer explicit export/import. Clear DFPs when new tracks are loaded, or ask.

findings.title: Module launcher's SOF card permanently flashes 'SOF ATTENTION REQUIRED' / 'SOF ACTION REQUIRED' with no weather data behind it
findings.user_impact: Every visit to the launcher shows a yellow flashing 'SOF ATTENTION REQUIRED' alternating with a red 'SOF ACTION REQUIRED' on the SOF card, whatever the weather. Users learn to ignore it, or worry needlessly; a real alert would be invisible among it.
findings.evidence:
Static markup `
⚠ SOF ATTENTION REQUIRED
⚠ SOF ACTION REQUIRED
` (452) animated by CSS keyframes sofAttentionCycle / sofActionCycle (80-92). No script references sofWxCenterAlert; the weather limit logic lives only in the SOF iframe (and the unreachable legacy dashboard). Screenshot of the launcher shows the yellow alert.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the fake alert or drive it from real data (e.g. postMessage from the SOF iframe when a limit is exceeded). If it is only decoration, label it as such and use neutral colours.

findings.title: Shell '← MODULES' button covers the SOF Dashboard's title
findings.user_impact: The first characters of the SOF title ('2 CFFTS') are hidden under the shell's back button, and the button also overlaps the subtitle line.
findings.evidence: `
findings.suggested_fix: Same fix as the Traffic Sim finding: reserve a shell bar or place the back button where the sub-app header has empty space.

findings.title: Two identical 'SINGLE FILE' debug badges are pinned on top of every screen
findings.user_impact: Two dev labels ('SINGLE FILE' and 'SINGLE FILE • SOF RADAR + LIGHTNING • ONE SOF DASHBOARD • WX HIGHLIGHTS V3') sit in the bottom-right corner above every module, the splash, and the SOF and Traffic overlays, one directly on top of the other. They also block clicks in a 415x18 px strip and hide the SOF iframe's own BUILD badge.
findings.evidence:
`
SINGLE FILE
` (4308) and the same style with the longer text (4315), both pointer-events auto. Measured badges: [1285,745,74,18] and [944,745,415,18], z-index 200000; the launcher screenshot shows the label.
findings.suggested_fix: Delete both divs (or show a single version tag in the About page).

findings.title: Legacy SOF dashboard inside main.html is unreachable but still runs and shares names with live code
findings.user_impact: No visible effect except a wasted 1 s timer and about 170 lines of duplicate SOF code that a future editor could mistake for the live SOF. The real SOF (iframe) is a different implementation with different settings, so changes made to this one would do nothing.
findings.evidence: `<section id="sofDashboard">` starts display:none (4317) and is only opened by `window.DADSSOF.show()` (4474), which nothing calls; the launcher opens the iframe (3342-3346). The block still runs `setInterval(clock,1000)` (4433), `load();render()`, a `dadSOF` localStorage key (4466-4467), and its <main>/<aside> elements match the global `main{...}` and `aside,.right{...}` rules (12-13). sofControlDeckSync (4479-4496) only wires this hidden UI.
findings.suggested_fix: Delete the inline SOF section, its style and both scripts (and the SINGLE FILE badge for it).

findings.title: 'dadEzLastTab' is written but never read, and the writes are not guarded
findings.user_impact: No visible effect today (the app never restores the last tab). If the browser blocks storage (private mode, some embedded browsers) the write throws inside showApp and inside each tab click handler.
findings.evidence: `localStorage.setItem('dadEzLastTab',tab);` (3313) and `['sim','kml','threeD','bfm'].forEach(tab=>document.getElementById(tab+'Tab')?.addEventListener('click',()=>localStorage.setItem('dadEzLastTab',tab)))` (3351); grep finds no getItem for this key. Other main-page writes are guarded (3492-3493) but not these.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the key, or read it to restore the last module and wrap access in try/catch.

findings.note: KML IIFE uses Turn Sim globals; literals copied in 3D/BFM
findings.title: Modules rely on each other's private helpers and copy flight constants as literals
findings.user_impact: No visible bug today, but changing a constant or moving code to modules would silently break other modules, and a fix made in one module's copy of a constant will not reach the others.
findings.evidence: The KML IIFE uses Turn Sim's top-level `G0`, `KTS_TO_FPS`, `deg2rad`, `rad2deg` (defined at 780/786). 3D and Turn Fight hard-code their own: `const g=32.174;` (3991), `1.68781` (3803, 3987), `KT=1.68781,G=32.174,NM=6076.12` (4234). The tail of the 3D script (4133-4144) wires Turn Sim controls (`$('rearCheckEnabled')`, `activeList(ac)`, `resetBreadcrumbHistory`) using Turn Sim globals. Static check (eslint no-undef) confirms the cross-block names.
findings.suggested_fix: Move G0, KTS_TO_FPS, FT_PER_NM and the angle helpers into one shared constants module with a test pinning the values; move the rear-check/breadcrumb wiring into the Turn Sim module.

findings.note: 4199-4205 functions do not exist; falls back to a global resize event
findings.title: EM toggle redraws the map by firing a synthetic global 'resize' event at every module
findings.user_impact: Toggling 'EM Diagram' works only because a fake window resize is dispatched; it also makes the Turn Sim, 3D and Turn Fight canvases resize and redraw for no reason (and would break if any of those handlers started to depend on real size changes).
findings.evidence: refreshKmlAfterLayout tests `typeof resizeKmlCanvas==='function'`, `typeof resizeKml==='function'`, `typeof drawKml==='function'`, `typeof drawKmlEmDiagram`, `typeof drawKmlEM` (4199-4205); none of these is a global (resizeKmlCanvas/drawKmlEmDiagram/drawKmlEM do not exist at all), so it falls through to `else window.dispatchEvent(new Event('resize'))` (4201), which fires fitCanvas (792), resizeKml (2193), the 3D resize (3569) and the Turn Fight resize (4293).
findings.suggested_fix: Replace with the KML module's own resize()/draw() (see the first finding).

findings.note: asset 3ee2a7e81a74880c.kml has one -100000.0 altitude fix; 2366 accepts any finite value
findings.title: ForeFlight altitude sentinel -100000 m is loaded as a real altitude (-328,084 ft)
findings.user_impact: In the built-in example flight, #2's third fix is an invalid-altitude sentinel. #2 is the last track to start, so playback begins at that track's first sample and about 7-11 s after Play (18:19:10.96Z to 18:19:15.2Z) #2's interpolated altitude sweeps down to about -328,000 ft. The Live Aircraft panel shows a huge negative Alt, in 3D view mode the ship and its trail spike off-screen, the 3D 'Center Formation' camera averages altitude over all ships (shifts by roughly -80,000 ft), and the flight-path pitch estimate pins at -30 deg. It also draws a permanent spike in the track polyline.
findings.evidence: Data (original/assets/3ee2a7e81a74880c.kml, track #2): '<when>2026-06-02T18:19:14.193749904Z</when><gx:coord>-105.553924 50.334265 -100000.0</gx:coord>' and the matching 'altitude' array value -328083.99. Code: 'altm:Number.isFinite(a[2])?a[2]:0' (2366) then 'altFt:p.altm*KML_FT_PER_M' (2379); no range check anywhere.
findings.suggested_fix: In parseKmlText treat altm < about -1000 m (ForeFlight uses exactly -100000.0) as missing: drop that sample's altitude and interpolate from the neighbouring fixes (or drop the sample). Add a test using track #2 from the examples.

findings.note: projectAll only pans (2384-2385); kmlZoom only set at 2106 default and VNC fit (2691); slider range cannot reach whole-sortie zoom
findings.title: Load Example Flight (and Load Tracks) leaves the map empty: pan is centred on the whole-flight bounding box, zoom is never fitted, and the zoom slider cannot show the whole sortie
findings.user_impact: After Load Example Flight the four aircraft sit on the ramp at CYMJ, but the view is centred about 12.7 NM away (bbox centre of the whole 27 x 39 NM sortie) at zoom 0.09 (only about 1.8 x 1.3 NM visible on a 1000x700 canvas). The canvas shows only grid lines. Even at the slider minimum (0.01, about 16.5 x 11.5 NM visible) the airfield is still off-screen (it is 11 NM north of centre). The user must drag-pan or tick Follow Lead to find anything, so the button looks dead. The whole flight can never be seen at once at any zoom.
findings.evidence: projectAll only sets 'kmlPan={x:-cx,y:-cy}' and never sets kmlZoom; 'kmlZoom=0.09' default (2106); slider 'min="10" max="500"' (line 690) and wheel clamp 'Math.max(.01,Math.min(.5,kmlZoom))' (3272). Example tracks span lon -106.067..-105.351, lat 49.826..50.470 (about 27 x 39 NM); airfield fix -105.555,50.336. Follow Lead checkbox (690) is unchecked by default.
findings.suggested_fix: After projectAll compute kmlZoom from the bbox (same formula as fitEmbeddedVncToView), lower the slider/wheel minimum to about 0.0005, and add a 'Fit' button. For the initial frame centre on the tracks' position at kmlStart (or tick Follow Lead) instead of the whole-flight bbox.

findings.note: loadKmlFiles clears tracks first, no try/catch
findings.title: Load Tracks wipes the loaded tracks before validating, has no error handling, and leaves a stale picture or half-loaded state
findings.user_impact: (1) After Load Example Flight the file inputs are still empty; pressing Load Tracks sets tracks={} then says 'Select at least one KML file first.' Tracks are gone but drawKml/readouts are not refreshed, so the old frame stays on screen while Play, the time slider and DFPs silently do nothing until reload. (2) If any chosen file fails to parse (not KML, KMZ renamed, truncated, no coordinates) parseKmlText throws inside the async click handler: nothing is shown to the user (unhandled promise rejection), tracks already parsed earlier in the loop remain in 'tracks' but with pts=[] (projectAll never ran), kmlStart/kmlEnd are stale, and the earlier good session is lost. (3) Two quick clicks run two overlapping loads on the same tracks object.
findings.evidence: 'async function loadKmlFiles(){ tracks={}; for(let id=1;id<=4;id++){ const f=el("kmlFile"+id).files[0]; if(!f) continue; const txt=await f.text(); tracks[id]=parseKmlText(txt,id,f.name); } if(!Object.keys(tracks).length){el("kmlStatus").textContent="Select at least one KML file first.";return;} projectAll(); ...' - no try/catch, no drawKml on the early return, tracks reset up front. Throw message 'XML parse error' / 'No usable timestamped coordinates found' never reaches the UI.
findings.suggested_fix: Parse into a local 'next' object inside try/catch, show err.message and the file name in kmlStatus, and only replace 'tracks' (then projectAll, draw) when everything parsed; otherwise keep the old tracks. Ignore clicks while a load is in flight.

findings.note: interpolates across GPS gaps up to 81 s with no marker; how to show gaps is a design choice (flag, break line)
findings.title: GPS dropouts are interpolated as straight lines with no marker; spacing, TIGHT/WIDE/FORE/AFT labels and Est G are computed on fabricated positions
findings.user_impact: ForeFlight logs are not 1 Hz continuous: there are in-flight gaps of 6-81 s. In the example flight #2 has 31 gaps over 3 s inside the common playback window, 769 s in total = 12.2% of the 6,288 s debrief, longest 81 s (about 5 NM at 230 kt, during manoeuvring at about 12,250 ft). During those seconds #2 moves in a straight line at constant speed while the app still shows spacing in feet, position labels (TIGHT/WIDE/FORE/AFT/ON PARAMETERS), aspect/HCA/closure and 'Est G 1.00' (straight line = zero turn rate) as if measured. An instructor could grade a pilot on positions that never happened.
findings.evidence: Analysis of original/assets/3ee2a7e81a74880c.kml timestamps, e.g. 'gaps>5s' entries (81.0 s starting +2341 s, 79 s at +2090, 71 s at +1854). interpTrack: 'f=(time-a.t)/(b.t-a.t||1) ... x=a.x+(b.x-a.x)*f' with no check on (b.t-a.t). Other tracks have 6-15 gaps over 3 s inside the window, up to 43 s.
findings.suggested_fix: In interpTrack flag a point as 'interpolated across gap' when b.t-a.t exceeds about 3 s: return {gap:true}, draw the aircraft hollow/greyed, show 'NO DATA' instead of spacing/labels/G, and break the trail polyline at the gap. Add tests pinning interpolation at normal and gap intervals.

findings.note: tracks #1/#2 pitch arrays are blank (thousands of empty gx:value); Number('') is 0 so pitch reads 0
findings.title: Blank ForeFlight 'pitch' array is read as 0 deg, so tracks #1 and #2 report 'native aircraft pitch' = 0 always
findings.user_impact: For the example flight, tracks #1 (Lead) and #2 carry a 'pitch' and 'bank' array with every value empty. Number('') is 0, which passes the finite/abs<=90 filter, so every sample gets pitchNative=0 and aircraftPitchAtTrack returns {deg:0, source:'native aircraft pitch'} instead of falling back to the flight-path estimate. The 3D Debrief shows Lead and #2 permanently level (even in climbs and dives, labelled 'native pitch'), and the tennis-ball solution uses 0 deg pitch whenever #1 or #2 is the shooter.
findings.evidence: 585aab2601b787ed.kml (#1): '<gx:SimpleArrayData name="pitch">' followed by 6,166 '<gx:value></gx:value>' (all blank); 3ee2a7e81a74880c.kml (#2): 5,571 blank. Code: 'const vals=[...node.getElementsByTagName("gx:value")].map(v=>Number(v.textContent.trim())); const clean=vals.map(v=>Number.isFinite(v)&&Math.abs(v)<=90?v:null);' (2351-2352). Same pattern in readNativeGArray (2333-2334) is only saved by its 'v>0' test.
findings.suggested_fix: Map empty/whitespace text to null before Number(): 'const s=v.textContent.trim(); return s===""?null:Number(s)'. Apply to G and pitch readers and the fallback tag readers.

findings.note: iPad sensor pitch/G likely not aircraft attitude; label or hide, Dad to decide
findings.title: ForeFlight 'pitch'/'g_load' for #3/#4 look like iPad sensor attitude, not aircraft attitude, but are shown as 'native aircraft pitch' and 'Native G'
findings.user_impact: For #3 and #4 the pitch values swing wildly (std dev 12-13 deg, raw range -262.7 to +250 deg) and are uncorrelated with the actual climb/descent angle, so the 3D aircraft attitude and the tennis-ball pitch for these ships are essentially random, while labelled 'native pitch'. 'g_load' reads 0.929 (#3) and 1.018 (#4) at rest, so 'Native G' has a per-device bias and the Lead-desired G check uses it directly.
findings.evidence: Computed from original/assets 3085ab3861e2bae6.kml (#3) and 46e14716b39044c4.kml (#4) over airborne samples (GS>=120 kt): corr(pitch, 6-s flight-path angle) = -0.25 (n=4047) and +0.10 (n=3492); 103 of 4,227 airborne #3 samples have |pitch|>90. Last g_load values in the files: 0.929 and 1.018. Source is ForeFlight Web with GPSModelName 'iOS'. (Inference: device IMU, not verified against the aircraft.)
findings.suggested_fix: Do not present these arrays as aircraft attitude: prefer the flight-path pitch estimate, or label them 'device pitch (unverified)' and add a per-track toggle. Consider zero-offsetting g_load using the ground-run median.

findings.note: no window.aircraftPitchAtTrack export; 3D fallbacks never reach it
findings.lines: 2446 (definition), 3793, 3984 (callers); IIFEs end at 3293 and start at 3556
findings.title: The flight-path pitch fallback can never be used by the 3D Debrief or the 3D tennis ball because aircraftPitchAtTrack is private to the KML IIFE
findings.user_impact: 3D attitude uses only p.pitchNative or 0; the estimated-pitch branch that the code comments describe is dead. Combined with the blank-pitch bug all four ships in the example flight show wrong or flat pitch in 3D, and the 3D tennis-ball shooter pitch is always 0 (+ bias).
findings.evidence: 'const pitchInfo = (tr && typeof aircraftPitchAtTrack==="function") ? aircraftPitchAtTrack(tr,t) : null;' (3793) and '(window.aircraftPitchAtTrack && ...) ? ... : {deg:0,source:"estimated"}' (3984). grep finds no 'window.aircraftPitchAtTrack=' assignment anywhere; DADS3DAPI (2113-2129) does not export it.
findings.suggested_fix: Expose the function (and estimatedGAtTrack) on DADS3DAPI, e.g. getPitch(id,time), and call that from the 3D code.

findings.title: Tracks that do not overlap in time silently switch to a union timeline, freezing aircraft at their end points; overlap truncation is also silent
findings.user_impact: If one file is from another sortie or day (easy to mix up when assigning four ForeFlight files), 'kmlEnd<=kmlStart' triggers the union fallback: the timeline can span hours or days, the slider has 1000 steps over that span, every track outside its own interval is frozen at its first/last fix, and spacing/closure/labels are computed between real and frozen positions. The status still says 'Common playback'. Even for valid overlapping flights the window is the intersection, so one late-starting or early-stopping log cuts everyone's playback with no notice.
findings.evidence: 'kmlStart=Math.max(...starts); kmlEnd=Math.min(...ends); if(...||kmlEnd<=kmlStart){kmlStart=Math.min(...starts); kmlEnd=Math.max(...ends);}' and interpTrack 'if(time<=pts[0].t) return pts[0]; if(time>=pts[pts.length-1].t) return pts[pts.length-1];'
findings.suggested_fix: When there is no overlap, refuse to load and name the offending file(s) and their date/time ranges. Show per-track UTC date+time in the summary, and when a track is outside its own range show it as 'no data' rather than frozen.

findings.note: t falls back to index when when[] missing; ForeFlight always writes Z
findings.title: Points without valid timestamps get t = array index (1970), misaligning or wrecking the timeline; the 'timestamped' error text is not actually enforced
findings.user_impact: (1) Any coordinate without a matching <when> (fewer <when> than <gx:coord>, an unparsable date that the isFinite filter dropped, or a plain LineString KML) gets t=index (0,1,2...). After the sort those points move to the front of the track, the track then starts at 1970, and a single-track load produces a 56-year slider. (2) The <coordinates> path uses the per-element index i for '<when>' but the running index for the fallback: 'when[i]??idx', so a second <coordinates> node reuses the first node's times. (3) 'when' is filtered with isFinite but 'gx' is filtered with Boolean, so one bad/empty item shifts all later timestamps by one sample. The message 'No usable timestamped coordinates found' is only raised for <2 points.
findings.evidence: 'let when=[...getElementsByTagName("when")].map(n=>Date.parse(n.textContent.trim())/1000).filter(Number.isFinite);' (2321); 't:when[i]??i' (2366); 't:when[i]??idx' (2369). Date.parse of a zone-less string is read as browser-local time (ForeFlight always writes Z, so this only affects other sources).
findings.suggested_fix: Require one valid timestamp per coordinate (parse when/coord pairwise, keep the pair or drop both), reject the file with a clear message when timestamps are missing, and treat zone-less times as UTC explicitly.

findings.title: Live Aircraft Lat/Lon and DFP lat/lon are the previous GPS fix, not the interpolated position
findings.user_impact: interpTrack returns '{...a, x, y, altFt, ...}': x/y/alt are interpolated but lat/lon (and altm) are copied from the earlier sample. The Live Aircraft panel prints 'Lat/Lon' that steps once per fix and, during a data gap, stays at the pre-gap fix while the aircraft symbol moves up to several NM away (81 s gap at 230 kt is about 5 NM). DFPs store the same stale lat/lon.
findings.evidence: 'return {...a,x,y,altFt,t:time,spdKt:spd,gNative,pitchNative};' (2443); readout 'Lat ${p.lat.toFixed(5)}, Lon ${p.lon.toFixed(5)}' (3250); 'dfps.push({...lat:p.lat,lon:p.lon...})' (2745).
findings.suggested_fix: Set lat/lon from kLocalToLatLon(x,y) (or interpolate lat/lon directly) inside interpTrack, and drop altm from the returned object.

findings.note: listeners added inside kmlTab onclick (2174-2191) on every click
findings.title: KML tab click handler re-registers the VNC/overlay listeners every time the tab is opened, so each slider input redraws N times
findings.user_impact: The entire block that wires kmlEmbeddedVnc, kmlEmbeddedVncOpacity, kmlVncResetAlign and the three nudge/scale sliders sits inside 'el("kmlTab").onclick=()=>{ switchTab("kml"); ... }'. Every visit to the KML tab (launcher entry, 3D 'Go to KML' button, Turn Sim -> KML) adds another copy of each listener. After N visits one nudge-slider tick runs drawKml N times (each may re-warp two VNC charts), so the viewer gets steadily slower and the Reset Alignment handler runs N times. Nothing is wired until the tab has been clicked once (it happens to be, because the launcher calls kmlTab.click()).
findings.evidence: 'el("kmlTab").onclick=()=>{switchTab("kml"); el("kmlEmbeddedVnc")?.addEventListener("change",...); el("kmlEmbeddedVncOpacity")?.addEventListener("input",...); el("kmlVncResetAlign")?.addEventListener("click",...); ["kmlVncNudgeX",...].forEach(id=>el(id)?.addEventListener("input",...)); initKmlOverlayDropdown();};' (2174-2191); showApp does 'document.getElementById("kmlTab")?.click()' (3309).
findings.suggested_fix: Move the addEventListener calls out of the onclick body (register once at load, like the other controls at 3271) and keep only switchTab('kml') in the tab handler.

findings.title: Fit-to-view for the embedded VNC charts sets a zoom the zoom slider and wheel cannot represent; next interaction jumps about 13x
findings.user_impact: Choosing 'VNC South' with no tracks loaded fits the whole chart (about 202 x 151 NM, kmlZoom about 0.0007). The slider min is 10 (0.01) so it is drawn at the far-left stop while the true zoom is 14x smaller; the first wheel tick or slider touch clamps to 0.01 and the view jumps from about 200 NM wide to about 16 NM wide, and there is no way back to whole-chart view except re-selecting the dropdown. When tracks are loaded the fit is skipped entirely (line 2174 condition), so the chart is only readable at the 0.01 minimum zoom.
findings.evidence: 'kmlZoom=Math.min(c.clientWidth/spanX,c.clientHeight/spanY)*0.92;' then 'zs.value=Math.max(+zs.min||10,Math.min(+zs.max||500,kmlZoom*1000))'; slider 'min="10" max="500"'; wheel 'kmlZoom=Math.max(.01,Math.min(.5,kmlZoom))'.
findings.suggested_fix: Allow the slider/wheel range down to about 0.0004 (use a log scale) and add a persistent 'Fit chart' button that works with tracks loaded.

findings.title: DFP flags are stored as ref-relative x/y and never re-projected or scoped to a flight
findings.user_impact: projectAll rebases the local x/y origin on the first point of the first loaded track every load, but DFPs (persisted in localStorage) keep the old x/y and an absolute epoch time. Loading a different flight, or a different subset of tracks, draws old DFP flags at wrong map positions and 'Go To' clamps the time to kmlStart/kmlEnd and pans to the stale x/y. Clear does not remove them, and flags from earlier sorties accumulate in the list.
findings.evidence: 'kmlRef={lat:ref.lat,lon:ref.lon,lat0,R}' (2378, ref=all[0]); 'dfps.push({...t:kmlT,x:p.x,y:p.y,lat:p.lat,lon:p.lon,...})' (2745); 'drawDfps' uses d.x,d.y directly (2770).
findings.suggested_fix: Draw DFPs from lat/lon via kLatLonToLocal (fix lat/lon first, see the interpolation finding), and key stored DFPs by a flight fingerprint (start time or track names) so only the current flight's flags show.

findings.note: 18x18 warp grid redrawn per frame; performance
findings.title: Embedded VNC warp is re-rasterised on every draw: 648 clipped full-image draws and 1,296 warp evaluations per chart per frame
findings.user_impact: With a VNC chart on, every drawKml (each playback frame, each slider input, each satellite/overlay tile that finishes loading, mouse-drag pan) re-renders the 2048x1190 chart as 18x18x2 clipped affine triangles. Playback with VNC 'both' does this for two charts per frame, and drawKml is also called from every tile img.onload, so stutter and dropped frames are likely on iPad/laptops. Triangle seams also show as faint grid lines at opacities under 100%.
findings.evidence: 'const NX=18,NY=18 ... drawTri(ctx,im,s00,s10,s11,d00,d10,d11);drawTri(ctx,im,s00,s11,s01,d00,d11,d01);' and drawTri calls 'ctx.clip(); ... ctx.drawImage(img,0,0)' for the whole image each time (2643-2654).
findings.suggested_fix: Pre-render the warped chart to an offscreen canvas keyed by (chart, nudge, scale) in local-metre space and blit it with one drawImage using the current pan/zoom; only re-render when the alignment sliders change. Throttle tile-load redraws with requestAnimationFrame.

findings.note: hand-tuned VNC georeference; add a 'not for navigation' note
findings.title: VNC chart georeferencing is a hand-tuned fit with no stated accuracy or 'not for navigation' warning
findings.user_impact: The charts are placed as if they were lon-linear/Mercator-lat images between four bounds, then corrected by a hand-entered 3x3 mesh (+-1.4 NM at the corners for North) and one Gaussian control point for South. VNC charts are conic projections, so residual error away from the anchors can be a few NM; the South mesh is all zeros except the one control point. A debrief viewer user could read airspace or landmark positions off the chart without any indication of the error. Cannot be verified against the source chart from the code alone.
findings.evidence: 'south:[[0,0,0,0],[.5,0,0,0],...]' and 'north:[[0,0,-1.0,1.4],[.5,0,0.0,1.0],[1,0,1.0,.5],...]' with the comment 'modest distributed correction removes the residual lake/feature drift'; status text 'Embedded chart images are georeferenced from Moose Jaw, Regina, Saskatoon and chart latitude references.'
findings.suggested_fix: Label the chart layer 'approximate registration - not for navigation', document the control points and residuals in the spec, and add a test that pins the anchor points (CYMJ, Regina, Saskatoon) to their expected screen positions.

findings.note: no GPS spike filter; data-quality design choice
findings.title: Position spikes from poor GPS fixes are plotted and measured as real motion
findings.user_impact: ForeFlight supplies an 'acc_horiz' array but it is ignored. In #2, 165 of 5,571 fixes have acc_horiz over 50 m (up to 174 m), and there are position jumps implying 1,025 kt (19:07:11Z, 527 m in 1 s), 925 kt (18:49:50Z, 476 m, acc_horiz 135) and 704 kt; #4 has four jumps of 458-583 kt. The aircraft teleports up to 1,700 ft in one frame, the GS readout shows 700-1000 kt, spacing/closure spike and the estimated G is corrupted for a few seconds.
findings.evidence: Computed from 3ee2a7e81a74880c.kml and 46e14716b39044c4.kml: implied speed between consecutive fixes vs the T-6 (max about 316 kt in the file speed_kts); 'spd=Math.hypot(b.x-a.x,b.y-a.y)/dt*KML_KT_PER_FPS' (2442) is not sanity-checked.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop or down-weight fixes with acc_horiz above about 50 m or implied ground speed above about 400 kt (or run a small median/Hampel filter), keeping the raw points for the CSV export, and mark the seconds as 'degraded GPS'.

findings.title: Error-injection panel (Enable error / Tight / Wide / Fore / Aft) can never appear because #kmlErrorControls does not exist; the code path is dead
findings.user_impact: Confirms the known missing id. buildKmlErrorControls returns immediately, so kmlErrors[*].on is always false and offsetKmlPoint/errorApplied never do anything. interpTrackWithError still runs headingAtTrack + offset check for every ship every frame. If the panel is ever restored: 'wide' is applied along heading+90 deg, which in this x-east/y-north CCW convention is the aircraft's LEFT (the helper is even named 'right' in kmlAxes), so 'Wide' would move a wingman on Lead's right side toward Lead (TIGHT) and vice versa.
findings.evidence: 'const box=el("kmlErrorControls"); if(!box) return;' (2134); grep finds no id="kmlErrorControls" in the markup; 'rx=Math.cos(heading+Math.PI/2), ry=Math.sin(heading+Math.PI/2)' (2148) with 'lat=(er.latDir==="wide"?1:er.latDir==="tight"?-1:0)*latMag' (2145).
findings.suggested_fix: Delete kmlErrors, buildKmlErrorControls, offsetKmlPoint, the errorApplied branches and the 'if(false)' draw block, or restore the panel and make wide/tight relative to the side of Lead the ship is on.

findings.note: 2411 and markup 651 say '#3 not loaded' (already on known list)
findings.title: Example flight status text hard-codes '#3 not loaded' in both JS and markup although all four tracks load
findings.user_impact: Extends the known finding: the same wrong text is also the initial HTML at line 651, so it is wrong before and after the button is pressed. The example set actually includes #3 (8738A6C9), and the loop order is 1,2,4,3.
findings.evidence:
'Loaded example flight: #1 Lead ED2F5, #2 60DF66, #3 not loaded, #4 083AC.' (2411) and '
Examples: #1 Lead = ED2F5, #2 = 60DF66, #3 = not loaded, #4 = 083AC.
' (651)
findings.suggested_fix: Generate the text from BUILT_IN_KML_EXAMPLES (names and count), and correct the initial markup.

findings.title: Interpolated point at a track's first/last sample omits speed, so GS shows 0 kt and Lead 'SLOW' at the boundaries
findings.user_impact: When time is at or beyond a track's ends interpTrack returns the raw sample object, which has no spdKt. The ship that starts last shows 'GS 0 kt' on the first frame after loading or Reset, and the ship that ends first shows 0 kt at the end of playback (Lead if #1 ends first, which makes the Lead-desired check say SLOW). Harmless when the aircraft is parked, wrong if a log stops mid-flight.
findings.evidence: 'if(time<=pts[0].t) return pts[0]; if(time>=pts[pts.length-1].t) return pts[pts.length-1];' vs the segment path that sets 'spdKt:spd'; readouts use 'p.spdKt||0' (3250) and 'const spd=lead.spdKt||0;' (3099).
findings.suggested_fix: Precompute spdKt (and gNative/pitch) for every sample at load time so the end points and interpolated points are the same shape.

findings.title: Export Combined CSV is not combined or time-aligned, drops G/pitch/speed, silently does nothing with no tracks, and leaks the object URL
findings.user_impact: The file is each ship's raw samples stacked one after another (columns ship,time_iso,lat,lon,alt_ft,x_ft,y_ft), so it cannot be compared side by side; x_ft/y_ft are relative to an origin that is not exported; the -328,084 ft altitude sentinel and GPS spikes are exported as-is; with no tracks the button returns without any message.
findings.evidence: 'if(!ids.length)return; let rows=["ship,time_iso,lat,lon,alt_ft,x_ft,y_ft"]; ids.forEach(id=>tracks[id].pts.forEach(p=>rows.push(...' and 'a.href=URL.createObjectURL(blob);a.download="combined_kml_tracks.csv";a.click();' with no revoke.
findings.suggested_fix: Export one row per second on the common time base (one column group per ship, with G, pitch, GS), include the reference lat/lon, show a status message when empty, and revoke the URL.

findings.note: four a.click() downloads; #2 file name ends .kml.xml
findings.title: Download Examples fires four downloads in one click; browsers block or prompt, and #2 saves as .kml.xml
findings.user_impact: Chrome asks 'download multiple files', Safari/iPadOS commonly keeps only the first, so users may end up with one or two of the four example KMLs. Example #2's stored file name ends '.kml.xml', which Google Earth will not open as KML.
findings.evidence: 'BUILT_IN_KML_EXAMPLES.forEach(ex=>{ ... a.download=ex.file.replace(...); a.click(); ...})' and '"file":"tracklog-60DF664C-9776-48B1-88FB-963FC1508BE8.kml.xml"'.
findings.suggested_fix: Offer the examples as a single .zip (or one button per file) and normalise the file name to .kml.

findings.title: Time slider has a fixed 1000 steps, so a 105-minute flight scrubs in 6.3 s jumps
findings.user_impact: Setting a DFP or pausing at an exact moment is only possible with Play/Pause at low speed; the slider cannot land on a specific second for the example flight (6,288 s window). There are no step-forward/back-1-second buttons.
findings.evidence: '<input id="kmlTimeSlider" type="range" min="0" max="1000" value="0">' and 'kmlT=kmlStart+(kmlEnd-kmlStart)*(+e.target.value/1000)'
findings.suggested_fix: Set the slider max to the window length in seconds (or 10 x seconds) and add +-1 s / +-5 s step buttons.

findings.note: failed tiles cached; no Esri attribution (licence issue for a public site)
findings.title: Map tiles: failed tiles are cached forever, every tile load repaints the whole canvas, and Esri imagery is shown without attribution
findings.user_impact: If the first request for a tile fails (offline briefly, proxy hiccup) img.failed is kept in the cache and that tile is never retried until page reload, leaving black holes in the satellite layer. Each tile's onload calls drawKml() (full scene redraw) so a screen of imagery triggers 20-40 full redraws. The ArcGIS World_Imagery tiles are displayed with no on-screen Esri/source attribution, which their terms require. The tile loop is bounded by the screen but z is clamped up to 19 where the service may return 'map data not yet available' placeholders.
findings.evidence: 'img.onload=()=>drawKml(); img.onerror=()=>{img.failed=true; drawKml();};' with 'cache[key]=img' (2551-2553); template 'https://services.arcgisonline.com/ArcGIS/rest/services/World_Imagery/MapServer/tile/{z}/{y}/{x}' (2570); no attribution text drawn.
findings.suggested_fix: Delete failed cache entries after a timeout so they retry, coalesce redraws with requestAnimationFrame, cap max zoom (about 17) and draw a small attribution string.

findings.title: Overlay is re-projected on every frame and Math.min/max(...spread) is used on whole-track arrays
findings.user_impact: drawSelectedKmlOverlay calls projectKmlOverlay every draw, rebuilding every point of the 210 KB TACNAV overlay with fresh objects (about 60 times per second during playback). projectKmlOverlay also silently sets kmlRef when none exists. projectAll and fitKmlOverlayToView spread whole coordinate arrays into Math.min/max, which throws RangeError above about 65k-120k points (a 10 Hz log of 2 hours, or several long logs) and kills the load.
findings.evidence: 'ov.projected=ov.paths.map(path=>path.map(p=>({x:...,y:...,altFt:...})))' recomputed on each call (2269) and 'Math.min(...xs)' in projectAll (2385).
findings.suggested_fix: Cache the projection keyed by kmlRef and recompute only when kmlRef changes; replace the spreads with a reduce loop.

findings.note: Clear handler 3266 leaves exampleKmlStatus and file inputs
findings.title: Clear leaves the example status, file inputs, time range and reference origin in place
findings.user_impact: After Clear the status still reads 'Loaded example flight: ...' (exampleKmlStatus is untouched), the four file inputs still hold their files, kmlStart/kmlEnd keep the old values, the selected overlay and DFPs remain, and the 3D/EM views read stale ranges from DADS3DAPI.getRange. Pressing Load Tracks then reloads the old files.
findings.evidence: 'el("clearKml").onclick=()=>{tracks={};kmlPlaying=false;kmlT=0;el("kmlStatus").textContent="Cleared..."; ... drawKml();}' - no reset of kmlStart/kmlEnd, exampleKmlStatus or the file inputs.
findings.suggested_fix: Reset kmlStart/kmlEnd, clear the file inputs and the example status text in the same handler.

findings.note: kmlClockMarks/kmlFightingWingCone appear only in markup and draw reads; not in 3271 redraw list
findings.title: Clock Marks and Fighting Wing Cone checkboxes do nothing while playback is paused
findings.user_impact: In a paused debrief (the normal way to use the tool), ticking 'Clock Marks' or 'Fighting Wing Cone' shows no change. The overlay only appears after the user nudges the time slider, pans, zooms or presses Play, so both look like dead buttons.
findings.evidence: Markup line 690 defines <input id="kmlClockMarks" type="checkbox"> and <input id="kmlFightingWingCone" type="checkbox">. The only places these ids are used are the draw-time reads at 3023 (el('kmlFightingWingCone')?.checked) and 3038 (el('kmlClockMarks')?.checked). The redraw-on-change list at 3271 ['kmlTrailMode',...,'kmlLeadGTol'] does not contain either id, and grep finds no other listener for them.
findings.suggested_fix: Add 'kmlClockMarks' and 'kmlFightingWingCone' to the id list at 3271 (or better, one shared 'redraw on any KML control change' handler for every input in #kmlApp).

findings.note: 3069-3083 both spread and offset standards run for #3 when both on
findings.title: Error classification applies the spread-four and offset-box standards to #3 at the same time, so #3 is never 'ON PARAMETERS' with default settings
findings.user_impact: With the default settings (Spread four = On and Offset box = On) an aircraft flying #3 exactly in the correct spot is still labelled FORE or AFT, and the same label can appear twice ('FORE / FORE'). An instructor sees 'errors' that are not errors, or wrong-way labels, on the canvas and in the Live Aircraft Data panel.
findings.evidence: spreadOn block (3069-3074) tests foreAft against +/-kmlForeAftTol (250 ft of Lead's 3/9), then the offsetOn && id===3 block (3076-3083) tests offsetAftFt=-foreAft against 8000 +/-1000 ft. Both run for #3 whenever both selects are 'on' (the defaults at 698 and 702). Worked examples: #3 abreast at 5000 ft lateral, foreAft=0 -> spread OK but offsetAftFt=0 < 7000 so labels.push('FORE'); #3 correctly 8000 ft aft in the offset box -> foreAft=-8000 < -250 so labels.push('AFT') from the spread block even though offsetStatus='OFFSET OK'; #3 500 ft fore of 3/9 -> 'FORE' pushed by both blocks -> 'FORE / FORE'. offsetStatus (3075/3082) is computed and returned but never displayed.
findings.suggested_fix: Model the formation type explicitly (Spread four vs Offset box) instead of two independent toggles. When the offset standard is active for #3, skip the 3/9 fore/aft test in the spread block (or evaluate spread lateral interval only). De-duplicate labels. Pin current outputs with a unit test first (CLAUDE.md flight-math rule), then change.

findings.note: classifyLeadDesired compares ground speed to 200 kt target; EM converts GS to IAS elsewhere. Dad to say which speed the target means
findings.title: Lead 'desired parameters' compare ground speed against a 200 kt target that is normally an indicated airspeed
findings.user_impact: Lead flying the briefed 200 KIAS at typical Moose Jaw working altitudes is reported FAST (or the target is meaningless), so the SLOW/FAST label on Lead is wrong by 10 percent or more; at 8000 ft ISA 200 KIAS is about 225 kt ground speed in still air, outside the +/-10 kt tolerance. Wind shifts it further.
findings.evidence: classifyLeadDesired: `const spd=lead.spdKt||0; if(spd < targetKt-speedTol) labels.push('SLOW'); else if(spd > targetKt+speedTol) labels.push('FAST');` where spdKt is horizontal ground speed from x/y (2442: `Math.hypot(b.x-a.x,b.y-a.y)/dt*KML_KT_PER_FPS`). The EM diagram in the same app converts ground speed to IAS with `gs*Math.sqrt(isaRhoRatio(alt))` (4158, isaRhoRatio at 4154), and its note says 'Uses KML ground speed as TAS proxy, converts to estimated IAS with ISA density' (691). The Lead-target field is labelled only 'Lead target speed kt' (706).
findings.suggested_fix: Confirm with the owner whether 200 is IAS or GS. If IAS, convert GS to estimated IAS (same isaRhoRatio as the EM diagram, ideally one shared function) before comparing, and label the field 'KIAS (est.)'. Add a test pinning the old behaviour before changing.

findings.note: resizeKml/drawKml live inside the KML IIFE (2103-3293); launcher 3314 throws ReferenceError (swallowed) and collapse-panels typeof checks (3396, 3513) skip them
findings.title: KML canvas is never resized after collapsing the side panels or after launching a module (resizeKml/drawKml are out of scope, ReferenceError swallowed)
findings.user_impact: After pressing the 'Hide controls' / 'Hide metrics' side tabs in the KML Viewer the map canvas keeps its old bitmap size and is CSS-stretched (distorted icons, drag/pan drifting from the cursor) until the browser window is resized or the tab is switched. This is part of why the collapse tabs feel broken.
findings.evidence: resizeKml and drawKml are declared inside the KML IIFE (2192, 3014, closed at 3293) and are not on window. The launcher IIFE calls `try{fitCanvas?.();resizeKml?.();window.DADS3DResize?.();window.DADSBFMResize?.();draw?.();drawKml?.()}catch(e){}` (3314). `resizeKml?.()` on an undeclared name throws ReferenceError (optional chaining does not guard unresolvable identifiers), the empty catch hides it, and everything after it is skipped. The collapse code has the same defect in another form: `if(typeof resizeKml==='function') resizeKml();` (3396, 3513) is always false from outside the IIFE, and neither script dispatches a window 'resize' event.
findings.suggested_fix: Expose an explicit API from the KML module (e.g. window.DADSKmlResize, like DADS3DResize/DADSBFMResize) or dispatch new Event('resize') after layout changes; delete the dead typeof checks. In the ES-module refactor import the function instead of probing globals.

findings.note: 3084 fallback fires for #2/#4 when only offset is on
findings.title: Aircraft with no applicable standard are labelled 'ON PARAMETERS'
findings.user_impact: With Spread four = Off and Offset box = On (or Offset On and any aircraft other than #3), #2 and #4 are shown 'ON PARAMETERS' although nothing was checked for them; this gives false reassurance in a debrief.
findings.evidence: `if(!labels.length && (spreadOn||offsetOn)) labels.push('ON PARAMETERS');` but the offset test only runs for `id===3` (3076), so for #2/#4 with spreadOn=false the labels array is always empty and the fallback fires.
findings.suggested_fix: Track whether any standard was actually evaluated for this aircraft; only add 'ON PARAMETERS' if at least one check ran, otherwise return null / 'NO STANDARD'.

findings.note: 3038 tests 'ON SPACING' but KML classifier only emits 'ON PARAMETERS'
findings.title: On-canvas position labels never turn green: code tests for 'ON SPACING' but the classifier emits 'ON PARAMETERS'
findings.user_impact: A wingman in position is drawn with the same amber colour as FORE/AFT/WIDE errors; only TIGHT is blue. The intended green 'good' cue never appears.
findings.evidence: 3038: `ctx.fillStyle=pos.labels.includes('ON SPACING')?'#7ee787':(pos.labels.includes('TIGHT')?'#58a6ff':'#ffcc66')`. classifyKmlError only ever pushes TIGHT, WIDE, FORE, AFT and 'ON PARAMETERS' (3070-3084); the string 'ON SPACING' exists nowhere else.
findings.suggested_fix: Compare against 'ON PARAMETERS' (or, better, colour from a structured status field rather than string matching).

findings.note: 2431 returns raw end points without spdKt
findings.title: First and last playback frame shows GS 0 kt, Lead flagged SLOW, and the tennis solution loses shooter speed
findings.user_impact: Right after Load, after Reset, and at the end of playback, the aircraft whose track starts latest (or ends earliest) reads 'GS 0 kt'; if that is Lead the 'Lead desired' line says SLOW, and the tennis-ball path is computed with a stationary shooter.
findings.evidence: interpTrack returns the raw point object at the clamp ends: `if(time<=pts[0].t) return pts[0]; if(time>=pts[pts.length-1].t) return pts[pts.length-1];` (2431). Raw points (2366/2369/2379) have no spdKt, so `Math.round(p.spdKt||0)` (3250), `const spd=lead.spdKt||0` (3099) and `const sv=(shooter.spdKt||0)*KTS_TO_FPS` (3158) all become 0. kmlStart is the max of the track start times (2380) so at least one track is always on this clamp path at t=kmlStart.
findings.suggested_fix: In interpTrack compute spdKt (and heading) for the end points from the adjacent segment, or precompute spdKt on every point in projectAll. Test at t=kmlStart and t=kmlEnd.

findings.note: bubble uses 2D projection formula; not rendered by me
findings.title: Safety bubble is drawn at the wrong place in the 3D altitude view
findings.user_impact: With View mode = '3D altitude view' the 500 ft bubble floats away from its aircraft (it ignores the oblique projection and the altitude lift) and is a circle where the ground-plane circle should be squashed, so the visual separation check is misleading.
findings.evidence: drawKmlSafetyBubble computes screen position by hand with the 2D formula: `const sy=kc().height/2 - (p.y+kmlPan.y)*kmlZoom*devicePixelRatio;` while kWorldToScreen in 3D uses `c.height/2-((y+kmlPan.y)*0.55 + z*0.45)*kmlZoom*devicePixelRatio`. The comment above it claims 'use the exact same zoom scale as aircraft positions'.
findings.suggested_fix: Use kWorldToScreen(p.x,p.y,kmlIs3D()?p.altFt:0) for the centre and draw an ellipse (ry = 0.55*rr) in 3D. Consider whether the bubble should also account for vertical separation.

findings.note: tennis solution ignores vertical velocity; physics choice for Dad
findings.title: Tennis-ball solution ignores the climb/descent of both the shooter and the target
findings.user_impact: Intercept status and 'closest pass' are wrong for climbing or descending aircraft; for example a target descending at 2000 fpm moves about 100 ft in 3 s that the model does not include, against a default 250 ft hit radius.
findings.evidence: Ball velocity is `vx=dir.x*(sv+ballFps*Math.cos(pitch))`, `vz=ballFps*Math.sin(pitch)` where sv is horizontal ground speed only, so the shooter's own vertical speed is not added to the ball; target is `targetV={x:tdir.x*tv,y:tdir.y*tv,z:0}` with z hard-coded to 0. The pitch used can be the estimated flight-path angle (2446-2459), which makes the missing shooter vertical term more visible.
findings.suggested_fix: Add shooter and target vertical speed (from the interpolated altFt slope) to vz / targetV.z. Write a test that pins current outputs for level flight first, then change.

findings.note: INTERCEPT independent of cone; cone length math per code
findings.title: Tennis 'INTERCEPT' status is independent of the cone setting, and the drawn cone is shorter than the ball path
findings.user_impact: The readout can say INTERCEPT while also showing 'LOS angle 8.0 / cone +/-3.0', and the yellow cone triangle ends short of where the ball actually travels, so users cannot tell what the 'Cone width deg' input does.
findings.evidence: status='INTERCEPT' if `best.dist<=hitRadius` (3181) regardless of `inConeNow` (3168, only used for 'IN CONE'). At 1500 ft range a 250 ft radius already accepts about +/-9.5 degrees. The cone length `maxR=(sol.ballKt*KTS_TO_FPS*sol.tof)` (3189) excludes the shooter speed that the ball path includes (`sv+ballFps*cos(pitch)`, 3163), so the cone edge is about sv*tof (about 1000 ft at 200 kt) shorter than the path.
findings.suggested_fix: Decide the intended semantics (cone gate vs hit radius) and show both clearly; draw the cone with the same relative-to-ground length as the ball path. Also the 0.15 s sampling (3171) can miss the true closest approach by up to about 60 ft at high closure; solve the closest approach analytically.

findings.note: 3263 end check stops play on the next frame; Play at end does nothing
findings.title: Pressing Play at the end of the flight does nothing
findings.user_impact: After a run reaches the end, Play appears dead; the user has to know to press Reset first.
findings.evidence: kmlPlay.onclick only sets `kmlPlaying=true;kmlLastReal=performance.now()` (3269). kmlLoop immediately hits `if(kmlT>=kmlEnd){kmlT=kmlEnd;kmlPlaying=false;}` (3263) on the next frame.
findings.suggested_fix: In the Play handler, if kmlT>=kmlEnd then set kmlT=kmlStart (and update the slider) before starting.

findings.note: single dfp storage key; Clear does not touch dfps
findings.title: DFPs are stored globally, not per flight, and survive Clear / loading a different flight
findings.user_impact: DFP flags and notes from an earlier flight (possibly another student's) show up on the map of a different flight, and 'Go To' jumps to a clamped time and stale x,y. Flags remain on an empty canvas after 'Clear'. Notes persist in the browser indefinitely with no way to tell which flight they belong to.
findings.evidence: One fixed key: `function dfpStorageKey(){ return 'dadsEzDebrief_dfps_v1'; }`. Stored records hold only `{id,label,t,x,y,lat,lon,altFt,note}` (2745); x,y are feet relative to the first point of the lowest-numbered loaded track (2378), so they change with the track set. drawDfps has no tracks check and the Clear handler (3266) never touches dfps.
findings.suggested_fix: Key DFPs by a flight fingerprint (track file names + start/end time) or store them with the loaded flight; hide/ignore DFPs whose fingerprint does not match; offer export/import of DFPs with notes.

findings.note: per-frame DOM lookups per vertex; performance, not a bug
findings.title: KML redraw loop re-projects every track vertex and rewrites five readout panels every animation frame, even when the KML tab is not visible
findings.user_impact: Long tracks (4 ships x thousands of points) make playback choppy on tablets/laptops; playback started from the 3D tab or left running behind the launcher keeps rendering the hidden KML canvas at 60 fps; readout text cannot be selected while playing.
findings.evidence: kmlLoop calls drawKml() and updateKmlReadouts() every frame while kmlPlaying. drawKml strokes the full trail with `tr.pts.forEach(p=>{... kWorldToScreen(p.x,p.y,kmlIs3D()?(p.altFt||0):0) ...})` and each kWorldToScreen does kc() and kmlIs3D() (getElementById + .value) so about 3 DOM lookups per vertex. Line 3032 adds `Object.values(tracks).find(t=>t.pts.includes(p))` per live point per frame, a linear scan whose result is unused. updateKmlReadouts sets innerHTML on kmlLive, kmlAspectHca, kmlSpacing, kmlTennisReadout each frame. The '← MODULES' handler (restoredSuiteNavigation, 4294-4306) does not pause playback.
findings.suggested_fix: Cache is3D/canvas per frame, pre-project or cache the trail path (Path2D) and only redraw it on zoom/pan/mode changes, remove line 3032, update readouts at about 10 Hz or only when values change, skip drawKml when #kmlApp is hidden, and pause on leaving the module.

findings.title: Ship #4's colour (#050505) is unreadable on the dark UI (readouts, trail, bubble, clock marks)
findings.user_impact: #4's name in 'Live Aircraft Data' and 'Aspect / HCA / Closure' is near-black text on the near-black card, and with satellite imagery off (the default, 658) or in 3D mode (imagery is disabled) its 3 px trail, bubble and clock ring nearly vanish into the #071018 canvas.
findings.evidence: KML_COLORS={...,4:'#050505'} (2104). `#${tr.id}` (3228, 3250) on `.card{background:var(--panel2)}` = #0e1720; trail `ctx.strokeStyle=tr.color` (3026); bubble `ctx.strokeStyle=KML_COLORS[id]` (3008); clock marks `ctx.strokeStyle=tr.color` (2896). Only the silhouette gets a white outline for id 4 (2932).
findings.suggested_fix: Give #4 a light colour (or a white halo/outline for trail, bubble, ring and a text-shadow/badge for readouts) so it is legible on both dark and satellite backgrounds.

findings.note: mouse-only listeners (tablets are secondary per Patrick)
findings.title: KML map cannot be panned or zoomed by touch
findings.user_impact: On an iPad/phone (the 'anyone, anywhere' requirement) the map cannot be dragged and there is no pinch zoom; only the zoom slider works. Debriefs on tablets are a likely use.
findings.evidence: Only `mousedown`, `mousemove`, `mouseup` and `wheel` listeners are attached to #kmlCanvas; no pointer or touch events.
findings.suggested_fix: Switch to Pointer Events (pointerdown/move/up with setPointerCapture, two-pointer pinch) and add `touch-action:none` on the canvas.

findings.note: horizontal vs 3D range; label or unify, Dad to choose
findings.title: Different 'range' definitions in different panels: spacing, aspect and closure are horizontal-only while the tennis solution uses 3D range
findings.user_impact: The same pair of aircraft shows two different ranges (e.g. 3000 ft in the Aspect panel vs 3162 ft in the tennis readout). Two ships stacked 1000 ft apart directly above each other read '0 ft' spacing, and the bubble overlaps, which can be read as a conflict when altitude separation exists (or the reverse, a horizontal gap that hides a collision course in altitude).
findings.evidence: Spacing lines/readouts: `Math.hypot(a.x-b.x,a.y-b.y)` (3030, 3256), aspect range `Math.hypot(p.x-lead.x,p.y-lead.y)` (3223), closure uses horizontal hypot (3126-3127); tennis range: `Math.hypot(target.x-shooter.x,target.y-shooter.y,(target.altFt||0)-(shooter.altFt||0))` (3183). Nothing on screen says 'horizontal'.
findings.suggested_fix: Label spacing values 'horiz' and add a 'slant/3D' value (and vertical separation) or switch consistently; document the choice in SPEC. Consider a 3D sphere option for the safety bubble.

findings.title: Traffic sim's '← MODULES' return button sits on top of the traffic sim's own 2D Map / 3D tab buttons
findings.user_impact: In the Traffic Pattern Sim the host's return button covers the right-hand '3D' tab and part of '2D Map', so the 3D view toggle cannot be clicked at full window width.
findings.evidence: #trafficReturn{position:absolute;z-index:5;right:14px;top:7px;...padding:7px 12px} (416) is placed over an iframe that fills the container (415). The sim header (traffic.html 10-11, 32) is `padding:0 14px` with `.topTabs{margin-left:auto}` holding `<button id="tab2D">2D Map</button><button id="tab3D">3D</button>` at the same top-right corner; the sim reserves no space for the host button.
findings.suggested_fix: Give the embed a host bar (e.g. 36 px strip above the iframe containing the return button) instead of overlaying the iframe, or move the button to the sim's header via postMessage. Same pattern should be checked for #sofStandaloneBack (443) over the SOF header.

findings.title: Playback jumps forward after the browser tab was hidden
findings.user_impact: If playback is running and the user switches browser tabs/apps and comes back, the clock jumps ahead by the hidden time x playback speed (or straight to the end).
findings.evidence: `const realDt=(now-kmlLastReal)/1000; kmlT+=realDt*(+el('kmlSpeed').value||1);` with kmlLastReal only updated inside the rAF callback, which is not called while the tab is hidden; realDt is not clamped.
findings.suggested_fix: Clamp realDt (e.g. Math.min(realDt,0.1)) or pause on document.visibilitychange.

findings.note: label from length, not sorted by time
findings.title: DFP labels can duplicate and Prev/Next follow creation order, not flight time
findings.user_impact: After deleting a DFP and adding another, two flags can carry the same 'DFP n' label. Because DFPs are added at whatever time the user scrubbed to, Prev/Next jump around in time instead of stepping chronologically.
findings.evidence: `label:'DFP '+(dfps.length+1)` (2745) with splice-delete (2756); prev/next use plain array index (3277-3278); the array is never sorted by t.
findings.suggested_fix: Use a monotonically increasing counter for labels (or label by time); sort dfps by t on insert, or step Prev/Next by time order.

findings.title: DFP storage is not validated or escaped and failures are silent
findings.user_impact: If the stored value is valid JSON but not an array (e.g. 'null'), updateDfpList throws at load time and the statements after loadDfps() on line 3292 (buildKmlErrorControls, resizeKml, requestAnimationFrame(kmlLoop)) never run, which would disable KML playback. Storage-full errors are swallowed, so the user believes notes were saved.
findings.evidence: `function loadDfps(){ try{ dfps=JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(dfpStorageKey())||'[]'); }catch(e){ dfps=[]; } updateDfpList(); }` (2723); `if(!dfps.length)` at 2759 throws for null. `saveDfps` has `catch(e){}` (2724). `🚩 ${d.label}` (2763) is not escaped although note text is.
findings.suggested_fix: Validate with Array.isArray and per-field checks after parse, escape label, and surface a small 'could not save notes' message.

findings.note: if(false) block and early return in buildKmlErrorControls (kmlErrorControls missing)
findings.title: Dead code in drawKml: unused per-frame lookup, permanently disabled error-overlay block, and unreachable error injection
findings.user_impact: No visible effect except wasted work and confusion for future maintainers; the per-aircraft 'Enable error' injection is unreachable because #kmlErrorControls does not exist, so every interpTrackWithError call is just interpTrack.
findings.evidence: 3032: `Object.values(live).forEach(p=>{ ... let id=Object.values(tracks).find(t=>t.pts.includes(p))?.id || p.id; });` computes s and id and discards them. 3033: `if(false){ ... raw vs error ghost markers ... }`. buildKmlErrorControls returns immediately (`const box=el('kmlErrorControls'); if(!box) return;`, 2134), so kmlErrors[*].on is always false and offsetKmlPoint returns p unchanged (2144). Also the 'right' vector everywhere is (cos(h+90 deg), sin(h+90 deg)), which in this east/north frame is the aircraft's LEFT, so 'wide/tight' in offsetKmlPoint (2145) would push in the wrong direction for aircraft on one side of Lead.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove 3032-3035. Decide whether to restore the error-injection UI; if yes, fix the side convention and add tests, if not delete kmlErrors/offsetKmlPoint/buildKmlErrorControls and use interpTrack directly.

findings.title: In the 3D altitude view, dragging pans at the wrong rate and the grid does not follow the tilted ground plane
findings.user_impact: Dragging the map vertically in 3D mode moves the map only about half as far as the cursor; the 5000 ft grid squares are drawn square while the 3D ground projection compresses y by 0.55, so the grid misrepresents distances in 3D.
findings.evidence: mousemove: `kmlPan.y=kmlDrag.pan.y-(e.offsetY-kmlDrag.y)/(kmlZoom)` (no 0.55), whereas kWorldToScreen uses `(y+kmlPan.y)*0.55` and kScreenToWorld divides by `yScale=kmlIs3D()?0.55:1` (2497). Grid: `const grid=5000*kmlZoom*devicePixelRatio` used for both x and y spacing (3020).
findings.suggested_fix: Divide the y drag by 0.55 in 3D and use grid*0.55 for horizontal grid-line spacing (and ideally skew the grid by altitude offset).

findings.title: In the 3D altitude view aircraft silhouettes and clock marks point in the 2D heading direction, not along the projected track
findings.user_impact: Aircraft icons appear to point up to about 16 degrees away from their own trail in 3D mode (worst at 45 degree headings), and the clock ring is not aligned with the drawn 3/9 line.
findings.evidence: Silhouette and ring both use `ctx.rotate(-hdg+Math.PI/2)` with the raw math heading, but positions go through the 3D projection with y*0.55 so the on-screen direction of travel is atan2(0.55*sin h, cos h).
findings.suggested_fix: In 3D mode rotate by the projected direction (project p and p+unit heading vector and use the screen delta).

findings.title: Two splash-screen 'route' buttons are wired but permanently hidden
findings.user_impact: No visible effect (the buttons are hidden), but they are dead controls whose labels promise to open the Formation Simulator / KML Viewer while their handler only opens the module launcher.
findings.evidence: `.splashRoute{display:none!important}` (273); `<button class="splashRoute" id="enterSim" aria-label="Open Formation Simulator">` and `id="enterKml"` (408-409) both get `addEventListener('click',showLauncher)`.
findings.suggested_fix: Delete both buttons, their CSS (55-57, 273) and handlers.

findings.title: 'dadEzLastTab' is written but never read, and the unguarded write can abort showApp
findings.user_impact: The last-used tab is never restored (no effect). In browsers where localStorage access throws (blocked storage, some private modes), showApp() throws before its post-launch resize call.
findings.evidence: `localStorage.setItem('dadEzLastTab',tab);` (3313) and the same key written again on every tab click (3351); grep finds no getItem for 'dadEzLastTab'. Elsewhere in the same file localStorage use is wrapped in try/catch (e.g. 2723-2724).
findings.suggested_fix: Delete both writes, or read the key on start and wrap access in try/catch.

findings.title: Live 'Lat/Lon' readout (and DFP lat/lon) is not interpolated
