findings.title: Launcher's '← MODULES' button covers the SOF title and subtitle
findings.user_impact: The back button (drawn by the parent page over the SOF iframe) hides '2 CFFTS •' and the first words of 'LIVE WEATHER + TRAFFIC COMMON OPERATING PICTURE'. Two always-on debug badges from the parent (bottom right, z-index 200000) and the SOF's own 'BUILD: DATE-AWARE / PROB30 FIX / SMART LAUNCHER' badge (sof.html 766) also sit over the lightning card and the bottom of the right column.
findings.evidence: main.html 443: `<button id=sofStandaloneBack style="position:absolute;top:9px;left:10px;z-index:100002...">` is a sibling of the iframe (444) that fills the same box; sof.html `.top` has `padding:0 14px` and the title starts at x=14,y~12. Rendering the parent markup with the decoded SOF as srcdoc shows the button over the title. Badges: main.html 4308 'SINGLE FILE', 4315 'SINGLE FILE • SOF RADAR + LIGHTNING • ONE SOF DASHBOARD • WX HIGHLIGHTS V3' (also claims highlights and lightning that do not work), sof.html 766 BUILD badge.
findings.suggested_fix: Reserve a header strip for the back button (put it in the SOF header as a real element or add left padding to .top), and remove the three fixed debug badges.

findings.title: After every weather refresh the right-rail airfield (CYYN by default) vanishes from the weather column for up to 30 s
findings.user_impact: Every 5 minutes, and every time ⟳ WX is pressed, one of the four airfield cards (the right-rail one, CYYN with the default alternates) disappears from view until a later timer moves it back. On a desk display this looks like a dropped feed.
findings.evidence: standaloneWeatherFeed.refresh() rebuilds both containers: `L.innerHTML=leftPrimary...; R.innerHTML=rightPrimary...` (827-828), with rightPrimary = odd-indexed alternates (790). The dock script hid the right rail's children with `old.forEach(el=>{ if(el!==rail) el.style.display="none"; })` (1085). The card is only moved into the visible left rail by mergePriority(), which runs on `setInterval(...,30000)` (1059). Headless run: at t=3 s all 4 cards visible; 0.8 s after clicking ⟳ WX: `CYYN:HIDDEN:wxRight`; 32 s later `CYYN:visible:wxLeft`.
findings.suggested_fix: Render all primary cards into one container (leftPrimary + rightPrimary in wxLeft) and delete the wxRight/mergePriority/dock machinery.

findings.title: Weather feed failure wipes the last good METAR/TAF and shows no error, status or observation age
findings.user_impact: If datamask.org is unreachable (network drop, DNS, rate limit) the four cards silently change to 'NO METAR AVAILABLE / NO TAF AVAILABLE' with grey 'UNK' category, replacing the last known weather until a later refresh succeeds (up to 5 min, unbounded if the outage lasts). Nothing tells the user the feed is down vs the station has no report, and a feed that is up but serving an old METAR is indistinguishable from a fresh one because no observation time or age is displayed.
findings.evidence: station() uses `Promise.allSettled` and maps every rejection or non-OK to null (802-803); card() prints `r.metar?.raw||"NO METAR AVAILABLE"` (809-810). The status element the code writes to does not exist: `const status=document.getElementById("wxstatus")` (820) is null so the LOADING/LIVE/WX ERROR text (821, 831, 834) is never shown, and the catch block (832-835) has nothing to display. Headless run with datamask requests aborted then ⟳ WX: all four cards read `cat=UNK | NO METAR AVAILABLE`; document.getElementById('wxstatus') is null. Fetches have no timeout (794-799). The NATO markers also drop those airfields because they skip cards whose text matches /NO METAR/ (994, 1044).
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the last good report per station and mark it STALE with its age (parse the DDHHMMZ group or use the API time) when a refresh fails or the report is older than about 90 min; add a visible status/last-updated chip in the header; add AbortController timeouts; treat 404 (no report) differently from network errors.

findings.note: dead evaluator also misses M1/4SM, VCTS, CB/TCU (agent ran lines 12-64 in node); matters when revived
findings.title: Latent bug in the (dead) limit evaluator: several hazardous METAR/TAF patterns raise no alert
findings.user_impact: Once the alert code is revived (see the first finding) it would miss some conditions a SOF cares about: visibility 'M1/4SM' (less than 1/4 SM) is not parsed at all, thunderstorms in the vicinity (VCTS) and cumulonimbus/towering cumulus (CB/TCU) are never flagged, and snow (SN, +SN) is highlighted orange on the card but excluded from the alert list, so snow by itself never raises an alert (for example '2SM -SN BKN030' alerts on visibility only). Limits use strict '<', so a ceiling of exactly 2000 ft or visibility of exactly 3 SM does not alert.
findings.evidence: Ran lines 12-64 in Node: `sofVisFromText('... M1/4SM FG SKC')` -> null and sofEvalText -> only ['METAR SIGNIFICANT WX']; `'15SM VCTS FEW040CB'` -> []; `'15SM FEW040TCU BKN100'` -> []; `'00000KT M1/4SM +SN OVC010'` -> vis null (only the ceiling alert); `'3SM BKN020'` -> [] at the 2000 ft / 3 SM limits. Cause: vis regex `(?:^|\s)(?:(\d+)\s+)?(\d+\/\d+|...)SM\b` (29, 57) cannot match an 'M' or 'P' prefix; thunderstorm regex `\b(?:\+?TS(?:RA|SN|GR|GS)?|FC|SQ)\b` (41) has no word boundary inside 'VCTS'; significant-weather list (42) omits SN/BCFG/CB/TCU while wxTokenHighlights (59) includes SN.
findings.suggested_fix: Before reviving, write tests with these METARs. Parse M/P prefixes (M1/4SM = below 1/4 SM), add VCTS, CB, TCU, SN and BCFG/MIFG, and agree with the owner whether limits mean '<' or '<='. Keep the evaluator a pure function in its own module.

findings.title: Latent bug in the (dead) alert popup: an alert text can only ever fire once per page load, and a new alert overwrites an unacknowledged one
findings.user_impact: For a dashboard that stays open all day: after 'CYMJ — METAR CEILING 1500 FT < 2000 FT' has fired once, the weather can improve and worsen again at 1500 ft and no caution appears the second time. If two different alerts arrive before the first is acknowledged, the popup text is replaced and the first is lost (and marked as seen so it never returns).
findings.evidence: `window.__sofSeenAlerts` is a Set that is never cleared (65); `alerts.forEach(a=>{const k=id+"|"+a;if(!window.__sofSeenAlerts.has(k)){fresh.push(...);window.__sofSeenAlerts.add(k)}})` (78); the popup does `sofLimitCautionText.textContent=fresh.join("\n")` (80), replacing rather than appending. The acknowledge handler `sofLimitAck.onclick=...` (894) runs before the button exists at line 959 and throws 'sofLimitAck is not defined' (confirmed in the headless console), which is the already-known issue.
findings.suggested_fix: Track active alerts per airfield and clear a key when the condition clears; append new alerts to the open popup; attach the ack handler after the element exists (put the markup first or use addEventListener in an init function); add a persistent 'active alerts' list instead of relying on a one-shot popup.

findings.note: render-blocking unpkg Leaflet with no SRI; only consumer crashes
findings.title: Leaflet is loaded from unpkg as a render-blocking script and stylesheet in <head>, without SRI, although nothing on screen uses it
findings.user_impact: If unpkg.com is slow or blocked on the base network (content filters, captive portal, offline), the whole SOF page can sit blank until the browser gives up on both requests, for a map that is not even displayed. The script also runs with the same origin as the main app (the SOF is loaded via srcdoc), so an unpinned third-party file has access to the app's localStorage and DOM.
findings.evidence: `<link rel=stylesheet href="https://unpkg.com/leaflet@1.9.4/dist/leaflet.css">` and `<script src="https://unpkg.com/leaflet@1.9.4/dist/leaflet.js">` (3-4): no async/defer, no integrity/crossorigin attributes. The only consumer is the legacy script that aborts at line 565.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove both tags together with the legacy map code. If Leaflet is ever needed again, vendor it locally or add `integrity`+`crossorigin` and `defer`.

findings.title: Two scripts both rebuild the NATO colour-state markers; the older one overwrites the newer one and drops the hover runway/crosswind card
findings.user_impact: After each weather refresh the NATO markers switch to the old plotting rules with no hover tooltip (favoured runway / headwind / crosswind) for up to a minute, then switch back at a later timer tick; markers can jump between two different positions for the same METAR. This is the kind of later-patch-breaks-earlier-patch interference the owner describes.
findings.evidence: sofWeatherReorgLogic.refresh() (990-998) and sofNatoCorrections.update() (1040-1049) both do `document.getElementById("natoMarkers").innerHTML=""` and re-create markers with different x/y mappings (`xp/yp` vs `x/y`). The older script also has `new MutationObserver(()=>setTimeout(refresh,0))` on wxLeft/wxRight (1007) that fires whenever mergePriority() (1050-1057) moves a card, so it runs after the newer update(). Headless: at t=3 s and 0.9 s after ⟳ WX markers were `CYMJ@46.3847%,31% NOTIP`; (a separate 65 s run, and the old form was still present about 36 s after ⟳ WX) at t=65 s they were `CYMJ@45%,22%` with `.natoTip` present. (Cross-check with the scan of lines 700+.)
findings.suggested_fix: Keep only sofNatoCorrections' renderer, delete sofWeatherReorgLogic's marker code (keep select()), and call one render function directly after each weather refresh.

findings.title: Live traffic is only visible half the time and a click-through selection is interrupted every 10 seconds
findings.user_impact: On the main screen the aircraft view is covered by Windy every other 10 s window and pointer events are switched, so a user cannot keep an aircraft selected or read its details for more than 10 s. There is no pause/lock control. The Setup text claims the embed preserves 'aircraft selections, filters, labels', and the on-screen source badge that names the current source is off-screen (see layout finding).
findings.evidence: `show()` toggles opacity and pointer-events of #mainGlobe and #windyRadar and resets `left=10`; `setInterval(()=>{left--;if(left<=0){radarOn=!radarOn;show()}...},1000)` (968-976). No button exists to hold one source.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a pause/lock toggle on the cycle pill, or show traffic and radar side by side.

findings.title: Large amount of dead or duplicated markup, CSS and clock code left in the page
findings.user_impact: No direct user effect but every later patch has to fight the earlier layers with !important, which is the cause of most of the overlap problems above.
findings.evidence: waveBar (524-530: waveDate/waveTO/waveLD) has no logic and is hidden by `#waveBar{display:none!important}` (460), doubly hidden by waveRowCorrectPlacementLogic; legacy CSS for .mapwrap/.side/.apt/.aircraft/.acTag/.leaflet-* (120-128) belongs to the removed map. #metarCloudFrame zoom/width/left is set three times (308-335: .72, .66, .60), #sofDecisionRight positioned four different ways (195-196, 213-225, 287-291, 297-301), #natoGrid backgrounds three ways (201-202, 259-267, 272-281). Three independent clock tickers for the same elements: updateClocks (750-757, dead), clockSafety (767-785) and tickMooseJaw (856-868) both writing cMoose every second, plus the hidden legacy control div on line 766 with 10+ inputs/buttons that have no handlers (listener check).
findings.suggested_fix: During the refactor keep one stylesheet with a single rule per selector, one clock module, and delete the hidden wave bar, legacy map CSS and hidden controls.

findings.note: scan-time-zulu#5 (verified: lines 5-113 are the body of <script src=leaflet>)
findings.title: Weather-limit evaluation, METAR/TAF highlighting and the NEW WEATHER LIMIT caution never run (code sits inside a <script src> tag)
findings.user_impact: No METAR/TAF token is ever coloured for low ceiling/visibility/TS, no per-card 'Configured weather limits clear' box appears, no card gets the orange sofLimitAlert outline and the 'NEW WEATHER LIMIT' popup can never open. The WX SETUP dialog and the 'WX HIGHLIGHTS V3' stamp imply limit alerts are active, so a SOF could believe silence means all-clear.
findings.evidence: Line 4 is `<script src="https://unpkg.com/leaflet@1.9.4/dist/leaflet.js">` and the next 109 lines (sofEvalText, wxTokenHighlights, applyWxHighlights, updateWave, localWindow ...) are its body, closed by </script> at line 114. Browsers ignore the inline body of a script that has src. Confirmed by loading the decoded __SOF_DOC__ in jsdom with incremental parsing: typeof applyWxHighlights, sofEvalText, updateWave are all 'undefined'. standaloneWeatherFeed guards the call (line 830 `typeof window.applyWxHighlights==="function"`) so it fails silently. Nothing else in the file sets .sofEval, .sofLimitAlert or opens #sofLimitCaution.
findings.suggested_fix: Close the Leaflet tag at line 4 (`<script src=...></script>`) and move lines 5-113 into their own script placed AFTER the markup (so sofLimitCaution/waveDate exist). Then re-verify: highlighting, popup, and remove the duplicated wave-time logic in 98-113 (see the wave findings). Add a smoke test that asserts window.applyWxHighlights is a function.

findings.note: 565 L.map('map') runs in script 562-766; the only id=map div is in the hidden stub after </script> at 766, so the script throws and lines 566-765 never run
findings.title: Main SOF script (lines 562-766) dies at L.map("map") even when Leaflet loads, because <div id=map> is declared AFTER the script
findings.user_impact: The whole legacy block (map, radar, traffic-marker drawing, clocks via updateClocks, /api/traffic polling, tab and toggle handlers) never executes. The dashboard only works because later patch scripts re-implement the pieces (standaloneWeatherFeed, clockSafety, sofUiRepair). Every function declared in it is dead weight and several visible controls are dead (see the Zulu DTG, TRAFFIC button and OTHER AIRFIELDS findings). This extends the known 'L is not defined' problem: it fails even when unpkg works.
findings.evidence: Line 565 `const $=s=>document.querySelector(s), map=L.map("map",{preferCanvas:true})...` runs while parsing; the only element with id=map is in the hidden stub at line 766 (`</script><div ...><div id="map" ...>`), which is parsed after the script. Leaflet throws 'Map container not found.' Reproduced in jsdom with incremental parsing and real Leaflet 1.9.4: window error 'Map container not found.', `fetch` is only ever called for datamask.org (never /api/traffic), zuluDTG stays '------Z --- --'. Only function declarations survive (hoisting).
findings.suggested_fix: Decide whether the Leaflet map is wanted. If not, delete lines 562-765 plus the hidden stub at 766 and the 'legacy' sections (globe/raw/setup panels 549-560). If it is, put the stub elements before the script and guard `typeof L`.

findings.note: 982-987 visM needs whitespace before digits; cloud regex needs \b after 3 digits so BKN030CB is skipped
findings.title: NATO colour-state grid drops or misplaces aerodromes: 'M1/4SM' visibility and CB/TCU-suffixed cloud layers are not parsed
findings.user_impact: An airfield reporting visibility below 1/4 SM (Canadian METAR 'M1/4SM', e.g. fog) gets NO marker on the NATO grid at all, i.e. it vanishes exactly in the worst case instead of showing RED. A lowest layer written 'BKN030CB' or 'SCT025TCU' is ignored, so the ceiling is taken from the next layer up (or 'unlimited'), placing the marker in a better colour state than reality during thunderstorm conditions.
findings.evidence: visM: `raw.match(/(?:^|\s)(?:(\d+)\s+)?(\d+\/\d+|\d+(?:\.\d+)?)SM\b/)` needs whitespace before the digits, so 'M1/4SM' and 'P6SM' do not match; the 4-digit fallback also fails and `if(v==null)return` (994/1044) skips the airfield. cloud: `/\b(?:SCT|BKN|OVC|VV)(\d{3})\b/g` requires a word boundary after the 3 digits, so 'BKN030CB' does not match. Verified in node/jsdom: for 'METAR CYMJ ... M1/4SM FG VV001' no CYMJ marker is created; 'SCT025TCU BKN040' yields only BKN040.
findings.suggested_fix: Write ONE METAR parser (module + unit tests) handling M/P prefixes, mixed fractions, CB/TCU suffixes, CAVOK, NSC/SKC and use it in NATO grid, wave assessment and cards. Add tests for M1/4SM, P6SM, 1 1/2SM, BKN030CB, VV001.

findings.title: Two scripts rebuild #natoMarkers and a MutationObserver re-fires the rebuild every ~1.3 s once wave times are set; the rich hover card is effectively never available
findings.user_impact: NATO markers flicker/are torn down and recreated about 47 times a minute in normal use. The marker set alternates between two different builders (continuous xp/yp positions with a plain title tooltip vs. discrete band positions with the wind / favored-runway hover card), so markers can jump and the wind/runway hover card shows for at most a moment. Any marker under the pointer is destroyed while hovered.
findings.evidence: Both scripts do `#natoMarkers.innerHTML=""` then rebuild (991 vs 1041), each on a 30 s interval (1008, 1059) plus Reorg also on `new MutationObserver(()=>setTimeout(refresh,0))` watching #wxLeft/#wxRight subtree (1007). The wave assessment scripts rewrite `.ifpAssess` / `.altWaveAssessV4` inside the cards every 1.5 s and 1.8 s (lines 1516, 1585) whenever wave date/takeoff/land are set, which fires that observer. jsdom simulation with wave times stored: 47 #natoMarkers rebuilds in 60 s and 0 of 120 sampled seconds showed the hover-card markers (all 'title only' Reorg markers). Without wave times the state flips between builders at each 30 s tick and after every 5-min weather refresh.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep exactly one NATO renderer (the sofNatoCorrections version) and delete sofWeatherReorgLogic's refresh(). Drive it from a single weather data model event (fired by the feed) instead of scraping .wxCard DOM text and observing DOM mutations.

findings.title: Wave 1-5 selector is unreachable: waveOpsSelect vs waveOpsWave id mismatch, and the whole wave row is hidden by CSS
findings.user_impact: Only one wave can ever be edited: the WAVE 1-5 selector, its stored per-wave alternate flag and the 'ALTERNATE REQUIRED / NO ALTERNATE REQUIRED' toggle live in #waveOpsRow which is display:none, and the 24-hour timeline that 'owns the wave controls' clones only date/takeoff/land. Whatever wave is stored in dadSofActiveWave (default 1) is the only one used, and there is no UI to change it.
findings.evidence: waveRowCorrectPlacementLogic creates `<select id="waveOpsSelect">`. sofTopWaveCleanupCss hides `#waveOpsBar,#waveOpsRow,#waveBar,...{display:none!important}` and `#waveOpsWave,#waveOpsDate,#waveOpsTakeoff,#waveOpsLand{display:none!important}` (460-470). The live timeline clones `['waveOpsWave','waveOpsDate','waveOpsTakeoff','waveOpsLand']` (line 2036) and skips missing ids (`if(!s)return`), but the id 'waveOpsWave' does not exist anywhere. jsdom: #swtControls contains swt_waveOpsDate, swt_waveOpsTakeoff, swt_waveOpsLand, swtTimeToggle only.
findings.suggested_fix: Pick one id (waveOpsSelect) everywhere and clone it into the timeline controls, or drop the 5-wave model. Remove the hidden row and put wave state in one small module with a single store.

findings.note: 894 before 959 (known); popup also cannot open because its opener is dead code
findings.title: SOF 'ACKNOWLEDGE / CLEAR' handler is attached before the button exists (confirmed; and the popup it would clear can never open)
findings.user_impact: Clicking ACKNOWLEDGE / CLEAR does nothing, so a caution that did open could not be dismissed. Today the caution does not open at all because of the applyWxHighlights problem, but fixing that alone would expose a permanent, un-dismissable orange box in the bottom-right corner (z-index 400000).
findings.evidence: Line 894 `sofLimitAck.onclick=()=>sofLimitCaution.classList.remove("open");` sits at the end of script#ecccLightningLive; the button is created at line 959, later in the document. jsdom with incremental parsing: window error 'sofLimitAck is not defined'. Also line 65/78: window.__sofSeenAlerts is never cleared, so a limit that clears and later returns with identical text will not re-alert all day.
findings.suggested_fix: Attach the handler after line 959 (or use document.getElementById inside DOMContentLoaded / event delegation). When reviving alerts, expire entries in __sofSeenAlerts when the condition clears and append (not overwrite) fresh alerts in the popup text.

findings.note: zuluDTG only written by dead updateClocks; clockSafety writes missing #dtg
findings.title: Top-bar Zulu DTG never fills in ('------Z --- --')
findings.user_impact: The date-time group next to the dashboard title is permanently the placeholder. The Zulu clock tile works, but the DTG a SOF would read out or log is not available.
findings.evidence: `------Z --- --` (511) is only written by updateClocks() line 755 (`zuluDTG.textContent=dtgZulu()`), which never runs (script dies at 565, see the main-script finding). The replacement clockSafety script updates `document.getElementById("dtg")` (781), an id that does not exist, and would use a 4-digit year (`now.getUTCFullYear()`), unlike dtgZulu()'s 2-digit year.
findings.suggested_fix: Target #zuluDTG, keep one clock module, and use one DTG format (DDHHMMZ MON YY).

findings.note: trafficbtn handler after the 565 crash; /api/traffic needs a server
findings.title: '⟳ TRAFFIC' button and the lone 'LIVE TRAFFIC' tab have no handler
findings.user_impact: Pressing ⟳ TRAFFIC or the LIVE TRAFFIC tab does nothing. (Traffic is now an Airplanes.live iframe, so the button has nothing left to refresh, but it still looks live.)
findings.evidence: `trafficbtn.onclick=loadTraffic` (730) and the `[data-tab]` onclick loop (742) are after the crash at line 565 and never execute; jsdom: trafficbtn.onclick === null, tab button onclick === null. loadTraffic itself would call fetch("/api/traffic") which only exists on the old Netlify setup (line 558 text) and is not present in a static deployment.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove both buttons (or, if a manual reload is wanted, reload the #mainGlobe iframe). Delete loadTraffic/drawTraffic/acIcon/silhouette (692-729).

findings.title: 'SHOW OTHER AIRFIELDS' buttons (two) toggle a list that is always empty
findings.user_impact: Pressing SHOW OTHER AIRFIELDS only flips the button text to HIDE OTHER AIRFIELDS; no extra airfields ever appear. The right-rail copy of the button has no handler at all (and is hidden by the dock script).
findings.evidence: standaloneWeatherFeed hard-codes `const leftOther=[], rightOther=[];` (791) and never fills them, so no `.wxCard.secondary` element is ever created. The original handler (759) never runs (after the crash). sofUiRepair binds only the first button: `document.querySelector(".otherWxBtn")` (846). jsdom: onclick handlers = [function, null]; secondary cards = 0.
findings.suggested_fix: Either restore the 'other airfields' list (the AP array at 563 has 15 stations) or delete both buttons, the .showOthers CSS (147, 161-162) and both wiring scripts.

findings.note: WX SETUP limits only read by dead code; 1493 hard-codes 2000/3
findings.title: WX SETUP dialog: 6 of 8 fields are saved but read by nothing; the 'Lightning alert radius' input is hidden by a blanket CSS rule
findings.user_impact: Changing ceiling/visibility limits (home and alternate), 'lightning alert radius' or 'New-alert caution box' has no effect on anything. The lightning radius box is not even visible (only its label shows). Only Home airfield and Alternates work.
findings.evidence: cfgSave stores homeCeil, homeVis, altCeil, altVis, lightningNm, popup (946). They are read only in the dead block (37, 54, 80) and in `type="text/plain"` scripts (1347, 1379). The live wave assessment hard-codes `tafHazards(taf,w,2000,3)` (line 1487). `#cfgLightning` matches the rule `[id*="lightning" i]:not(#lightningFrame):not(#lightningNative){display:none!important}` (243).
findings.suggested_fix: Wire limits into one evaluator (and the wave assessment) or remove the fields. Narrow the blanket attribute-substring CSS at 235-244.

findings.title: NATO markers are drawn about half a marker-width right and half-height below their computed spot, so they can sit on a colour-band boundary
findings.user_impact: Marker position on the colour-state grid is offset by roughly 15-20 px right and 9 px down, i.e. up to about half a band (bands are 12-14% of width). A marker meant to sit mid-band lands on or across the edge to the next colour, which is misleading for a colour-state display. Where several airfields overlap the spread is applied twice.
findings.evidence: `.natoMarker{transform:translate(-50%,-50%)}` centres the marker. deconflict() ALWAYS sets `m.style.transform=`${base} translateX(${dx}px)`` (1162) even when dx is 0, which overrides the stylesheet centring. The guard `if(!m.dataset.natoBaseTransform)m.dataset.natoBaseTransform=m.style.transform||''` (1159) stores an empty string, which is falsy, so the base is re-read on the second call and the first translateX becomes part of the 'base' (jsdom showed `translateX(-34px) translateX(-34px)`). Runs on every DOM mutation.
findings.suggested_fix: Do not touch the transform: use CSS custom properties or `translate` (individual property) for the deconflict offset, store the base with hasAttribute, and only run deconflict after markers are rebuilt.

findings.note: hover card loses styling when moved to body
findings.title: NATO hover card is moved into <body>, losing all its styling; can be left stuck on screen
findings.user_impact: When the hover card does appear it is unstyled (no background, width, border, padding) so text floats over the map/rails, and depending on which of the two handlers wins it can be placed at the left screen edge. If the markers are rebuilt while the pointer is over one (every 30 s, or ~1 s when wave times are set) the card stays on screen as a stale copy of old wind/runway data until another marker is hovered.
findings.evidence: All card styling is `.natoMarker .natoTip{display:none;position:absolute;...width:270px;background:#06111bf7;border...}` (251-253) which stops matching once show() does `document.body.appendChild(tip)` (1104/1186). natoHoverPortalFix computes left from tip.offsetWidth BEFORE it is fixed-positioned (1108), when it is a static block as wide as the page, giving left of about -8px. Both scripts bind the same markers and both move the same tip; hide() only runs on mouseleave, which never fires for a removed marker. jsdom: after mouseenter then a rebuild, one .natoTip remained in body with position:fixed and z-index 2147483647.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the tip inside the marker (position:fixed relative to a transform-free ancestor or use a single shared tooltip element that is styled by an id/class not scoped to .natoMarker), remove one of the two hover scripts, and hide the shared tooltip whenever markers are rebuilt.

findings.title: Right-rail weather card disappears for up to 30 s after every weather refresh
findings.user_impact: With the default alternates the odd-numbered alternate (CYYN) is rendered into #wxRight, which the dock script hides. It is only moved to the visible left rail by the 30 s mergePriority timer, so every 5-minute refresh blanks that airfield's METAR/TAF card for up to 30 s (and any ifpAssess / alt badges on it).
findings.evidence: standaloneWeatherFeed splits `rightPrimary=__alts.filter((_,i)=>i%2===1)` and writes `R.innerHTML=` (828) on each refresh. dock() sets `old.forEach(el=>{ if(el!==rail) el.style.display="none"; })` on the right rail's children, including #wxRight (1085). sofNatoCorrections.mergePriority (1050-1057) moves cards back to #wxLeft only on `setInterval(...,30000)` (1059). jsdom simulation across the 300 s refresh: left[CYMJ+CYQR+CYXE] right[CYYN] from t=300 s until the next tick at 330 s.
findings.suggested_fix: Render every airfield straight into one container (left rail), delete leftPrimary/rightPrimary splitting and mergePriority.

findings.note: #wxstatus missing; failures become NO METAR AVAILABLE with no age (R13)
findings.title: No visible weather status or freshness indicator; failures silently replace last-good METAR with 'NO METAR AVAILABLE'
findings.user_impact: The desk screen can show METAR/TAF of unknown age with no 'LOADING / LIVE / ERROR' indicator and no 'last updated' time. A single failed request flips a card to 'NO METAR AVAILABLE' until the next 5-minute poll, and a hung request (no timeout) freezes the display with no warning.
findings.evidence: The status element `#wxstatus` does not exist in the markup (the brief's missing-id list is right for wxstatus and dtg), so `const status=document.getElementById("wxstatus"); if(status){...}` (820-835) never shows anything. get() has no AbortController/timeout; station() uses allSettled and maps any failure to null (803). The old loadWx (609) references wxstatus/all/leftPrimary directly and would throw ReferenceError at line 610.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a visible status pill with last-success time and an amber/red state after N minutes without a good response; keep the previous card contents on transient errors and add fetch timeouts.

findings.title: Wave date is not defaulted or rolled: stored date persists across days; timeline and IFP assessment disagree
findings.user_impact: A dashboard left open overnight keeps yesterday's wave date until someone edits it. The home card then reports 'TAF DOES NOT COVER WAVE' / 'SET WAVE TIMES' while the timeline (which falls back to today) shows a normal day. The original bar defaulted to today's Regina date (lines 105-112); the replacement row defaults to empty.
findings.evidence: `date.value=localStorage.getItem(keys()+'date')||''` (1283) with no default or expiry. The IFP wave() returns null when the date is empty (1438), whereas the timeline selectedDate() falls back to today in CST (2000).
findings.suggested_fix: Default the date to today (America/Regina) when empty or when the stored date is in the past, or store wave times as day-relative.

findings.note: 12 intervals never cleared; live iframes keep streaming (R4)
findings.title: SOF keeps polling, animating and streaming after the user leaves the module (three live map iframes + 12 intervals)
findings.user_impact: All day the SOF iframe is never unloaded: '← MODULES' only sets display:none on the wrapper (main.html 4311). While the user works in the formation sim / debrief tools the SOF still fetches weather every 5 min, an ECCC lightning image every 2 min, rebuilds the NATO grid, and keeps Airplanes.live and Windy running. A third full Airplanes.live globe (#globeFrame) is loaded in a display:none panel that no tab can show.
findings.evidence: 12 setIntervals are registered at load (1 s x3, 1.5 s, 1.8 s, 5 s x2, 15 s, 30 s x2, 120 s, 300 s) and none are ever cleared. jsdom simulation over 2 simulated hours: timer count constant at 12, DOM node count constant at 431, so no stacking/leak, but nothing is paused. `<iframe id=globeFrame ... src="https://globe.airplanes.live/...">` (551) is inside `<section id=globe class=panel>` (display:none) and the tab bar only has data-tab=main (520).
findings.suggested_fix: On '← MODULES' remove/blank the SOF iframe (or postMessage pause); delete #globeFrame, #raw, #setup panels; keep one Airplanes.live iframe and lazy-load the Windy one.

findings.note: METAR/TAF parsing copied ~8 times with different bugs
findings.title: METAR/ceiling/visibility parsing is copy-pasted ~8 times with different bugs
findings.user_impact: Different widgets disagree about the same METAR/TAF: the NATO grid ignores M/P prefixes and CB/TCU suffixes, the alternate-at-ETA assessment (1558) turns 'M1/4SM' into 4 SM, the home assessment (1421) handles P/M but not SCT, and the dead code uses yet another rule. Any fix has to be repeated in every copy.
findings.evidence: Same regex families in sofVisFromText/sofCeilFromText (28-35, dead), visM/cloud (982-987), vis/ceil (1022-1026, byte-identical logic), metarVals (1313, text/plain), P()/T() (1379, text/plain), vals() (1419, no SCT), v() (1558). Verified in node: V4's chain on 'TEMPO 2918/2920 M1/4SM FG VV001' returns vis=4 because `\b(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)SM\b` matches '4SM' after the '/'.
findings.suggested_fix: One tested parser module (see NATO finding); every widget consumes its output.

findings.title: Three timers write the same clocks; live DTG code targets a missing id
findings.user_impact: Cosmetic: clocks are updated three times a second-equivalent by unrelated scripts (updateClocks is dead; clockSafety and sofUiRepair.tickMooseJaw both write cMoose every second). No visible bug except the Zulu DTG.
findings.evidence: updateClocks (750-756, never runs), clockSafety tick (767-785, also lists ['cGMT','zGMT','UTC'] and America/Edmonton vs America/Denver), tickMooseJaw (856-862) all target cMoose/cGMT. `zGMT` and `dtg` ids do not exist.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep one clock function (clockSafety's zones + the DTG target fixed) and delete the other two.

findings.title: Two document-wide MutationObservers plus forced layout run every second all day
findings.user_impact: Continuous small CPU/layout cost on the desk screen (does not grow over time). Any DOM change, including the once-per-second clock text updates, triggers bind()/deconflict().
findings.evidence: `new MutationObserver(bind).observe(document.documentElement,{childList:true,subtree:true})` (1139) and the rAF variant (1210). deconflict() calls getBoundingClientRect for every marker each time (about 9 forced-layout calls per second in the jsdom simulation). No observers or intervals accumulate: counts stayed constant over 2 simulated hours.
findings.suggested_fix: Observe only #natoMarkers (or call the renderer directly after it rebuilds); drop the document-level observers.

findings.note: 242-243 CSS hides eccc/lightning while refresh interval runs
findings.title: ECCC lightning panel refreshes an image every 2 min into a panel that CSS hides; lightning UI is removed but its JS and settings remain
findings.user_impact: No lightning data is visible anywhere on the dashboard (right card literally says 'Lightning overlay removed'), yet a 900x500 WMS image is still requested every 120 s and the Blitzortung websocket (line 1658) stays connected. The panel's ON/OFF button and opacity slider are unreachable.
findings.evidence: `[id*="eccc" i],[class*="eccc" i],[id*="lightning" i]:not(#lightningFrame):not(#lightningNative){display:none!important}` (242-243) hides #ecccLightningPanel; the script still runs `refresh();setInterval(refresh,120000)` (892). #lightningNative shows only the .lnEmpty placeholder (507) and the native canvas host #lightningUnderNato is display:none!important (429).
findings.suggested_fix: Either bring a lightning display back (and honour the 'alert radius' setting) or delete the ECCC panel, its script, the Blitzortung script and the setup field.

findings.title: waveBannerModule builds a hidden 5-wave banner whose stored values nothing reads
findings.user_impact: No visible effect; wasted DOM, a second per-wave storage scheme (dadSofWave_0..9) that disagrees with the active one (dadSofWave1_date/to/land).
findings.evidence: `#waveBanner{display:none!important}` (360) immediately after the module adds it (1219-1231); keys `dadSofWave_+j` (1234) are read only here.
findings.suggested_fix: Delete the module and its CSS (344-360); also delete the old #waveBar markup (524-529) whose handlers are dead.

findings.title: Inert 'text/plain' script blocks and no-op code left in the page
findings.user_impact: No visible effect; ~3.5 KB of JS that looks live to a reader, plus a no-op resize listener and unused variables.
findings.evidence: `<script type="text/plain" id="ifpFlowWaveAssessment_old">` (1307-1378) and `ifpWeatherParserFixV2_old` (1379, one 3.3 KB line) never execute; `window.addEventListener("resize",()=>{})` (1088); `const $=id=>...` unused in sofWxSetupScript (943); `rows` array in tip() is built but unused (1034-1035). The file has 35 script blocks and 37 style blocks; most *_old blocks are inert.
findings.suggested_fix: Delete all *_old blocks; git history is the archive.

findings.title: Traffic/radar rotation cannot be paused, so neither map can be inspected for more than 10 s
findings.user_impact: While reading an aircraft label or panning the radar the view flips to the other source every 10 s (1.2 s crossfade); there is no pause/lock control, and the hidden iframe gets pointer-events:none.
findings.evidence: `setInterval(()=>{left--;if(left<=0){radarOn=!radarOn;show()}...},1000)` with no hover/click/focus pause.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a pause toggle or pause the timer on pointerenter/interaction with either iframe.

findings.note: API category and config ICAO into innerHTML unescaped
findings.title: Third-party and user-config strings are put into innerHTML unescaped in a same-origin iframe
findings.user_impact: If datamask.org (a third-party API) or the stored config returned markup, it would execute in the SOF document; the srcdoc iframe inherits the parent's origin and has no sandbox, so it could read the whole app's localStorage.
findings.evidence: card(): `${cat}` and `data-icao="${r.id}"` (813-814) where cat is `m?.decoded?.flightCategory` from the API and r.id comes from the cfgAlts text field; raw METAR text is correctly escaped via esc() (815-816). apRow `${id}` (1389).
findings.suggested_fix: Escape or textContent all interpolated values; validate ICAO ids with /^[A-Z0-9]{4}$/ when saving; add sandbox="allow-scripts allow-same-origin" only if needed (or drop allow-same-origin).

findings.title: localStorage is used without try/catch in wave and setup code
findings.user_impact: With storage blocked (private window, strict tracking protection) WX SETUP 'SAVE + APPLY' throws and does nothing, and the wave row initialisation aborts half-way. (The config bootstrap at 179-182 is correctly guarded.)
findings.evidence: `localStorage.setItem("dadSofWxConfig",JSON.stringify(n));location.reload()` (946), `el.value=localStorage.getItem(key)||''` (1235) and load() (1283-1286) are unguarded.
findings.suggested_fix: Wrap storage in a tiny safe helper (get/set with try/catch) shared by all SOF code.

findings.title: Alternate-planning rows in WX SETUP are built by two different scripts with different parsing of the alternates list
findings.user_impact: Editing the alternates field re-renders rows with a different layout and without the immediate-save behaviour of the other renderer. Alternates separated by spaces or semicolons are accepted by the feed (789 splits on /[\s,;]+/) but the planning rows split on commas only, so 'CYQR CYYN' yields one bogus row 'CYQR CYYN'.
findings.evidence: cfgAltPlanningScript render()/save() (1384-1403) vs renderSetup() (1495) both write #cfgAltPlanningRows and both hook #sofWxSetupBtn (1406 vs 1514); ids() uses `.split(",")` (1383).
findings.suggested_fix: One renderer, one shared parseIcaoList() used by the feed, setup and planning.

findings.note: 766 BUILD stamp fixed bottom-right (third debug badge)
findings.title: Debug build stamp is permanently drawn over the bottom-right corner
findings.user_impact: Stale text ('DATE-AWARE / PROB30 FIX / SMART LAUNCHER') sits over the corner at z-index 99999 on top of the weather/decision rails; unrelated to SOF and can overlap the parent page's own stamp.
findings.evidence:
`
BUILD: DATE-AWARE / PROB30 FIX / SMART LAUNCHER
`.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove; show a version string only in an About dialog.

findings.title: Docking of the decision rail is a single layout-dependent attempt with no retry
findings.user_impact: If the layout is not ready or the rail is narrower than the thresholds at 900 ms the rail stays absolutely positioned over the right weather column and never docks; a later resize does not fix it (the resize listener at 1088 is empty).
findings.evidence: `setTimeout(dock,900)` picks a host by `r.width>180 && r.height>250 && r.left>best` from getBoundingClientRect of ancestors of the 'PRIORITY WEATHER' text; on failure it just returns. It also hides every existing child of the host (1085).
findings.suggested_fix: Place #sofDecisionRight in the right rail in the markup instead of moving it with JS.

findings.note: ran vals() from sof.html 1420-1429 in node: 'TEMPO 2916/2920 1/2SM FG' gives v=2920.5 (hazard missed). Same regex in V8 visibility() 2008
findings.module: SOF Dashboard - wave/weather timeline & IFP wave assessment
findings.lines: 1423 (vals), 1466, 2008 (visibility), 2010 (parts), 2011; same pattern in head code at 29-31 and 57
findings.title: Fractional visibility in TEMPO/BECMG/PROB groups is read as ~2920 SM (hour group taken as whole-number part)
findings.user_impact: Any change group whose visibility is a bare fraction (e.g. 'TEMPO 2916/2920 1/2SM FG', 'BECMG 2915/2917 3/4SM BR') is parsed as whole part 2920 + 1/2 = 2920.5 SM. The home-airfield alternate check therefore says 'NO HOME-WX ALT TRIGGER / IFP HOME WX GOOD' for forecast fog below 3 SM, and the timeline paints the segment BLU with a label such as 'TEMPO 2914 1/2SM'. The most hazardous visibilities (<1 SM) are the ones lost.
findings.evidence: Regex '\b(\d+)\s+(\d+)\/(\d+)SM\b' matches '2920 1/2SM' inside 'TEMPO 2916/2920 1/2SM FG'. Tested in node: tafHazards() for TEMPO 2916/2920 1/2SM FG -> hits:[] (control with '1SM' -> hit); vals('TEMPO 2916/2920 1/2SM FG') -> {v:2920.5}; V8 visibility() -> 2920.5, nato() -> BLU. Reproduced in headless Chromium: lane label 'TEMPO 2914 1/2SM OVC004'.
findings.suggested_fix: Parse visibility only from the tokens after the period header (strip 'DDHH/DDHH' first) or require the mixed-number whole part to be 1-2 digits (\b\d{1,2}\s+\d+/\d+SM) and not preceded by '/'. Add a test pinning: TEMPO 2916/2920 1/2SM FG -> 0.5 SM, and apply the same fix in the head copies (lines 29-31, 57).

findings.note: 1459-1466 BECMG group ends at its transition time; persisting conditions not carried forward
findings.module: SOF Dashboard - wave/weather timeline & IFP wave assessment
findings.title: BECMG changes stop counting once the BECMG period ends: alternate check says 'good' while the timeline shows IFR
findings.user_impact: tafHazards() treats BECMG like TEMPO: its weather only counts while the BECMG window overlaps the wave. After the transition completes, the new (worse) conditions persist in a real TAF but the code falls back to the INITIAL group. Result: home card badge 'IFP HOME WX GOOD FOR WAVE' (green) and status 'NO HOME-WX ALT TRIGGER' for a wave that is fully inside forecast 1 SM / OVC003, while the timeline (V8, which does persist BECMG) shows the yellow/IFR segment for the same time. Two parsers give opposite answers.
findings.evidence: Test: 'TAF CYMJ 291120Z 2912/3012 27010KT P6SM SKC BECMG 2913/2915 VRB03KT 1SM BR OVC003 FM300600 ...', wave 17Z-19Z -> hits:[]. In headless Chromium the CYMJ card showed 'ifpAssess good: IFP HOME WX GOOD FOR WAVE' while the CYMJ lane showed 'VRB/03KT 1SM OVC003' from 16Z onward.
findings.suggested_fix: Use one TAF parser for both timeline and alternate check. Model BECMG as: old conditions until BECMG start/end, new prevailing conditions from BECMG end until the next FM (as V8's tafGroups already does), and evaluate limits over that prevailing timeline plus TEMPO/PROB overlays.

findings.note: ran vals(): 'P6SM BKN015CB' gives no ceiling (c=99999); regexes need \d{3}(CB|TCU)?
findings.module: SOF Dashboard - wave/weather timeline & IFP wave assessment
findings.title: Cloud regex ignores CB/TCU layers, so ceilings are missed and stale ceilings are inherited
findings.user_impact: 'BKN015CB', 'OVC008CB', 'SCT025TCU' do not match '(?:BKN|OVC|VV)(\d{3})\b' (no word boundary before 'CB'). A convective ceiling below the 2000 ft home limit is not seen by the alternate check, NATO colour is too good, and the label omits the layer. Because the sky field is then empty, inherit() carries the PREVIOUS group's ceiling forward, so the timeline shows the wrong ceiling (e.g. FM group says BKN015CB but the bar reads OVC004).
findings.evidence: node: vals('27010KT P6SM BKN015CB') -> c:99999 (BKN015 -> 1500). Chromium: TAF '... FM291500 27010KT P6SM BKN015CB' rendered 'FM' segment label '270/10KT P6SM OVC004 OVC004'. No occurrence of CB or TCU anywhere in sof.html.
findings.suggested_fix: Use /\b(?:BKN|OVC|VV)(\d{3})(?:CB|TCU)?\b/ (and /\b(?:FEW|SCT|BKN|OVC|VV)(\d{3})(?:CB|TCU)?\b/ for labels) in one shared helper; keep CB/TCU flag for display.

findings.note: V8 visibility() 2008 has no M branch; 'M1/4SM' falls to the plain SM regex and reads 4
findings.module: SOF Dashboard - wave/weather timeline & IFP wave assessment
findings.title: METAR/TAF 'M1/4SM' (less than 1/4 SM) is shown as 4 SM in the live timeline
findings.user_impact: V8 has no 'M' branch. In 'M1/4SM' the fraction regex fails on the word boundary and the whole-number regex then matches the trailing '4SM'. The METAR marker for a dense-fog observation displays '4SM' with NATO WHT instead of RED, and inherited/other groups can show 4SM for a sub-1/4 mile forecast. The alternate cards use V4's v(), which also has no M branch.
findings.evidence: Chromium with METAR 'CYMJ 291500Z 00000KT M1/4SM FG BKN002CB': lane text 'METAR 000/00KT 4SM'. node: nato(inherit('27010KT P6SM SKC','FM300600 00000KT M1/4SM FG SKC')) -> WHT.
findings.suggested_fix: Add /\bM(\d+)\/(\d+)SM\b/ (value just under the fraction) before the other patterns in every copy, ideally via one shared parseVisibility() as in V2's vals().

findings.note: 1477 badge is 'good' unless gnssOnly; altCeil/altVis only read in dead scripts
findings.module: SOF Dashboard - wave/weather timeline & IFP wave assessment
findings.lines: 1471-1478 (altInfo), 1510, 1567-1581 (V4 render); altCeil/altVis only used at 1347 and 1379 (dead scripts)
findings.title: Alternate airfield cards show GREEN 'good' badges regardless of actual weather; configured alternate minima are never applied in the wave assessment
findings.user_impact: For every non-GNSS-only alternate, altInfo() calls badge(...,'good') and V4 adds a green 'NOT GNSS-ONLY' box; neither compares the METAR/TAF to the alternate limits set in WX SETUP (altCeil 600 / altVis 2). An LIFR alternate is presented in green with the text 'APPROACH MINIMA CHECK REQUIRED'. The V2 badge also shows the CURRENT METAR (not the forecast at ETA) under an ETA-oriented alternate assessment.
findings.evidence: Chromium, METAR 'M1/4SM FG BKN002CB' for CYQR: 'ifpAssess good: NO CEILING / 0.2 SM  APPROACH MINIMA CHECK REQUIRED' and 'altWaveAssessV4 good: ALT CYQR: NOT GNSS-ONLY ... NO CEILING / 6.01 SM'. Line 1477: badge(c, ..., A.gnssOnly?'warn':'good', need).
findings.suggested_fix: Compute pass/fail against C.altCeil/C.altVis on the TAF prevailing conditions at ETA; use neutral styling when the approach-minima branch cannot be evaluated; remove one of the two duplicate alternate badges.

findings.note: timeline clones 'waveOpsWave' but the real select is waveOpsSelect (1250); row hidden by CSS 460-470
findings.module: SOF Dashboard - wave/weather timeline & IFP wave assessment
findings.title: Timeline has no WAVE selector: control list uses non-existent id 'waveOpsWave' and the real wave row is hidden, so waves 2-5 cannot be chosen
findings.user_impact: The CSS comment says the timeline 'owns Wave controls', but the timeline only clones DATE, TAKEOFF and LAND. The <select id=waveOpsSelect> (WAVE 1-5) and the click-to-toggle 'ALTERNATE REQUIRED' status live in #waveOpsRow, which is display:none!important. Users can only ever edit whichever wave is stored in dadSofActiveWave (default Wave 1); waves 2-5 and the manual alternate toggle are unreachable.
findings.evidence: Chromium: #swtControls children = DATE, TAKEOFF, LAND, LOCAL/ZULU; no <select> inside #sofWaveTimeline; #waveOpsRow computed display 'none'. Source: ['waveOpsWave','waveOpsDate','waveOpsTakeoff','waveOpsLand'].forEach(k=>{let s=document.getElementById(k);if(!s)return;...
findings.suggested_fix: Clone/move #waveOpsSelect into the timeline header (fix id to 'waveOpsSelect') and rebuild the timeline on its change; or un-hide the wave row. Remove the unused manual-toggle code if not needed.

findings.note: 1493 tafHazards(taf,w,2000,3) hard-coded; homeCeil/homeVis ignored in that script
findings.module: SOF Dashboard - wave/weather timeline & IFP wave assessment
findings.title: Wave assessment hard-codes 2000 ft / 3 SM and ignores the home limits set in WX SETUP
findings.user_impact: WX SETUP stores homeCeil/homeVis and the weather cards' limit check (lines 37/54) honours them, but the wave 'ALTERNATE REQUIRED / NO HOME-WX ALT TRIGGER' decision always uses 2000/3. Changing the limits makes the card say one thing and the wave assessment another. Also the text 'DEST TRIGGER <3000 FT / 3 SM' is static.
findings.evidence: let taf=block(hc,'TAF'),q=tafHazards(taf,w,2000,3); -- C.homeCeil / C.homeVis are never read in this script.
findings.suggested_fix: Pass +C.homeCeil||2000 and +C.homeVis||3 and build the chip text from them.

findings.note: INITIAL extended to TAF end when first group is TEMPO (1459 logic reads that way)
findings.module: SOF Dashboard - wave/weather timeline & IFP wave assessment
findings.title: INITIAL TAF group is extended to the end of the TAF whenever the first change group is not an FM, giving false 'ALTERNATE REQUIRED'
findings.user_impact: e:ms[0]&&ms[0][2]?...:tv.e only looks at the first token. A TAF like 'BKN004 TEMPO ... FM291500 SKC' (TEMPO before the FM is very common) keeps the INITIAL bad weather 'valid' through the whole TAF, so a wave after the improvement still shows ALTERNATE REQUIRED. (Conservative direction, but wrong and inconsistent with the timeline.)
findings.evidence: node: 'TAF CYMJ 291120Z 2912/3012 27010KT 1SM BR OVC004 TEMPO 2912/2914 1/2SM FG FM291500 27010KT P6SM SKC', wave 17Z-19Z -> hits:[INITIAL 400ft/1SM]; the same TAF without the TEMPO -> no hit.
findings.suggested_fix: End INITIAL at the first FM group (find first token with m[2]) rather than at the first token.

findings.module: SOF Dashboard - wave/weather timeline & IFP wave assessment
findings.title: Alternate 'weather at ETA' (V4) reads the whole TAF text when ETA is before the first FM, mixes TEMPO/BECMG text, and prints raw floats
findings.user_impact: at() starts with part=t (entire TAF) and only narrows when an FM start <= ETA, so before the first FM the ceiling is the minimum over every group in the TAF (including hours long after ETA) and visibility is chosen by regex priority, not time. Output such as 'ETA 29/1900Z: 300 FT / 6.01 SM' mixes a BECMG ceiling with the base P6SM; 1/3 SM prints as 0.3333333333333333 SM.
findings.evidence: Chromium alternate box: 'ETA 29/1900Z: 300 FT / 6.01 SM'. Code: part=t,ms=[...] ; for(...){...if(st<=e)part=t.slice(...)} ; return v(part).
findings.suggested_fix: Use the shared TAF timeline (prevailing at ETA + active TEMPO/PROB) and format visibility with a helper (P6SM -> '>6 SM', fractions rounded).

findings.note: Zulu window vs CST wave times (agent reproduced in Chromium)
findings.module: SOF Dashboard - wave/weather timeline & IFP wave assessment
findings.title: ZULU mode drops evening waves: the window is the UTC day of the local date, but the wave times are always CST
findings.user_impact: With DATE = the local wave date, ZULU mode shows 00Z-24Z of that number, i.e. 18:00 (previous day) to 18:00 CST. A 19:00-21:00 CST wave (01Z-03Z next day) gets no wave band, no landing/+1h markers, while the alternate check (which uses the local date) still evaluates it. Switching LOCAL/ZULU therefore changes which wave is visible. The default date when none is entered also uses the CST date even in ZULU mode.
findings.evidence: Chromium, wave 19:00-21:00 stored: LOCAL bands ['79.1667%/8.33333%']; after clicking ZULU bands [] while badge still 'IFP ALT TRIGGER IN WAVE WINDOW'.
findings.suggested_fix: Treat DATE as the local wave date and, in ZULU mode, start the window at the wave's local day start (06Z) or centre it on the wave, only changing the axis labels; or show 30 h when the wave crosses 00Z.

findings.note: full-day band with no wave set
findings.module: SOF Dashboard - wave/weather timeline & IFP wave assessment
findings.title: With no wave times entered the timeline draws a full-day wave band; V2 and V8 disagree about a missing date
findings.user_impact: mm('') returns 0 for both takeoff and land, land<=take then adds 1440, so a 24 h blue 'wave' band and a landing marker at 24:00 are drawn before any wave is set. If only takeoff is set the band runs to midnight. V2 shows 'SET WAVE TIMES' for the same state and requires a date, whereas V8 silently substitutes today's CST date.
findings.evidence: Chromium first load (no wave stored): .swtWaveBand left/width = '0%/100%'.
findings.suggested_fix: Return null from mm() for empty/invalid input and skip the band/markers until both times are valid.

findings.module: SOF Dashboard - wave/weather timeline & IFP wave assessment
findings.title: Timeline is torn down and rebuilt on every change of its own inputs, so the field being edited loses focus
findings.user_impact: Editing TAKEOFF/LAND/DATE in the timeline header fires change after the first valid segment; build() removes #sofWaveTimeline and recreates the inputs 80-100 ms later, so keyboard entry of a time (hours then minutes) stops after the first segment and the user must click back in. The same rebuild happens whenever any card's METAR/TAF text changes.
findings.evidence: Chromium: focused swt_waveOpsTakeoff, typed '08' -> document.activeElement was BODY and the value had been rebuilt.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the header controls persistent and only rebuild the lanes; or restore focus/selection after build.

findings.module: SOF Dashboard - wave/weather timeline & IFP wave assessment
findings.title: Lightning strike display never appears: native lightning canvas is hidden by two CSS rules while its WebSocket keeps running
findings.user_impact: nativeLightningScript opens a Blitzortung WebSocket and redraws a canvas on every strike, but its host #lightningUnderNato is display:none (attribute selector [id*=lightning] and an explicit rule). The right-hand card still says 'Lightning overlay removed', and the ECCC lightning panel is also hidden. The dashboard shows no lightning information at all, yet still consumes a socket and CPU.
findings.evidence: Chromium computed display: #lightningUnderNato 'none', #ecccLightningPanel 'none'. Rule at 429: #lightningUnderNato{display:none!important}.
findings.suggested_fix: Decide on one lightning display: either show #lightningNative fed by the strike data (remove the hiding rules) or delete nativeLightningScript and the ECCC panel/script.

findings.module: SOF Dashboard - wave/weather timeline & IFP wave assessment
findings.title: Wind labels and the METAR marker overprint the TEMPO/BECMG/PROB row of the timeline
findings.user_impact: Wind text ('270/10KT') is placed in the same vertical band as the overlay row, so it prints over the start of TEMPO/BECMG/PROB segments and makes them unreadable; the white 'M.' METAR marker also covers the first characters of the underlying TAF text ('70/10KT'). The 7 px legend text (#swtHead>span:last-child{font-size:7px!important}) is hard to read.
findings.evidence: Screenshot in headless Chromium: 'TEMPO 3SM BKN020' garbled by '↗ 270/10KT'; lane text reads '70/10KT P6SM'.
findings.suggested_fix: Give lanes 3 rows (base, wind, overlay) or move wind into the tooltip; shrink/offset the METAR marker.

findings.note: V8 regex matches TEMPO inside 'PROB30 TEMPO' (probability lost)
findings.module: SOF Dashboard - wave/weather timeline & IFP wave assessment
findings.title: 'PROB30 TEMPO' groups are parsed as plain TEMPO in the timeline (probability lost)
findings.user_impact: Token regex requires digits after PROB30/PROB40, so 'PROB30 TEMPO 2916/2920 ...' matches only 'TEMPO ...' and is drawn as a firm TEMPO (dashed) instead of hatched PROB. V2's regex (line 1458) handles it, so the two views disagree.
findings.evidence: Regex: \b(BECMG|TEMPO|PROB30|PROB40)\s+(\d{2})(\d{2})\/(\d{2})(\d{2})\b -- 'PROB30 TEMPO 2916/2920' matches at TEMPO.
findings.suggested_fix: Allow an optional 'TEMPO ' between PROB and the period, and keep the PROB flag.

findings.module: SOF Dashboard - wave/weather timeline & IFP wave assessment
findings.title: TAF/METAR days-of-month are resolved relative to the selected wave date, and stored wave dates persist across days
findings.user_impact: Raw TAFs carry only DDHH, so the code picks the month whose day is nearest the WAVE date, not nearest 'now'. A stale or far-future stored date whose day-of-month matches today's TAF (e.g. exactly one month off) displays today's forecast/METAR as if valid for that date, and 'TAF covers wave' can be true. Wave dates are saved per wave in localStorage and reloaded next day without any staleness warning.
findings.evidence: utcFor()/resolveDay() choose min |candidate - ref| across month -1..+1 with ref = wave start or window midpoint.
findings.suggested_fix: Anchor day-of-month resolution to the current time (or TAF issue time) and flag waves whose date is not today/tomorrow.

findings.module: SOF Dashboard - wave/weather timeline & IFP wave assessment
findings.title: SKC/NSC/CLR/CAVOK groups inherit the previous group's cloud, and label text is duplicated
findings.user_impact: inherit() copies the previous sky when the new group has no FEW/SCT/BKN/OVC/VV token. A group that clears the sky ('SKC', 'NSC', 'CAVOK') therefore keeps the old BKN/OVC layer, so the bar shows the wrong colour and text. inherit() also appends the raw group after the extracted fields, so every label with cloud repeats it ('OVC003 OVC003').
findings.evidence: node: label(inherit('27010KT P6SM BKN008','FM301200 27010KT P6SM SKC')) -> '270/10KT P6SM BKN008'; Chromium label 'VRB/03KT 1SM OVC003 OVC003'.
findings.suggested_fix: Treat SKC/NSC/CLR/CAVOK/NCD as an explicit 'no ceiling' sky value; build labels from parsed fields only.

findings.note: five build() copies, six text/plain disabled scripts (known)
findings.module: SOF Dashboard - wave/weather timeline & IFP wave assessment
findings.title: Five copies of the 24-hour timeline build(): only the last (V8) runs; ~450 lines of dead scripts plus their CSS remain
findings.user_impact: No user-visible effect, but every script is <script type="text/plain" id="..._old"> and never executes. Only sofTimelineAbsoluteTimeV8 (LOCAL/ZULU, absolute dates, METAR marker) runs. Their CSS (lines 428-487) is still loaded and stacks (V1 .swtSeg/.swtLane heights overridden by V2, id-based #swtWaveBand/#swtLand/#swtPlus unused, V5 compact CSS has no matching script). Confusing to maintain: fixes applied to V2-V4 do nothing.
findings.evidence: grep: type="text/plain" on ids sofWaveTimelineScript_old, sofWaveTimelineScriptV2_old, sofWaveTimelineScriptV3_old, sofWaveTimelineScriptV4_old, sofTimelineTimeToggleV6_old, sofTimelineTrueLocalV7_old; V8 comment 'V5 rebuilds periodically' shows the V4 script was really V5.
findings.suggested_fix: Delete V1-V4/V6/V7 and the *_old scripts and their CSS; keep one timeline module with a shared TAF parser used by both the timeline and the alternate check.

findings.note: three wave input sets hidden by CSS 460-470
findings.module: SOF Dashboard - wave/weather timeline & IFP wave assessment
findings.lines: 526-529 + 86-113 (#waveBar, hidden); 1215-1241 (#waveBanner, hidden, keys dadSofWave_0..9 never read); 1243-1304 (#waveOpsRow, hidden); 1491, 1499-1504 (V2 writes #waveIfpTrigger which is only created in dead script at 1356); 1495-1497 vs 1295-1298

findings.module: SOF Dashboard - wave/weather timeline & IFP wave assessment
findings.title: Two scripts render the alternate planning rows in WX SETUP
findings.user_impact: Both render into #cfgAltPlanningRows; the click on WX SETUP triggers render() then renderSetup() 30 ms later, and typing in the alternates field triggers only the old render(), which rebuilds rows from storage (dropping V2's change handlers and hint text). Behaviour depends on which ran last.
findings.evidence: cfgAlts 'input' -> render (1407); sofWxSetupBtn click -> setTimeout(render,0) and setTimeout(renderSetup,30).

findings.note: multiple 1.5-5 s DOM rewrite intervals (28 setIntervals known)
findings.module: SOF Dashboard - wave/weather timeline & IFP wave assessment
findings.title: Repeated DOM rewriting from several 1.5-5 s timers
findings.user_impact: V2 rewrites card badges every 1.5 s, V4 removes and re-appends its alternate boxes every 1.8 s (cards change height each time), V8 recomputes signatures every 5 s, and the hidden lightning canvas redraws on every strike. Wasted CPU and small layout jitter in the weather rails.
findings.evidence: setInterval(()=>{hook();update()},1500); setInterval(render,1800); cards().forEach(c=>c.querySelectorAll('.altWaveAssessV4').forEach(x=>x.remove()));
findings.suggested_fix: Recompute only when inputs or card text change (observer/signature), and update boxes in place.

findings.note: tooltip Zulu only, global lane leak
findings.module: SOF Dashboard - wave/weather timeline & IFP wave assessment
findings.title: Timeline tooltips always show Zulu times and the build leaks a global variable
findings.user_impact: In LOCAL (CST) mode the axis is local but the tooltip time range is Zulu with no local equivalent, which can be misread. The comma in 'lab.textContent=A,lane=...' creates an implicit global `lane` (would throw under strict mode).
findings.evidence: tooltip: new Date(g.s).toISOString().slice(8,17).replace('T','/')+'Z'; window.lane exists after build.
findings.suggested_fix: Show both local and Z in the tooltip; declare lane with let.

findings.title: 'AIRFIELD WEATHER' label overprints the PACIFIC clock heading
findings.user_impact: The fixed/absolute 'AIRFIELD WEATHER' caption is positioned at top:67px and lands on top of the PACIFIC world-clock card at 1500 px width.
findings.evidence: Screenshot in headless Chromium at 1500x900: 'AIRFIELD WEATHER' text overlaps 'PACIFIC 14:57:30'. #sofLeftWeatherLabel{position:fixed;left:10px;top:67px;z-index:180001}.
findings.suggested_fix: Move the caption into the left rail header instead of absolute positioning.

findings.note: 4158 chords (t-1,t) and (t,t+1) are 1 s apart but result is divided by 2; EM turn rate is half. Flight math: pin old value, Dad signs off fix
findings.title: EM diagram plots turn rate at exactly half the real value
findings.user_impact: Every dot on the T-6 Energy-Maneuverability chart sits at half its true turn rate (a 19.2 deg/s level turn plots at 9.6 deg/s), so the aircraft look far below the T-6 envelope and the debrief conclusion about achieving max rate is wrong. The KML viewer's own Est G uses a different, correct formula, so the two panels disagree for the same track.
findings.evidence: metrics(): a=interp(t-1), p=interp(t), b=interp(t+1); h0=hdg(a,p); h1=hdg(p,b); then `const tr=Math.abs(dAng(h1,h0))*180/Math.PI/2;`. The two chords are centred at t-0.5 and t+0.5, i.e. only 1 s apart, but the result is divided by 2. I reproduced it in node with a synthetic 1 Hz circular track (220 kt, 4G, true omega 19.2 deg/s): the formula returns 9.60 deg/s. estimatedGAtTrack (2462-2478) divides by the whole t1-t0 window and is right. The same /2 mistake is in the 3D bank estimate (3802, see separate finding).
findings.suggested_fix: Per CLAUDE.md, first add a test that pins the current output, then (with the owner's OK) change the divisor to 1 s (or compute heading change over a symmetric window and divide by that window's real width). Put heading/turn-rate in one shared function used by EM, 3D bank and estimatedGAtTrack.

findings.title: 3D estimated pitch and the 3D tennis-arc pitch are unreachable: aircraftPitchAtTrack is private to the KML script
findings.user_impact: The T-6 model label always reads 'P 0deg' for any KML that has no native pitch channel (climbs and dives look level, and the label looks like measured data). The 3D tennis arc always fires with 0 deg + bias pitch, even when the KML has native pitch, and its readout says 'Pitch 0.0 (estimated)'. The KML 2D overlay uses the real pitch, so 2D and 3D give different results for the same shot.
findings.evidence: aircraftPitchAtTrack is a function declaration at 2446 inside the KML IIFE (opens 2103, closes 3293) and is never exported (no window.aircraftPitchAtTrack anywhere). 3D code does `(tr && typeof aircraftPitchAtTrack==='function') ? aircraftPitchAtTrack(tr,t) : null` (3793) and `(window.aircraftPitchAtTrack && a.getTracks?.()[shooterId]) ? aircraftPitchAtTrack(...) : {deg:0,source:'estimated'}` (3984). Both conditions are always false. attitudeFor's `src` is computed (3814) but never shown.
findings.suggested_fix: Expose pitch/G/heading helpers from the shared tracks module (or add them to window.DADS3DAPI) and call them from 3D. Show the source ('native' vs 'flight-path estimate') in the attitude label.

findings.note: 3799-3802 same chord/dt=2 halving; bank sign positive for left turn raises left wing; gNative>1.01 forces bank in wings-level pulls
findings.title: 3D T-6 model banks the wrong way, under-reads bank, and shows bank in wings-level pull-ups
findings.user_impact: In a left turn the model raises its left wing (a real left bank lowers it), so the picture is mirrored; the printed 'B' angle is about 17 percent low for a 4G turn, and any pull (g > 1.01) is displayed as a steep left bank even when the aircraft is wings level.
findings.evidence: Left turn = heading increasing (atan2(dy,dx)), so cross=sin(h1-h0)>0 and bank stays positive. wp() adds r=(cos(hdg+90deg),sin(hdg+90deg)), which is the LEFT side, and `const wingL=wp(s*.02,s*.66,Math.sin(bank)*s*.20)` gives that left wing +altitude for positive bank. Magnitude: `turnRate=Math.abs(headingDelta(h1,h0))/dt` with dt=2 s but h0/h1 chords are 1 s apart (same halving as EM); node test: true bank 75.5 deg, estimate 62.7 deg. G override: `bank = Math.sign(bank||1)*gBank;` so bank 0 becomes +gBank (always left) and any load factor implies bank. The wingtip offset is also only sin(bank)*0.2*size in feet, not span*sin(bank), and the horizontal span is not scaled by cos(bank).
findings.suggested_fix: Pin the current numbers with a test, then: negate the sign of the wing offset (or the sign of bank), use the corrected turn rate, apply the G-to-bank conversion only when pitch rate is small (or drop it), and drive the wing points from a real roll rotation (span*cos(bank) laterally, span*sin(bank) vertically).

findings.note: two ball solvers with different velocity formulas (3163 vs 3987); design: keep one
findings.title: Two different tennis-ball solvers (KML 2D overlay and 3D arc) disagree, share one readout element, and the controls live only in the 3D tab
findings.user_impact: For the same shooter/target/inputs the KML overlay and the 3D arc can show different verdicts (INTERCEPT vs NO INTERCEPT). The 3D cone is drawn twice as wide as the KML cone for the same 'Cone width' number. The KML viewer's tennis overlay is switched on by controls that are only reachable in the 3D tab, and its readout is written into a hidden 3D panel.
findings.evidence: Ball velocity: KML `vx=dir.x*(sv+ballFps*Math.cos(pitch)); vz=ballFps*Math.sin(pitch)` (3163-3165); 3D `vfps=ballKts*1.68781 + shooter.spdKt*1.68781; vz0=Math.sin(pitchDeg..)*vfps` (3987-3988), so with a non-zero pitch bias 3D climbs ~57 percent faster (161 vs 103 ft/s at 10 deg, 200 kt shooter). Target: KML extrapolates at constant speed, level (3166,3175); 3D samples the real future track (4002). Cone: KML uses +/- coneDeg/2 (3190, 3168); 3D `const h=hdg+side*cone` uses +/- the full coneDeg (4025). Min radius 10 vs 1 (3156 vs 3981). Heading: headingAtTrack vs 1-s look-back chord. Both writers set el 'kmlTennisReadout' (updateKmlTennisReadout 3202, draw3DDogfightArc 4052; the element exists once, in the 3D panel at 770) and the 3D rAF loop rewrites it every frame, so KML's IN CONE / OUT OF CONE status is never visible.
findings.suggested_fix: Extract one pure solver (inputs: shooter/target track, settings; output: points, best pass, in-cone flag) used by both views, drawn via each view's projection. Move the tennis controls and readout into the KML panel so they work in 2D and 3D.

findings.title: 3D view has no Play/Pause/scrub; threeDPlay and threeDPause do not exist, and playback keeps running invisibly
findings.user_impact: Someone watching the 3D view cannot start, stop or scrub the replay; they must switch tabs. Playback started in the KML tab keeps advancing while the user is in the 3D tab, Turn Sim, BFM or the launcher, and can only be stopped back in the KML tab. The help text admits this ('Play/Pause still controls playback there').
findings.evidence: `$('threeDPlay')?.addEventListener('click',()=>api()?.setPlaying?.(true));` and the threeDPause twin attach to ids that are not in the markup (the 3D toolbar at 749-754 has only a time pill and three sliders). window.DADS3DAPI (2113-2129) has setPlaying but no seek/setTime. switchTab only re-asserts playing (2164, 2171) and never pauses on leaving KML.
findings.suggested_fix: Delete the two dead lines. In the merged KML 2D/3D view the existing kmlPlay/kmlPause/kmlTimeSlider already serve both modes. Pause on leaving the debrief module (or when the tab is hidden).

findings.note: 4108/4188/3262 rAF loops run regardless of visible tab
findings.title: 3D, EM and KML redraw loops never stop when their module is hidden
findings.user_impact: Roughly 350 track interpolations per frame (about 21,000 per second at 60 fps with 4 tracks) run on every screen of the app, including Turn Sim, the launcher and other modules, even if the user never opens 3D; extra battery and heat on tablets. While playing in the 3D tab the hidden 2D KML map is also fully redrawn (tiles, VNC warp) every frame. One exception inside draw3D permanently kills the 3D loop.
findings.evidence: 3D: `function loop(){ draw3D(); requestAnimationFrame(loop); }` started unconditionally at 4131; draw3D calls getLive (4 interps), withHeading (4), drawTrails (4 x 81 getInterp = 324), attitudeFor (8) and rewrites innerHTML of threeDLive/threeDTracks/threeDStatus each frame (4087-4105). EM: `function loop(){try{draw()}catch(e){}requestAnimationFrame(loop)}` (4188): 16 interps per frame plus `img.src` checks while kmlEmCard is display:none, and the empty catch hides all errors. kmlLoop (3263) calls drawKml() and updateKmlReadouts() whenever kmlPlaying, regardless of which tab is showing. The 3D loop has no try/catch, unlike EM's, so a throw stops rendering until reload.
findings.suggested_fix: One scheduler: draw only the visible module (check offsetParent or IntersectionObserver), and only when time or a control changed (dirty flag). Wrap the frame in try/catch that re-arms requestAnimationFrame.

findings.note: ascending depth sort draws far aircraft last (on top) at pitch 0 and 90
findings.title: Aircraft are painted in the wrong depth order (far aircraft drawn on top of near ones)
findings.user_impact: When two aircraft overlap on screen (close formation, merges, stacked altitudes) the one farther from the camera is drawn last and hides the nearer one, so the picture gives the wrong sense of who is in front.
findings.evidence: `Object.entries(live).sort((A,B)=>project(A[1],ctr).depth-project(B[1],ctr).depth)` sorts ascending. In project(), depth=z2=y1*sp-dAlt*cp is larger for points farther north/lower, i.e. farther from the camera (checked at pitch 0 and 90). Numeric check at default view: near aircraft depth -446, far +446, ascending order draws near first and far last.
findings.suggested_fix: Sort descending (farthest first) so nearer aircraft overwrite farther ones.

findings.note: ground datum from live points; AGL label misleading
findings.title: Ground datum is not fixed, 'AGL' labels are not AGL, and three different horizontal planes are drawn
findings.user_impact: Default 'Lowest loaded alt' datum jumps in 500 ft steps as the lowest aircraft climbs or descends, so the ground plane hops and every '#n xxxx ft AGL' number shifts by 500 ft during playback. The labels say AGL/'ground' but are height above an arbitrary datum (or above sea level in 'Sea level' mode). Users see a landscape plane and a 'ground grid' at formation altitude plus a datum plane below, three planes with different meanings.
findings.evidence: groundDatumAlt: `Math.floor((Math.min(...vals)-500)/500)*500` over the CURRENT live points only (not the loaded tracks, despite the label 'Lowest loaded alt'). Overlay text 756 claims 'fixed ground datum'. Tower text: `${Math.round(agl)} ft AGL` (3731). drawLandscape and drawGrid place their planes at ctr.z (formation centre altitude, 3613-3616, 3771); drawGroundReference uses baseAlt. Only the 'field' mode (1892 ft, CYMJ elevation) is a stable, meaningful datum, and altitudes come from raw KML (altm*3.28084, 2379) with no altitudeMode check.
findings.suggested_fix: Default the datum to field elevation (or min over the whole loaded track, computed once). Label 'ft above datum' unless the datum is field elevation and altitude is known to be MSL. Remove the formation-altitude landscape/grid planes or rename them.

findings.title: Ground grid, landscape and reference arrows move with the formation centre, so the ground never appears to move
findings.user_impact: In Follow Lead or Center Formation mode the grid is re-centred on the camera every frame, so the aircraft appear to hover over a ground that slides along with them; ground speed, drift and track over the ground can only be judged from the trails. The highlighted 'x===0' grid line always runs through the centre.
findings.evidence: Grid lines are drawn at `ctr.x+x` / `ctr.y+y` for x,y in a fixed +/- range (e.g. `project({x:ctr.x+x,y:ctr.y-extent,altFt:baseAlt},ctr)`), not at world multiples. Comments say 'Fixed ground plane' and 'Fixed reference arrows' but the anchor is ctr. Cell size is fixed at 10,000 ft (3677), about 700 px at default zoom, so at most one or two lines are ever visible.
findings.suggested_fix: Snap grid origin to world multiples (Math.floor(ctr.x/step)*step) and offer a smaller step (1,000/5,000 ft) scaled with zoom.

findings.note: arrows off-screen at default zoom (computed, not rendered)
findings.title: N/E arrows, altitude scale and grid extent are far off-screen at default zoom
findings.user_impact: There is no visible compass/north indication and no visible altitude scale in the normal view, so after orbiting there is no way to tell which way is north. The 'Altitude scale' toggle appears to do nothing.
findings.evidence: Arrows are 30,000 ft long (`arrow('N',0,30000,...)`); the altitude scale sits at `ctr.x-42000, ctr.y+36000`. With the default view (yaw -35, pitch 52, zoom 70 = 0.07 px/ft, vertical exaggeration 2) on a 1280x1000 canvas I computed: N arrow tip at (1845,-504), E tip at (2360,1297), altitude scale base at (-323,-1754): all off-screen. They only come into view at zoom of about 12 or less, where aircraft are a few pixels long.
findings.suggested_fix: Place compass and altitude scale in screen space (a small corner gizmo/HUD) or size them from the current zoom.

findings.title: T-6 pitch is drawn as a screen-pixel shift of the whole aircraft, not as nose-up/nose-down, and mixes feet with pixels
findings.user_impact: A climbing aircraft is drawn up to 52 px above its true position (and a descending one below it), disconnected from its altitude tower; nose-up and nose-down look the same apart from that shift. The size of the error depends on zoom, not on altitude, so it looks like a false altitude change.
findings.evidence: `const pitchLift=Math.sin(pitch)*s*.20*dpr();` (feet used as pixels), `ctx.translate(0,-pitchLift);` then the label is shifted again with `pc.y-14*dpr()-pitchLift` (label offset applied twice). The nose point is always `wp(s*.82,0,s*.04)`, independent of pitch. `bankShift=Math.sin(bank)*s*.28` is used as pixel offset too (3866-3868). The canopy ellipse is rotated by world heading in screen space (3888), ignoring camera yaw and the y-flip, so it is misaligned.
findings.suggested_fix: Rotate the model points in 3D by pitch (nose alt = sin(pitch)*length) and project them; remove the screen-space translation.

findings.note: 3580 centerOf only tests followLead; threeDSticks unreachable in T-6 model
findings.title: Several 3D settings do nothing in the default configuration
findings.user_impact: 'Show altitude sticks' has no effect while 'Low-poly T-6' (the default) is selected; 'Free Orbit' behaves exactly like 'Center Formation'; 'Show attitude labels' does nothing with the flat model. Ground datum, grid, landscape, ground reference and altitude scale are five overlapping toggles for one idea.
findings.evidence: drawPlane returns at `if($('threeDModel')?.value==='t6') return drawLowPolyT6(id,p,ctr);` before the only use of threeDSticks (3916). centerOf tests only `=== 'followLead'` (3580), so both 'formation' and 'free' fall through to the centroid. The flat model has no label code (3936).
findings.suggested_fix: Remove Free Orbit and the sticks toggle (the datum towers already show altitude), or implement them. Collapse the ground toggles into one 'Ground reference' choice.

findings.note: collapse CSS targets main and #kmlApp only
findings.title: Hide controls / Hide metrics rails and the Tab shortcut do nothing in the 3D view
findings.user_impact: The always-visible side rails show 'Hide controls'/'Hide metrics' over the 3D panels, but pressing them (or Tab / Shift+Tab) changes nothing in 3D; it silently collapses the panels of the other modules and the rail hint flips to 'Show controls' although the 3D side panels are still open. The fixed rails also sit on top of the 3D card headings. Tab is prevented on every non-input element, which breaks keyboard navigation of buttons.
findings.evidence: The grid overrides target only `main` and `#kmlApp` (`body.leftCollapsed main, body.leftCollapsed #kmlApp{...}`), never `#threeDApp`, and the redraw after collapse does not call DADS3DResize. The keydown handler `if(e.key==='Tab' && ...) {e.preventDefault(); ...}` only exempts input/textarea/select.
findings.suggested_fix: Either include #threeDApp in the collapse rules and resize the canvas, or hide the rails on modules that do not support them. Do not hijack Tab.

findings.title: KML tab click handler re-attaches the VNC/overlay listeners on every click (reachable from 'Go to KML Viewer')
findings.user_impact: Each visit to the KML tab (including the 3D 'Go to KML Viewer' button and every module-launcher entry) adds another copy of the embedded-VNC change/opacity/nudge/scale/reset listeners, so after N visits one slider move calls the expensive drawKml() N times. Before the first visit those controls are not wired at all.
findings.evidence: `el('kmlTab').onclick=()=>{switchTab('kml'); el('kmlEmbeddedVnc')?.addEventListener('change',...); el('kmlEmbeddedVncOpacity')?.addEventListener('input',...); ... initKmlOverlayDropdown();};` The closing `};` at 2191 shows all of these lines are inside the onclick body. threeDGoKml just calls `kmlTab.click()`.
findings.suggested_fix: Move the listener wiring out of the onclick body so it runs once at startup.

findings.title: Aircraft #4 (black) has an invisible trail and altitude tower on the 3D background
findings.user_impact: The #4 trail and the dashed altitude tower are drawn in #050505 on a #050b12 / dark-green scene, so they cannot be seen; #4 can only be found by its white outline and label.
