findings.evidence: KML_COLORS 4:'#050505'; colorFor(4) returns the same; drawTrails uses `ctx.strokeStyle=colorFor(+id)` at alpha .55 and drawGroundReference uses colorFor for the tower at alpha .95, over `ctx.fillStyle='#050b12'` and a ground gradient ending #07100a. Only the plane body gets a white stroke (3865).
findings.suggested_fix: Use a light outline/halo (or a lighter colour such as light grey) for #4 trails and towers in the dark 3D scene.

findings.title: EM diagram x-axis uses ground speed as airspeed, so wind moves the dots
findings.user_impact: The dot's speed position swings by the wind speed as the aircraft turns (in a full circle GS varies from V-W to V+W: about +/-30 kt for a 30 kt wind, which is about 110 px on this chart), and the energy comparison to the published T-6 curve is off by that amount. The limitation is mentioned only in the small note under the chart.
findings.evidence: `const gs=Number.isFinite(p.spdKt)?p.spdKt:...; const ias=gs*Math.sqrt(Math.max(.15,isaRhoRatio(alt)));` (also EAS not IAS/CAS, negligible at T-6 speeds). ISA density itself is correct: my check gives sigma 0.8232 at 6,500 ft, 0.7860 at 8,000 ft, 0.6713 at 13,000 ft.
findings.suggested_fix: Allow a manual wind (or estimate wind from GS vs heading over the loaded track) and convert GS to TAS before density correction; show the assumed wind on the chart.

findings.title: 3D canvas has no touch or pinch support
findings.user_impact: On a tablet the scene cannot be orbited or zoomed by touch; only the three sliders work. (CLAUDE.md requires the tool to be usable anywhere in a normal browser.)
findings.evidence: Only mousedown/mousemove/mouseup and wheel listeners exist; no touch/pointer events. Yaw is clamped to +/-180 (4117), so a drag stops instead of wrapping.
findings.suggested_fix: Use Pointer Events with pointer capture and two-pointer pinch for zoom; wrap yaw.

findings.title: Vertical exaggeration defaults to 2x with no on-screen indication
findings.user_impact: Altitude separations, climb angles and the aircraft's own vertical dimensions look twice as large as the horizontal ones; nothing in the 3D view says so, while the tower labels quote true feet.
findings.evidence: `<input id="threeDAltScale" ... value="2.0">`; project() applies `z=-((p.altFt||0)-ctr.z)*altScale` to every point including model offsets and the ground plane; the overlay text at 756 does not mention it. Aircraft size default 260 ft makes each icon about 410 ft long (real T-6 is about 33 ft).
findings.suggested_fix: Show 'Vertical x2.0' in the overlay/HUD and default to 1.0 for debrief geometry.

findings.title: Toolbar pills cover the empty-state message and wrap over the scene on narrow stages
findings.user_impact: With no tracks loaded, the first part of 'Load KML tracks in the KML Viewer...' is hidden behind the '3D Debrief' pill. At stage widths under about 650 px (window narrower than roughly 1300 px) the four pills wrap to two rows and hide the top of the scene.
findings.evidence: `.threeDToolbar{position:absolute;top:10px;...;flex-wrap:wrap}` over the canvas; the message is drawn at `fillText(...,24*dpr(),40*dpr())`; pills have an opaque background (`.pill{...background:#0b141d}`). Grid column is minmax(520px,1fr) with 300px + 340px side panels (34).
findings.suggested_fix: Draw the message centred, and reserve toolbar height (put the toolbar in normal flow above the canvas).

findings.title: EM card is stretched and styled by three stacked !important CSS blocks; two of them are dead
findings.user_impact: The EM chart image is stretched to whatever box the flex layout gives it (2:1 aspect ratio is forcibly disabled), so the chart's text and curves are probably distorted on wide windows; the dots stay registered because they use the same stretch.
findings.evidence: kmlEmLayoutFix (relative), kmlEmBottomOverlayFix (absolute overlay, height min(46%,430px)) and kmlEmAutoShrinkMapFix (relative flex 43%) all target #kmlEmCard; whenever the card is visible the stage has .kml-em-open, whose higher-specificity rules override the first two, so their position/size rules never take effect. `aspect-ratio:auto!important` with `` (691).
findings.suggested_fix: Keep one rule set; keep aspect-ratio:2/1 with max-height and centre the chart (letterbox) so it is not distorted.

findings.title: Post-layout refresh code calls functions that are not global; showApp's refresh throws and skips the rest
findings.user_impact: After 'Hide controls' the KML canvas backing store is never resized (bitmap is CSS-stretched until the next window resize or tab switch), and the EM toggle only works because its fallback dispatches a global window 'resize'. The 60 ms refresh in showApp throws, so its DADS3DResize/draw/drawKml calls never run (switchTab's own 30 ms timer covers 3D).
findings.evidence: resizeKml and drawKml are declared inside the KML IIFE (2192, 3014), so `typeof resizeKml==='function'` is false everywhere else and `resizeKml?.()` at 3314 throws ReferenceError (optional call does not guard an undeclared name), caught by the surrounding try, aborting the rest of the line. drawKmlEmDiagram, drawKmlEM and resizeKmlCanvas (4197-4205) do not exist anywhere.
findings.suggested_fix: Export a small module API (resizeKml, drawKml) and call it explicitly; delete the lookups for non-existent names.

findings.note: Turn Sim listeners live in the 3D script block (4134-4144)
findings.title: Turn Sim rear-check and breadcrumb listeners are wired inside the 3D script block
findings.user_impact: If the 3D IIFE ever throws while initialising, the Turn Sim 'Check turn' and breadcrumb controls silently stop working; the coupling is invisible.
findings.evidence: After the 3D IIFE closes at 4132, the same script tag continues with `['rearCheckEnabled','rearCheckStart',...].forEach(...)` and `['breadcrumbToggle','breadcrumbInterval'].forEach(...)`, which call Turn Sim globals (activeList, resetRearCheckState, updateRearCheckStatus, resetBreadcrumbHistory, draw). `n.addEventListener(id==='breadcrumbInterval'?'change':'change',...)` is a no-op ternary.
findings.suggested_fix: Move these lines to the Turn Sim module.

findings.module: SOF Dashboard - IFP wave assessment / weather timeline / alternate ETA
findings.lines: 1419-1430 (vals, used at 1466); 1559 (v() in altWaveAssessmentV4); 2008-2010 (visibility/parts in timeline V8)
findings.title: TAF visibility parser treats the TAF period token as the whole-number part of a fraction, so TEMPO/BECMG/PROB groups with 1/2SM, 3/4SM or 1/4SM are never flagged
findings.user_impact: For a forecast like 'TEMPO 2918/2922 1/2SM FG' the home-weather check reads visibility as 2922.5 SM, so during the wave the page says 'IFP HOME WX GOOD FOR WAVE' / 'NO HOME-WX ALT TRIGGER' when an alternate should be required. The timeline bar for the same TEMPO is labelled '2922 1/2SM' and its NATO colour is graded as if visibility were huge. In the alternate panel 'M1/4SM' is read as 4 SM.
findings.evidence: Line 1423 `else if(x=t.match(/\b(\d+)\s+(\d+)\/(\d+)SM\b/))v=+x[1]+ +x[2]/+x[3];` is tried before the plain-fraction regex at 1424, so in 'TEMPO 2916/2920 1/2SM FG' it matches '2920 1/2SM'. I ran the copied functions in node: vals('TEMPO 2916/2920 1/2SM FG') -> {v:2920.5}; vals('BECMG 2916/2918 3/4SM BR') -> {v:2918.75}; tafHazards on 'TAF CYMJ 291130Z 2912/3018 27010KT P6SM SCT050 TEMPO 2918/2922 1/2SM FG' with a 19-20Z wave returned hits [] while the same TAF with '2SM BR' returned a TEMPO hit. Running timeline V8 tafGroups on a TEMPO 0106/0110 1/2SM group produced the label '0110 1/2SM'. V4 line 1559 has no M-prefix branch: 'M1/4SM' falls through to `(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)SM` and returns 4.
findings.suggested_fix: Blank out validity/issue tokens (\d{4}/\d{4}, FM\d{6}, \d{6}Z) before extracting visibility, and anchor the mixed-fraction case to a single-digit whole part not preceded by a digit or slash. Handle M1/4SM explicitly. Keep one shared TAF/METAR parser (there are 4 copies: 1419, 1559, 2008 plus inert ones) with unit tests for 1/4SM, 1/2SM, 1 1/2SM, M1/4SM, P6SM, 9999, CAVOK directly after a period token.

findings.title: BECMG conditions stop applying when the transition period ends, so a forecast deterioration after BECMG is reported as 'home weather good for wave'
findings.user_impact: If the TAF says 'BECMG 2918/2920 BKN008' and the wave is 21-23Z, the IFP badge shows 'IFP HOME WX GOOD FOR WAVE' (or 'NO HOME-WX ALT TRIGGER') although the forecast ceiling after 20Z is 800 ft. This is the unsafe direction: an alternate requirement is missed.
findings.evidence: Each change group gets s..e equal to its own period (`else{s=utcFor(+m[5],...);e=utcFor(+m[7],+m[8],0,s)...}` line 1463) and `groups.forEach(g=>{if(!overlap(g.s,g.e,w.s,w.plus1))return;...` line 1466 only tests groups overlapping the wave. Under ICAO/WMO rules BECMG conditions persist after the transition until superseded. Node test with TAF 'TAF CYMJ 291130Z 2912/3018 27010KT P6SM SCT050 BECMG 2918/2920 BKN008' and wave 21Z-22Z (+1h = 23Z): hits [] (groups: INITIAL 12Z-18Z(30th), BECMG 18Z-20Z). The visual timeline (line 2025) does handle this correctly (`current=inherit(current,source)`), so the timeline and the alternate verdict can disagree.
findings.suggested_fix: Build one prevailing-conditions timeline (BASE -> FM replaces everything -> BECMG blends over its period then becomes the new base -> TEMPO/PROB are overlays) and use it for both the timeline and the wave/alternate check. The V8 tafGroups (2014-2030) is the closest to correct; extract it into a shared, tested module.

findings.note: scan-sof-c#8 (confirmed code: part starts as whole TAF, 1559)
findings.title: Alternate-airfield 'at ETA' forecast uses the whole TAF text when the ETA precedes the first FM group, and ignores TEMPO/BECMG times
findings.user_impact: The alternate card can show ceilings and visibilities from hours after the ETA (or from a different group than the one in force). Example: ETA 2100Z with 'P6SM SCT050 FM300300 ... 1SM BR OVC004' shows '400 FT / 6.01 SM' - the OVC004 is from a group that starts 6 hours after the ETA, and vis is taken from the first match only. Pilots may reject a perfectly good alternate, or (with vis taken only from the first token in a FM group) accept one with a TEMPO/BECMG low-visibility period.
findings.evidence: `let t=...,part=t,ms=[...t.matchAll(/\bFM(\d{2})(\d{2})(\d{2})\b/g)];for(...){let st=uf(...);if(st<=e)part=t.slice(ms[i].index,ms[i+1]?.index??t.length)}return v(part)` - `part` starts as the ENTIRE TAF and only shrinks if a FM group is already in force. `v()` then takes the MIN ceiling of every BKN/OVC/VV in `part` (all groups) but the FIRST visibility match. Node test: at(raw='... P6SM SCT050 FM300300 27008KT 1SM BR OVC004', ETA 29th 21Z) -> {vis:6.01, ceil:400}; ETA 30th 04Z -> {vis:1, ceil:400}. Also displays P6SM as '6.01 SM' (line 1573 prints z.vis).
findings.suggested_fix: Use the shared prevailing-conditions timeline (see finding on BECMG) and evaluate BASE plus any TEMPO/PROB overlay whose period contains the ETA (with a clear label such as 'TEMPO 1SM BR'). Display P6SM as '>6 SM'.

findings.note: 1441 Date.UTC(...,ah+6,...) always; labels say TAKEOFF/LAND with no zone
findings.module: SOF Dashboard - wave inputs / IFP assessment / timeline
findings.title: Wave TAKEOFF/LAND inputs are always interpreted as Moose Jaw local (CST) time but nothing near them says so, and the LOCAL/ZULU toggle does not change how they are read
findings.user_impact: A pilot who flips the timeline to ZULU and types a Zulu takeoff (e.g. 1800) gets the wave treated as 1800 CST = 0000Z the next day. TAF coverage, 'ALTERNATE REQUIRED' and the alternate ETA check are then computed for the wrong 6 hours, with no warning. The only text saying the times are local is aria-label 'Wave local date' on the hidden old waveBar (line 526).
findings.evidence: Labels are plain `TAKEOFF` (1255) and the timeline clones get `l.textContent=k.replace('waveOps','').toUpperCase()+' '` (2036) i.e. 'TAKEOFF', 'LAND', 'DATE'. Conversion is always `Date.UTC(Y,M-1,D,ah+6,am)` (1441) / `sh+6` (1561) / `CST+mins*60000` (2032) regardless of the toggle stored in `dadSofTimelineTimeMode`.
findings.suggested_fix: Label the inputs with the active zone ('TAKEOFF (L CST)' or '(Z)') and make the inputs follow the global time mode: convert what the user types using the selected zone, store the result as an absolute UTC instant, and show both Z and local next to each value.

findings.note: UTC-6 and America/Regina hard-coded in 10+ places; conflicts with decision that home airfield is a setting
findings.title: The home-airfield setting does not carry a time zone: every wave/TAF conversion, the 'MOOSE JAW / CST' clock and the '(CST)' timeline header are hard-wired to UTC-6
findings.user_impact: Today the setup dialog already lets a user change HOME from CYMJ. If they do (or once the home field becomes a general setting), wave times are still converted at a fixed UTC-6 with no DST, the header still says '(CST)' and the world clock still says MOOSE JAW, so a US or eastern-Canada home field gets a Zulu window that is off by 1-5 hours (or 1 hour in summer for US Central) and the TAF-coverage/alternate verdicts are wrong.
findings.evidence: Active hard-codes: 515 `MOOSE JAW...CST`; 753 `cMoose.textContent=timeAt("America/Regina")`; 771 `["cMoose",null,"America/Regina"]`; 859 `timeZone:"America/Regina"`; 1441 `Date.UTC(Y,M-1,D,ah+6,am)`; 1561 `sh+6`; 1987 `CST=3600000*6`; 2000 `Date.now()-CST`; 2001 `Date.UTC(y,m,d,local?6:0)`; 2032 `+CST+mins*60000`; 2035 `(W.local?' (CST)':'')`. Inert copies also at 88, 93, 109 (dead block) and 1527 (old script). None of them read C.home.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a Home Time Zone (IANA id, e.g. America/Regina) chosen with the home airfield (ICAO->tz table plus manual override) and route all conversions through one helper that uses Intl (DST-safe), e.g. localToUtc(dateStr,timeStr,tz) and zoneAbbrev(tz,instant). Keep America/Regina as the default for CYMJ (fixed UTC-6, no DST).

findings.note: sof.html line 4 <script src=leaflet> holds inline lines 5-113 until </script> at 114; browsers ignore that code, so applyWxHighlights (66) never exists
findings.module: SOF Dashboard - weather limits / wave bar
findings.title: First SOF script block is swallowed by the Leaflet <script src> tag, so applyWxHighlights, the limit-highlighting, the 'NEW WEATHER LIMIT' caution and localWindow/updateWave never run
findings.user_impact: Configured weather-limit highlighting on raw METAR/TAF (orange/yellow tokens), the per-airfield 'configured limits clear / warning' box and the amber 'NEW WEATHER LIMIT' caution popup never appear, because applyWxHighlights is never defined. (This makes the already-known 'ACKNOWLEDGE / CLEAR' ordering bug moot until the tag is fixed - the popup is never opened at all.)
findings.evidence: Line 4 `<script src="https://unpkg.com/leaflet@1.9.4/dist/leaflet.js">` is immediately followed by 109 lines of inline code (lines 5-113) and the first `</script>` is at line 114. Browsers ignore the text of a script element that has src. I decoded window.__SOF_DOC__ from original/shell.html line 4309 and it is byte-identical to sof.html, so this is in the shipped file. `applyWxHighlights` is defined only at line 66; the live weather feed calls it behind `typeof window.applyWxHighlights==="function"` (830) so it silently skips; the older loadWx (629) calls it unguarded but dies earlier at 610 because there is no #wxstatus element. localWindow/updateWave (83-113, the +6 CST wave-bar text) are in the same swallowed block.
findings.suggested_fix: Close the Leaflet tag (`<script src=...></script>`) and put lines 5-113 in their own <script>. Then fix the ack-button ordering (894 runs before the button at 959) and de-duplicate the highlight/limit logic in the refactor.

findings.title: In ZULU mode the 24-hour timeline covers 0000Z-2400Z of the LOCAL wave date, so evening waves (after about 1800 local) fall outside the axis and disappear
findings.user_impact: Night/late waves (takeoff 1800-2359 local = 0000-0559Z next day) show no wave band, no LAND / LAND+1 markers and no TAF context in ZULU mode, so the wave looks unplanned or the timeline appears broken after toggling.
findings.evidence: windowUtc: `let s=Date.UTC(y,m,d,local?6:0);return{s,e:s+DAY,...}` - in ZULU mode s is 00Z of the same calendar date that was entered as a local date. absTake for 19:00 local = Date.UTC(y,m,d,0)+6h+19h = d+1 01:00Z > W.e, so `we=Math.min(absLand,W.e); if(we>ws)` is false and the band is skipped; the marker test `x>=W.s&&x<=W.e` (2042) also fails.
findings.suggested_fix: Anchor the Zulu axis on the wave itself (start at the wave's local midnight, or takeoff-2h, or let the user pick the Zulu date). Show the local hour ticks beside the Zulu ones.

findings.title: INITIAL TAF group is treated as valid for the whole TAF when the first change group is not FM, causing false 'ALTERNATE REQUIRED'
findings.user_impact: A TAF such as 'P6SM BKN012 TEMPO 2912/2915 3SM BR FM291800 P6SM SKC' flags the 1200 ft ceiling for a wave at 20-21Z even though FM291800 replaces those conditions. Users learn to distrust the verdict (or stop reading it).
findings.evidence: `groups.push({name:'INITIAL',...,e:ms[0]&&ms[0][2]?utcFor(...):tv.e})` - the INITIAL period ends at the first FM only if the FIRST change group happens to be an FM. Node test with that TAF and a 20-21Z wave: hits [{name:'INITIAL',c:1200,v:6.01}]. Both this and the BECMG finding come from the same missing 'prevailing conditions' model.
findings.suggested_fix: Same fix as the BECMG finding: base conditions end at the first FM (or when a completed BECMG replaces them), regardless of the order of TEMPO/PROB groups.

findings.note: fmtTime Z-only in KML, seconds in 3D, local-first in hidden SOF; no shared switch (requirement R10)
findings.module: Cross-module (KML, 3D, Turn Sim, Traffic, SOF, launcher)
findings.title: No shared Zulu/local switch: every module shows time differently (Z only, local only, relative seconds, or a private toggle)
findings.user_impact: Owner wants Zulu first with local beside it and one switch. Today: KML debrief shows Zulu only ('t = 18:19:04Z'), never local, and no date; the 3D debrief shows only elapsed seconds ('3D time 12.3 sec'); Turn Sim shows 't = 12.3 sec'; Traffic shows sim MM:SS; SOF has its own LOCAL/ZULU toggle that only affects the timeline (default LOCAL, and a one-time migration forces LOCAL again); SOF TAF chips and alternate ETA are Z only; the (hidden) launcher SOF clock shows local first then Z. The example flight is 18:16-20:04Z which is 12:16-14:04 CST, so a debrief between pilots talking local time cannot line up with the on-screen clock.
findings.evidence: main.html 2429 `function fmtTime(sec){... toISOString().substr(11,8)+'Z'; }` is the only KML formatter (used by pill 3039, status 2426, summary 2427, DFPs 2763, per-track readout 3250); 4089 `tp.textContent=`3D time ${fmt(rel,1)} sec``; 4432 `d.toLocaleString(...)+'  |  '+d.toISOString().slice(11,19)+'Z'` (local first, no zone name); sof.html 1987-1988 `if(!localStorage.getItem(MIG)){localStorage.setItem(KEY,'LOCAL');...}`; 1469 `fmt(d)` -> 'DD/HHZ'; traffic.html 461 `toISOString().substr(14,5)`.
findings.suggested_fix: Create one time module (mode: ZULU-first | LOCAL-first | Z only | L only; home tz; both shown as '1829Z (1229 CST)') persisted in localStorage under one key. srcdoc iframes are same-origin with the parent, so SOF and Traffic can read the same key and react to the 'storage' event. Route every clock, DTG, KML/DFP time and TAF time through it.

findings.note: clock order and hard-coded MOOSE JAW/CST (515)
findings.title: SOF world clocks put ZULU last and label the home clock with hard-coded 'MOOSE JAW' / 'CST'
findings.user_impact: Owner wants Zulu first. Order is PACIFIC, MOUNTAIN, MOOSE JAW, NEW YORK / OTTAWA, GMT / UTC, so the reference clock is at the far right; the home clock cannot be re-pointed at another field; the 'CST' caption is static text rather than the zone abbreviation.
findings.evidence: 513-517 markup order and `<small>CST</small>` (515); DTG 'zuluDTG' (511/755) is correct (`DDHHMMZ MON YY`) but is small text in the title row, not with the clocks.
findings.suggested_fix: Render Zulu first and largest with the DTG, then Home (label and zone from the setting via Intl timeZoneName:'short'), then the other reference zones.

findings.note: 1283 restores stored date with no today check
findings.title: Wave date saved in localStorage is never rolled to today, so the timeline and TAF-coverage check silently use yesterday's date
findings.user_impact: Next morning the wave date still says the previous day. The timeline shows the wrong 24-hour window and the verdicts show 'TAF DOES NOT COVER WAVE' (or, for a still-valid TAF, judge the wrong day) until the pilot notices and retypes the date. If the date is empty the timeline defaults to today's CST date (2000) but the assessment returns null and shows 'SET WAVE TIMES' (1438), so the two views disagree.
findings.evidence: `date.value=localStorage.getItem(keys()+'date')||'';` (1283) with no comparison to today; `date.onchange=()=>localStorage.setItem(keys()+'date',date.value)` (1292). The dead wave bar had a default-to-today (88-111) but that block never executes (see the swallowed-script finding).
findings.suggested_fix: Default to today's date in the home zone when nothing is stored or the stored date is in the past, and show the resolved Zulu window under the inputs.

findings.note: reportTime stored but never shown; status always LIVE (831) - conflicts with stale-data requirement
findings.title: SOF weather cards show no observation/issue time or age and the status says 'LIVE' whatever the data age
findings.user_impact: A stale or cached METAR/TAF (feed outage, Datamask caching) looks exactly like a fresh one. For an SOF the age of the observation matters more than the text; nothing tells them the last successful refresh time or that a METAR is 3 hours old. (Same on the launcher's own AWC cards, main.html 4450, though those are unreachable.)
findings.evidence: parseRawMetar stores `reportTime:observedAt||null` (579) but no code renders it; card() prints only `.wxraw` text (619, 808-818) and sets `status.textContent="LIVE"` (831 and 629). The timeline parses the DDHHMMZ out of the raw text only to place a marker (2013).
findings.suggested_fix: Show 'OBS 291900Z (23 min ago)' on each card, colour it amber when a METAR is older than about 75 min or a TAF older than 6 h, and show the last successful fetch time in Zulu beside the status. Prefer the AWC JSON fields obsTime/reportTime and validTimeFrom/validTimeTo.

findings.note: traffic rebuild multiplies speed twice (per quoted 431-454)
findings.title: Traffic sim rewind and +/-10 s buttons place aircraft wrongly whenever sim speed is not 1x
findings.user_impact: At 2x/4x/0.5x, 'Back 10 s', 'Fwd 10 s' and Rewind put every aircraft at 2x/4x/0.5x the distance the same moment had when played forward, so replay does not match the live run and separation/conflict readouts at a rewound time are wrong. Speed changes also change the rebuilt position of the same clock time.
findings.evidence: Forward: `t+=dt*mult; ... a.prog+=speedFps(pr.speed)*dt*mult` (454) so prog = speed * t. Rebuild: `t+=stepDt; ... let fakeAdvance=stepDt*mult; ... a.prog+=speedFps(pr.speed)*fakeAdvance` (431-440) so prog = speed * t * mult. 579: `$('back10Btn').onclick=()=>{t=Math.max(0,t-10);rebuildPositionsAtTime(t);...` and fwd10 the same. Reverse play (454) rebuilds from t=0 every frame (O(t/0.5) per frame).
findings.suggested_fix: Do not multiply by mult inside rebuildPositionsAtTime (t is already sim-time). Better, record per-aircraft snapshots or use a fixed-step deterministic simulation so reverse is a lookup.

findings.title: KML <when> without a zone designator is parsed as the viewer's local time and then labelled Zulu
findings.user_impact: A KML exported without 'Z' or an offset shows every timestamp shifted by the viewer's UTC offset but printed with a 'Z' suffix (e.g. a Toronto viewer sees 22:16:56Z for a track logged at 18:16:56). Tracks from different sources will also not line up in the common playback window. ForeFlight files carry Z, so the built-in example is not affected.
findings.evidence: `Date.parse(n.textContent.trim())/1000`. Node with TZ=America/Toronto: Date.parse('2026-06-02T18:16:56') -> 22:16:56Z; with '+00:00' or 'Z' it is correct. fmtTime prints `toISOString().substr(11,8)+'Z'`. Built-in example timestamps look like '2026-06-02T18:16:56.405344963Z' (9 fractional digits; V8 parses them, ms precision).
findings.suggested_fix: If the string has no Z/offset, decide explicitly (assume UTC per the KML/XSD convention used by ForeFlight, or warn and ask) instead of using the browser zone. Show a small 'times assumed UTC' note when guessing.

findings.title: DFP flags are stored under one global key, so flags and notes from an old flight appear on any other flight
findings.user_impact: Debrief a new sortie and the DFP list still shows the previous sortie's flags with their old Zulu times. 'Go To' clamps the time into the new flight's [start,end] (jumps to start or end) and the flag is drawn at the old flight's x/y (local plane relative to the old reference point). Notes written for one debrief leak into the next.
findings.evidence: `function dfpStorageKey(){ return 'dadsEzDebrief_dfps_v1'; }` with `loadDfps()` at page start (3291) and `goToDfp`: `kmlT=Math.max(kmlStart,Math.min(kmlEnd,dfps[i].t))`. DFPs store t (epoch seconds) plus x/y relative to kmlRef, but not which flight they belong to.
findings.suggested_fix: Key DFPs by flight identity (e.g. the common start epoch plus track file names/first-point hashes), store lat/lon and re-project on load, and add an export/import.

findings.title: The WAVE 1-5 selector, the manual 'alternate required' toggle and the IFP verdict chips are hidden or never created
findings.user_impact: Only the last-saved wave (dadSofActiveWave) can be edited; there is no visible way to switch to WAVE 2-5 or to toggle 'ALTERNATE REQUIRED'. The verdict 'TAF DOES NOT COVER WAVE / ALTERNATE REQUIRED / NO HOME-WX ALT TRIGGER' is written to #waveAltStatus (hidden) and to #waveIfpTrigger, which the active code never creates (it is created only in an inert text/plain script at 1355), so the only visible result is the badge on the home card.
findings.evidence: `#waveOpsBar,#waveOpsRow,#waveBar,#waveRow,... {display:none!important}` (460-465) hides the row containing `<select id="waveOpsSelect">`; the timeline copies controls with `['waveOpsWave','waveOpsDate','waveOpsTakeoff','waveOpsLand']` (2036) but there is no element `waveOpsWave` (the selector is waveOpsSelect); 1491 `box=document.getElementById('waveIfpTrigger')` then `if(box){...}`.
findings.suggested_fix: Clone waveOpsSelect (and the alternate toggle) into the timeline header, or in the refactor make Wave 1-5 a proper model; render the verdict chips explicitly in the timeline header.

findings.title: Duplicate clock timers rewrite the same world-clock elements up to three times a second
findings.user_impact: No visible bug today, but cMoose is written by 3 timers, the other clocks by 2, and each tick builds ~10 new Intl.DateTimeFormat objects; Mountain uses America/Denver in one and America/Edmonton in the other, so they only agree by luck of matching DST rules. clockSafety also contains a second DTG formatter (4-digit year) for a #dtg element that does not exist, so it never runs, while the visible DTG (zuluDTG) uses a 2-digit year.
findings.evidence: `setInterval(updateClocks,1000)` (757), `tick();setInterval(tick,1000)` (784), `setInterval(tickMooseJaw,1000)` (868); 752 `timeAt("America/Denver")` vs 770 `"America/Edmonton"`; 781 `document.getElementById("dtg")` (no such id, so the 4-digit-year DTG code is dead).
findings.suggested_fix: One clock component fed by the time module, formatters created once.

findings.title: KML timestamps fall back to point index, and a bad <when> shifts all later timestamps
findings.user_impact: A KML with no <when> (plain LineString) is shown with fake 'Zulu' clocks such as 00:00:05Z and all loaded tracks start at the same instant regardless of real time; the CSV export writes 1970 dates. If one <when> is blank/unparseable the array is compacted and every later point gets the previous point's time. <TimeStamp><when> elements elsewhere in the file are also picked up and misalign the index.
findings.evidence: `let when=[...xml.getElementsByTagName('when')].map(n=>Date.parse(...)/1000).filter(Number.isFinite)` then `t:when[i]??i` (2366) and per-node `when[i]` for <coordinates> (2369).
findings.suggested_fix: Keep NaN placeholders so indexes stay aligned, scope <when> to the gx:Track being read, and when there are no times show 'no timestamps' instead of 00:00:xxZ.

findings.title: Pressing Play after the KML playback reaches the end does nothing
findings.user_impact: After a run finishes the Play button appears dead until the user presses Reset or drags the slider.
findings.evidence: kmlLoop: `if(kmlT>=kmlEnd){kmlT=kmlEnd;kmlPlaying=false;}`; `el('kmlPlay').onclick=()=>{if(Object.keys(tracks).length){kmlPlaying=true;kmlLastReal=performance.now();}}` - it does not rewind when kmlT===kmlEnd, so the next frame stops again.
findings.suggested_fix: In the Play handler, if kmlT>=kmlEnd set kmlT=kmlStart first.

findings.title: Time text formats are inconsistent inside the SOF panel: chips drop minutes, alternate ETA keeps them, tooltips are Zulu-only with a colon on a local axis
findings.user_impact: 'WAVE 29/20Z -> LAND+1 29/23Z' truncates a 20:30Z start / 23:40Z end, so 'TAF DOES NOT COVER 29/20Z-29/23Z' can hide a 40 minute gap. The alternate card uses 'DD/HHMMZ' and the timeline tooltip uses 'DD/HH:MMZ'. In LOCAL mode the axis is local but hover text is Zulu only.
findings.evidence: 1469 `${DD}/${HH}Z` (no minutes) vs 1570 `${DD}/${HH}${MM}Z`; 2044 `new Date(g.s).toISOString().slice(8,17).replace('T','/')+'Z'`.
findings.suggested_fix: One formatter (DDHHMMZ plus local in brackets) used by all of them.

findings.note: traffic clock MM:SS wraps at 1 h
findings.title: Traffic sim clock shows only MM:SS and wraps to 00:00 after one hour of sim time
findings.user_impact: Long runs at 4x-8x show a clock that restarts at 00:00 every hour, and it is not a wall/Zulu time.
findings.evidence: `$('clock').textContent=new Date(t*1000).toISOString().substr(14,5);` - substr(14,5) is MM:SS only.
findings.suggested_fix: Format as HH:MM:SS from t, and (if useful) show optional Zulu wall-clock start + t.

findings.note: hidden main.html SOF (4316-4476) with running 1 s timer; DADSSOF.show has no callers
findings.title: Hidden older SOF dashboard in main.html (with its own local|Zulu clock and AWC fetch) is never shown but keeps a 1-second timer running
findings.user_impact: No visible effect except a wasted timer and duplicate logic. The launcher's SOF card opens the iframe (main.html 3344-3346), not this section; DADSSOF.show() is defined at 4474 but nothing calls it. Its clock is the only local-first/Z-second display (`d.toLocaleString(...) | HH:MM:SSZ`) and its cards never show METAR/TAF times.
findings.evidence: `window.DADSSOF={show(){...}}` (4474) has no callers; `setInterval(clock,1000);clock();` (4433) runs forever against a display:none section.
findings.suggested_fix: Delete section #sofDashboard and its two scripts in the refactor.

findings.title: Three redundant wave-time input sets and 13 inert text/plain script blocks (8 of them old wave/timeline builds using minute-of-day math that ignores date and zone)
findings.user_impact: No visible effect, but it is where the 'time zone' bugs live: #waveBar (waveDate/waveTO/waveLD) and #waveBanner (5 wave cells) are display:none!important; the inert build() versions (1688, 1727, 1785, 1832, 1894, 1926) use `hm(day,hour,min)=((day*1440+hour*60+min)%1440+1440)%1440` (minute-of-day, Zulu treated as local, no date) and 1527 has another +6 conversion. Future edits may accidentally revive them.
findings.evidence: `<script type="text/plain" id="sofWaveTimelineScriptV3_old">` etc.; CSS 360 `#waveBanner{display:none!important}`; CSS 460-465 hides #waveBar.
findings.suggested_fix: Delete all of them; keep only V8's absolute-time approach (2014-2030) as the seed for the shared TAF timeline.

findings.note: hour12:false midnight rendering on old engines
findings.title: Clocks are formatted with hour12:false and en-CA/en-US; older engines render midnight as '24:mm:ss'
findings.user_impact: On older Chrome/Edge/Safari builds (still common on managed government machines) every clock reads 24:00:00-24:59:59 during the first hour of its day, including the Zulu clock. Modern engines print 00:mm:ss (verified in Node 22).
findings.evidence: `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-CA",{timeZone:tz,hour:"2-digit",minute:"2-digit",second:"2-digit",hour12:false})`
findings.suggested_fix: Use `hourCycle:'h23'` instead of hour12:false.

findings.title: '← MODULES' return button sits on top of the 2D Map / 3D tabs
findings.user_impact: Inside the launcher the Traffic Sim header's 2D Map and 3D tab buttons are covered by the launcher's absolutely positioned '← MODULES' button. Clicking the middle of either tab returns to the launcher instead. The 3D tab is completely hidden, so the 3D view cannot be reached with a mouse. Only a 24 px sliver of '2D Map' is still clickable.
findings.evidence: main.html: '#trafficReturn{position:absolute;z-index:5;right:14px;top:7px;...}' is a sibling of the iframe. traffic.html: header with '.topTabs{margin-left:auto}' puts the tabs at the right edge. Measured in headless Chromium at 1440x900: return button x=1333..1426, y=7..36; 3D tab x=1385..1426; 2D tab x=1309..1377. document.elementFromPoint at the centre of both tabs returns #trafficReturn. Same result at 1024 and 390 px wide.
findings.suggested_fix: Move the return button into the traffic header (left of the tabs, or add padding-right of about 120px to the header). Or give the iframe a top offset and let the wrapper own its own toolbar. Do not overlay a control on a child document's header.

findings.note: rebuild adds prog with fakeAdvance=stepDt*mult while t advances by stepDt (431-440) vs live 454
findings.title: Rewind and +/-10 s rebuild the simulation at a different rate (x sim-speed) than live play
findings.user_impact: With Sim speed other than 1 (the shipped default profile uses 8, the HTML default 2), pressing Rewind, -10s or +10s puts aircraft far ahead of where they actually were at that clock time. At speed 2 they are more than 2x too far along the route, so the aircraft jump forward on a rewind and continue from the wrong place after Start.
findings.evidence: Live loop: 't+=dt*mult; ... a.prog+=speedFps(pr.speed)*dt*mult' (t and prog both scaled once). Rebuild: 't+=stepDt' but 'a.prog+=speedFps(pr.speed)*fakeAdvance' with 'fakeAdvance=stepDt*mult', so prog per sim-second is speed*mult. Measured with simSpeed=2, splits/landing disabled: at t=60 s live A1 prog=9,925 ft, rebuildPositionsAtTime(60) gives 23,391 ft. At simSpeed=1 they agree (9,939 vs 9,906 ft).
findings.suggested_fix: In rebuildPositionsAtTime advance prog by speedFps(speed)*stepDt (no mult). t is already in sim seconds. Add a test that runs N live steps and compares with rebuild at the same t for several sim speeds.

findings.note: 581 spawnPair reads #spawnRoute twice; first spawnLive's refreshAll resets the select
findings.title: '+ Pair 15 sec' puts the second aircraft on a different route than the first
findings.user_impact: If the Spawn route chosen on the right is not the route currently selected on the left, the pair splits: the first aircraft goes to the chosen route, the second to the left-panel selection. The 'pair' is not a pair.
findings.evidence: 'spawnPair' calls spawnLive twice, reading $('spawnRoute').value for each call. spawnLive() ends with refreshAll() -> refreshRouteSelects(), which rebuilds the select with 'selected' on selectedRouteId (line 469-470). Reproduced: selectedRouteId='PAT1', spawnRoute set to 'ENT2', click spawnPair -> added ['A8:ENT2:delay0','A9:PAT1:delay15'].
findings.suggested_fix: Read type/route/start/delay once into local variables before the first spawnLive and reuse them for the second. Also fix the dropdown reset (next finding).

findings.note: 573-575 Object.assign(r,fresh) replaces the selected route instead of adding a new one
findings.title: 'Build Default Pattern / Entry to Selected Pattern / Split From Selected Pattern' overwrite the selected route itself
findings.user_impact: The labels suggest these create a new entry/split for the selected pattern. They actually run Object.assign(selectedRoute, freshRoute). Clicking 'Build Entry to Selected Pattern' with the user's edited Pattern 1 selected replaces it with a 4-point entry attached to itself, so all patterns are gone and every aircraft/split that referenced it now points at an entry. There is no confirm and no undo, so a hand-tuned pattern is lost (unless it was saved as a profile).
findings.evidence: '$("buildDefaultEntry").onclick=()=>{let r=selectedRoute();...let fresh=defaultEntry(r.id,r.name,pat,r.color);Object.assign(r,fresh)...}'. Reproduced on the shipped profile: before {kind:'pattern',n:13}, after {kind:'entry',n:4,attach:'PAT1'} and patternsLeft=0. Same for buildDefaultSplit (PAT1 became a 3-point split with sourceRoute 'PAT1').
findings.suggested_fix: Make Build Entry / Build Split create a new route (new id) attached to the selected pattern. Keep 'Build Default Pattern' as 'Reset this pattern to default' with a confirm, and disable it unless kind==='pattern'. Consider a one-level undo.

findings.note: refreshRouteSelects writes the same options (selected=left panel) into spawnRoute
findings.title: Spawn-route dropdown on the right is overwritten by the left-panel selection on every refresh
findings.user_impact: The right-hand spawner and the left-hand pattern editor interfere. Selecting a route on the left to edit it silently changes 'Spawn route' on the right. After every spawn, add point, delete point and so on, the dropdown snaps back to the left selection, so the user must re-pick the route for each spawn. This breaks the intended 'left defines, right spawns' split.
findings.evidence: refreshRouteSelects: "['routeSelect','spawnRoute'].forEach(id=>$(id).innerHTML=opts)" where opts marks 'selected' for selectedRouteId, then '$('spawnRoute').value=$('spawnRoute').value||r.id' is a no-op. Reproduced: spawnRoute='ENT3', then routeSelect change to SPL2 -> spawnRoute becomes 'SPL2'. Also after spawnNow on SPL2 the dropdown returns to PAT1.
findings.suggested_fix: Rebuild the two selects separately and preserve the spawn select's current value (only fall back if that route no longer exists).

findings.note: useProfile never set false (244), so aircraft type speeds are unused
findings.title: Aircraft type does not change speed (or anything except colour)
findings.user_impact: 'Spawn type' (CT-157/CT-156/CT-102/CT-114) and the per-aircraft type dropdown suggest different performance, but every type flies the same waypoint speeds. A CT-114 labelled 230 kt in the type table flies the pattern at 100 kt like the rest.
findings.evidence: types has {spd:125|180|150|230}. makeAircraft sets useProfile:true and acProfile returns 'speed:a.useProfile!==false?(p.spd??a.speed):a.speed'. useProfile is never set false anywhere, so a.speed/types[].spd are never used. Measured acProfile() at the PAT1 start for all four types: speed=100 for each.
findings.suggested_fix: Either drop the speed field and label the type as a callsign/colour, or add a real per-type speed scale/cap (for example min(waypoint speed, type max)). Decide with the owner which one is intended.

findings.note: 394-408 forEach keeps testing later splits after one is taken, compounding odds
findings.title: Two splits from the same pattern point compound instead of using the stated odds (shipped default affected)
findings.user_impact: The Split Probability Manager says each value is the odds an aircraft takes that split at its point. When two splits share a source point, the later one re-rolls and overrides the earlier one. In the built-in profile SPL1 and SPL4 both leave PAT1 at point 6 with 50% each, and an aircraft actually takes SPL1 25%, SPL4 50%, neither 25%.
findings.evidence: 'routes.filter(x=>x.kind==='split'&&x.sourceRoute===r.id).forEach(sp=>{... if(Math.random()<+(sp.splitOdds??.5)){a.phaseRouteId=sp.id;...a.prog=0}})' keeps iterating after a split is taken and r is still the pattern. Monte Carlo (20,000 crossings of PAT1 index 5): {none:0.251, SPL1:0.251, SPL4:0.499}.
findings.suggested_fix: Group splits by trigger point, draw one random number, and pick a split (or none) from the cumulative probabilities. Normalise or warn if the sum is over 1. Add a test.

findings.note: Math.random in decisions re-rolled on every rebuild
findings.title: Rewind/seek is not repeatable: random landings and splits are re-rolled on every rebuild
findings.user_impact: After -10s, +10s or Rewind, the aircraft you were watching can land, take another split or stay in the pattern differently than before, and aircraft that had landed can reappear. History cannot be reviewed reliably.
findings.evidence: checkDecisions uses Math.random() at 392 and 401, and rebuildPositionsAtTime replays from t=0 through it. Measured: rebuildPositionsAtTime(1500) three times in a row gives three different states ('PAT1:0,PAT1:1,SPL2:1,...' vs 'PAT1:0,PAT1:0,PAT1:1,...' with a different set landed each time).
findings.suggested_fix: Use a seeded per-aircraft RNG (for example mulberry32 seeded from aircraft id + lap + split id) or pre-draw decisions when the aircraft spawns. Then replay, rewind and forward are identical.

findings.note: rebuild from t=0 each frame (agent timed 302 ms at 600 s)
findings.title: Rewind and +/-10 s replay the whole run from t=0 every time (every frame while rewinding)
findings.user_impact: Cost grows with elapsed sim time. Rewinding after about 10 minutes of sim time drops to a few frames per second, and after 30 minutes to under 1 fps. A single +10s at t=1800 s freezes the tab for about 1.7 s.
findings.evidence: step() calls rebuildPositionsAtTime(t) each animation frame when reversePlay is on, and that function re-simulates from 0 in 0.5 s steps, recomputing roundedPoints via navSegs/routeLen/posOnRoute for every aircraft. Measured on the shipped profile: rebuild to 120 s = 30 ms, 600 s = 302 ms, 1800 s = 1,727 ms, 3600 s = 4,256 ms.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep periodic snapshots (for example every 10 s of sim time) of aircraft state and rewind from the nearest snapshot. Cache navSegs()/routeLen() per route and invalidate on edit.

findings.title: Route cross-references are numeric indices and unlinked copies, so inserting/deleting/dragging a point silently retargets or detaches them
findings.user_impact: Adding or deleting a point on a pattern shifts every entry mergeIndex and split sourceIndex/mergeIndex, so they now point at a different waypoint. Dragging a pattern point does not move the entry/split endpoints that were built from it. The aircraft then leaves the pattern at one place and pops up at another.
findings.evidence: addPoint: 'r.points.splice(i+1,0,np)' with no remap of other routes' indices. Reproduced: SPL1.sourceIndex=5 was 'New Point' (-10974,12100) which equals SPL1's first point. After '+ Point After Selected' at index 2 the same sourceIndex points to 'Crosswind' (-28411,1450) while SPL1's first point is still at (-10974,12100). Split/entry end points are copies (Object.assign in the snap buttons at 503 and 524-525) and the drag handler at 585 only edits the selected route.
findings.suggested_fix: Store cross-references by stable point ids, or remap indices on insert/delete. Optionally keep split-start and merge points slaved to the pattern vertex they reference.

findings.title: Aircraft visibly teleport when leaving a pattern for a split and when merging (up to about 1,900 ft)
findings.user_impact: Aircraft jump sideways at split start and at entry/split merges, with a heading discontinuity, and the trail draws a straight jump line. This can also create momentary false conflicts. It is worst at splits on a rounded corner.
findings.evidence: The split trigger uses pointProg() (start of the rounded corner) but the split route starts at the raw vertex (a.prog=0). The merge uses closestProg(target, mergeVertex) while the entry ended at the vertex. Measured on the shipped profile: SPL2 start jump 1,944 ft; ENT3 merge 892 ft; SPL3 merge 678 ft; SPL2 merge 197 ft; ENT1 91 ft.
findings.suggested_fix: Trigger the split when the aircraft reaches the point on the rounded path nearest the vertex, and start the split at that same position (or build split/entry routes with the rounded corner tangent points). Blend or align heading on merge.

findings.note: rounded corners are quadratic Beziers; flown radius smaller than the stated R (flight math, Dad to decide)
findings.title: 'Fly rounded turns' flies a tighter turn than the radius/bank the UI shows
findings.user_impact: The turn radius calculated from KT/G and shown by 'Show turn data' is the target, not the radius flown. A 90 degree corner is flown at about 0.71 R (about 2.6 G at a 2 G waypoint) and a 135 degree corner at about 0.39 R (about 4.6 G). A pattern designed at 2 G therefore silently needs much more G, and short legs (0.45 leg-length cap at line 205) reduce the radius further with no warning.
findings.evidence: Corners are a quadratic Bezier 'bez(a,{...cur},c,u)' between tangent points at distance d=r*tan(turn/2). That gives apex radius R*cos(turn/2), not R. Measured with 120 kt, 2 G (stated R=736 ft): 45 deg -> min flown radius 682 ft (0.93), 90 deg -> 523 ft (0.71, 2.64 G), 135 deg -> 285 ft (0.39, 4.59 G).
findings.suggested_fix: Per CLAUDE.md, first add a test pinning the current geometry. Then replace the Bezier with a true circular arc (tangent-arc fillet) of radius R, or at least display the effective radius/G. Warn when a leg is too short for the requested radius.

findings.title: Satellite overlay can request tens or hundreds of thousands of tiles and never evicts them
findings.user_impact: The built-in profile enables the overlay, so opening the module fires about 480 ArcGIS tile requests. The tile zoom is independent of map zoom: at Satellite tile zoom 18 one redraw creates about 29,000 Image objects, and after zooming the map out it creates about 385,000 (about 3 s per redraw). The tab freezes, memory grows and the tile server may throttle or block the user. Every arriving tile also triggers a full draw(), and failed tiles are cached as failed forever (no retry when the network returns).
findings.evidence: drawSatellite loops 'for(tx=minTileX..maxTileX) for(ty=minTileY..maxTileY){let img=getTile(z,tx,ty)...}' with no cap. getTile: 'img.onload=()=>draw()', 'img.onerror=()=>{img.failed=true}', tileCache is a Map that only grows. Measured: 480 requests at load; satZoom=18 -> 28,860 new tiles in one draw (151 ms); satZoom=18 + map zoom 0.25 -> 385,540 tiles (2,992 ms).
findings.suggested_fix: Derive the tile zoom from the map zoom, cap tiles per frame (for example 64), use an LRU cache, coalesce redraws with requestAnimationFrame, and allow retry of failed tiles. Show a 'tiles unavailable' hint when they fail.

findings.title: Satellite 'Moose Jaw default align' un-aligns the built-in profile; runway geometry is defined three different ways
findings.user_impact: The built-in pattern only lines up with the imagery at Overlay scale trim 1.20 (the slider maximum). The button labelled 'Moose Jaw default align' resets the trim to 1.0, so pressing it shifts the imagery about 17% relative to the built-in routes. The tile scale formula itself is correct, so the 1.2 fudge suggests the profile's world coordinates are not true feet. The code also holds conflicting runway definitions, so 'Build Default Pattern' and '+ Pattern' do not match the shipped pattern or the imagery.
findings.evidence: alignMooseJaw: "$('satZoom').value=15;$('satScale').value=1;..." vs EMBEDDED_DEFAULT_PROFILE settings "satScale":"1.2". defaultPattern() uses 'hdg=290,len=8000' centred on the ARP (0,0). Shipped PAT1 runway (points 1-2) measures 298.4 deg / 8,150 ft with midpoint (-481, 1257), 1.3 kft from the ARP. Real CYMJ main runways are about 10,000 ft (verify in the CFS). ArcGIS was blocked in the audit sandbox, so the imagery alignment could not be viewed.
findings.suggested_fix: Pick one authoritative CYMJ runway definition (ends in lat/lon converted to feet), draw it on the map, generate default patterns from it, and set the default trim to 1.0 after fixing the coordinates. Remove or repurpose the 1.2 trim.

findings.title: 3D view is not a consistent camera: inverted depth cue, unequal lateral/vertical scales, tiny default framing
findings.user_impact: Objects nearer the top of the screen are drawn larger (inverse perspective) and are drawn last, so overlap order is wrong. Lateral distance is scaled /16 but altitude /10, so altitude (vertical separation) looks about 1.6x more than lateral distance. At the default camera the whole shipped pattern (about 50,000 ft wide) is about 100 px wide, and the 'High Lookdown' and 'Low Chase' presets don't frame it either. 2D panning also moves the 3D camera (viewCenter is added at line 322). The 3D view is not a reliable picture of lateral or vertical spacing.
findings.evidence: project3D: 'forward=ry*cp+dz*sp+26000' (south = farther) but 'sy=H*0.58-vertical*scale/10' where vertical=dz*cp-ry*sp puts larger ry lower on screen; 'sx=W/2+rx*scale/16'; scale=(zoom*850)/max(2200,forward). Measured at the default camera: 3000 ft east -> 4 px, 3000 ft north -> 4 px up (near side is up), 3000 ft of altitude -> 6 px.
findings.suggested_fix: Use a real look-at camera (view matrix + perspective divide, same units on all axes) and frame the pattern automatically (fit-to-routes). Decide whether 3D shares the 2D pan.

findings.title: Selected Route Points: ALT / KT / G inputs are pushed outside the panel
findings.user_impact: The waypoint table is the main way to define a pattern's altitude, speed and G, but only the label, X and Y fields fit. ALT, KT and G sit off the right edge of the 389 px left column and need horizontal scrolling of the whole panel. The columns have no headers, so it is unclear which field is which.
findings.evidence: CSS '.pointrow{display:grid;grid-template-columns:38px 90px 1fr 1fr 70px 62px 52px;...}' with plain <input> items (no min-width:0/width:100%, unlike .acrow at line 25). Measured: .left clientWidth 389 vs scrollWidth 699; X input 161..328, Y 333..500, ALT 505..575, KT 580..642, G 647..699 (card right edge is 366).
findings.suggested_fix: Add 'min-width:0;width:100%' to '.pointrow input', add a header row (Label / X / Y / Alt / KT / G), and consider a wider or collapsible editor panel.

findings.title: Route removal leaves dangling references and ids are reused, so aircraft can silently join a different, newer route
findings.user_impact: Deleting a route does not touch the aircraft, entries or splits that reference it. Aircraft fall back to the first route without notice and entries/splits silently deactivate their aircraft at the end ('Done'). Because newId() reuses the smallest free number, creating a new pattern later re-attaches those aircraft and entries to it. Changing 'Route type' of a pattern to entry/split has the same problem.
findings.evidence: deleteRoute: 'routes=routes.filter(r=>r.id!==selectedRouteId)' only. currentAcRoute: 'routeById(a.phaseRouteId)||routes[0]'. Reproduced: added PAT2, spawned A8 on it, deleted PAT2 -> A8 flies PAT1 and its row shows PAT1; added a new pattern (id PAT2 again) -> A8 now flies the new 'Pattern 2'. handleRouteEnd: 'if(target&&target.kind==='pattern'){...} a.active=false'.
findings.suggested_fix: Use never-reused unique ids. On delete, warn and list dependents, then re-home or remove them (or block deletion). Validate attachTo/sourceRoute after kind changes.

findings.note: saveStore unguarded; name field not updated on load
findings.title: Profile Save/Load: name field does not follow Load, silent overwrite, unhandled storage errors, and no way back to the built-in default
findings.user_impact: After Load, 'Profile name' still shows the old text (default 'Moose Jaw Dynamic'), so the next Save silently overwrites a different saved profile (no overwrite confirm; Delete also has no confirm). A full localStorage or blocked storage throws an uncaught error with no message and the user thinks it saved. The built-in default profile is not in 'Saved profiles', so after loading another profile the only way back is reloading the page. Profiles are whole-simulation snapshots (routes + aircraft + settings); a single pattern cannot be saved or reused on its own, and Load replaces the built-in pattern rather than adding to it.
findings.evidence: loadProfile: 'if(s[n])applyProfile(s[n])' (does not set $('profileName')). saveStore: 'function saveStore(s){localStorage.setItem(STORE,JSON.stringify(s))}' with no try/catch. Reproduced: saved 'Alt', typed 'Moose Jaw Dynamic', Load, Save -> keys ['Alt','Moose Jaw Dynamic']. With setItem forced to throw, the click raises 'PAGEERR quota'.
findings.suggested_fix: Set profileName on load, confirm overwrite/delete, wrap storage in try/catch with a visible message. List the built-in profile (read-only) in the dropdown. Add a separate pattern library: built-in patterns as data plus user patterns saved individually under one localStorage key.

findings.note: ids/colours into innerHTML unescaped on import
findings.title: Import JSON injects unescaped ids/colours/types into innerHTML (script runs) and has no validation
findings.user_impact: Opening a shared/edited profile JSON can run script in the app's origin (the module is a srcdoc iframe of the launcher). Hand-edited or older files with missing fields can also leave the UI half-loaded. The owner said patterns are local-only with no sharing, so the Export/Import buttons may be unwanted anyway.
findings.evidence: Route and aircraft ids, colours and types are interpolated raw ('
findings.suggested_fix: Escape every interpolated value (or build DOM nodes with textContent), validate the schema (ids match /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$/, colours match #hex, numbers finite, unknown types rejected), and apply into a copy before swapping state. Remove Export/Import if there is to be no sharing.

findings.note: fixed 390+430 px columns, mouse only (desktop is the target)
findings.title: Page layout is fixed-width and mouse-only, so it is unusable on tablets/phones and small windows
findings.user_impact: The three columns are fixed at 390px + map + 430px with body overflow hidden. At 1024 px wide the map is only 204 px wide, and at 390 px wide it is 0 px, with no way to scroll. Point dragging, panning and wheel zoom use mouse events only, so nothing on the map works by touch. This conflicts with the 'usable by anyone, anywhere' rule.
findings.evidence: CSS 'main{...grid-template-columns:390px 1fr 430px}' and 'body{...overflow:hidden}'; handlers are canvas.onmousedown/onmousemove/onmouseup/onwheel. Measured stage widths: 620 px at 1440, 204 px at 1024, 0 px at 390.
findings.suggested_fix: Collapse to tabs/drawers below about 1100 px, let the panels scroll, and switch to pointer events with touch support (drag, pan, pinch).

findings.note: followSelect populated but never read (2 occurrences)
findings.title: Follow-aircraft dropdown in the map toolbar does nothing
findings.user_impact: The toolbar has an aircraft dropdown (A1, A2, ...) that looks like a 'follow' camera. Changing it has no effect. It also overlaps/crowds the hint pill on narrow widths.
findings.evidence: '<select id="followSelect">' is only populated at line 471 ('$('followSelect').innerHTML=aircraft.map(...)'); the id is never read anywhere else in the file.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove it, or implement follow (center viewCenter on the selected aircraft).

findings.note: Closed loop checkbox overridden by kind
findings.title: 'Closed loop' checkbox has no effect
findings.user_impact: Ticking or unticking 'Closed loop' is immediately undone. Patterns are always closed and entries/splits always open.
findings.evidence: updateSelectedRouteFromForm: 'r.closed=$('routeClosed').checked; if(r.kind==='pattern')r.closed=true; if(r.kind!=='pattern')r.closed=false;' then refreshAll() re-syncs the checkbox. Verified: ticking it on ENT1 leaves closed=false and the box unticked.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the checkbox (or show it disabled with a note).

findings.note: developer changelog in Notes; test state in default profile
findings.title: Notes box starts with a developer changelog and the built-in profile carries leftover test state
findings.user_impact: Notes textarea starts with a developer changelog line ('V37: Rewind now plays...'), replaced at startup by other text. The built-in default profile also carries leftover test state: simSpeed 8, conflict limits 200/200 ft and caution 500/500 (panel defaults are 1500/500 and 2500/1000), and aircraft delays such as 12.0000000000005, 136.6792, 591.8656, 856.0984, 884.1256 and 902.088 s (four of seven aircraft do not appear for the first 10+ sim minutes). A first-time user sees one aircraft and a very small conflict bubble.
findings.evidence: Line 131 textarea text and EMBEDDED_DEFAULT_PROFILE aircraft 'delay' values and settings {"simSpeed":"8","latSep":"200","vertSep":"200","cautionLatSep":"500","cautionVertSep":"500"}.
findings.suggested_fix: Clean the built-in profile: tidy delays (0/15/30/45 s), sim speed 1-2, agreed conflict limits, and a meaningful note. Keep it as a JSON data file with a version.

findings.title: Spawner inputs use inconsistent conventions (0-based start point; delay is relative in the spawner but absolute in the aircraft list)
findings.user_impact: 'Spawn start point' 0 means the first waypoint but everywhere else points are numbered from 1 (map labels, point table, route setup), so typing 1 starts at waypoint 2. The spawner's 'Delay from now sec' is stored as an absolute time (t+delay); the Aircraft list then shows that absolute value in an unlabelled box, so a 15 s delay spawned at 5 min reads 315. Aircraft rows have no column labels.
findings.evidence: '<input id="spawnStart" ... value="0" min="0">'; makeAircraft uses pointProg(route,start). Verified: start=1 gives prog 8,149.8 ft = 'Departure End' (waypoint 2). spawnLive: 'a.delay=t+(...delayFromNow...)'; refreshAircraftRows shows 'Math.round(a.delay)'.
findings.suggested_fix: Use 1-based numbers in the spawner (or show the label next to it), show 'starts at mm:ss' with a header row in the aircraft list.

findings.title: Coincident waypoint labels draw on top of each other; 'Show turn data' skips the first pattern vertex
findings.user_impact: Entries and splits are built from pattern vertices, so several routes' labels and ft/kt/G readouts are printed at the same screen position (up to six at the threshold) and become unreadable. 'Show turn data' never prints the radius/bank at waypoint 1 of a closed pattern although that corner is rounded.
findings.evidence: drawRoute draws '${r.name} ${i+1} ${pt.label}' for every visible route's points. Measured groups of coincident points on the shipped profile: [PAT1#1,ENT2#5,SPL1#7,ENT4#1,ENT4#5,SPL4#3], [PAT1#6,SPL1#1,SPL4#1], plus five more pairs. Turn data condition: 'i>0&&(r.closed||i<r.points.length-1)'.
findings.suggested_fix: Draw labels only for the selected route (or offset/merge duplicates), and change the condition to '(r.closed||(i>0&&i<r.points.length-1))'.

findings.title: Keyboard editing of the waypoint table loses focus after every field
findings.user_impact: Editing X then pressing Tab drops focus to the page body, so the user must click each field. Typing values through the table with the keyboard is not possible.
findings.evidence: Each input's onchange calls refreshPointRows(), which does 'el.innerHTML=""' and rebuilds all rows. Verified in Chromium: after fill('-4000') + Tab in X, document.activeElement is BODY.
findings.suggested_fix: Update the underlying point and only redraw the map, or restore focus to the next input after re-render.

findings.note: left/right layout vs Patrick's model (left defines patterns, right spawns); design for the traffic spec
findings.title: Left column buries the pattern editor; the pattern-related tools are split across both sides
findings.user_impact: The intended 'left defines patterns / right spawns aircraft' is not what the page does. The left column starts with transport, conflict limits, 3D camera and satellite cards before Route Manager. On a 900 px tall screen Route Manager starts about 1,386 px down and Selected Route Points about 2,303 px down. On the right, pattern-definition items (Split Probability Manager, Leg Distances) sit between the spawner and Save/Load, and Save/Load is about 2,667 px down under a 1,237 px Leg Distances table. The split odds can be edited in two places.
findings.evidence: Measured card offsets: left [Simulation Controls 12, Conflict 419, 3D Camera 707, Satellite 1034, Route Manager 1386, Selected Route Setup 2151, Selected Route Points 2303]; right [Spawner 12, Aircraft 249, Readout 829, Conflict Monitor 1111, Split Probability 1184, Leg Distances 1420 (h 1237), Save/Load 2667, Notes 2856].
findings.suggested_fix: Left: Route Manager + Selected Route (points/logic/split odds/leg distances) + pattern save/load. Right: spawner, aircraft, readout, conflict monitor. Move sim transport to the map toolbar and put conflict limits/3D/satellite in a collapsible 'View' panel.

findings.title: 3D title box is drawn under the map toolbar
findings.user_impact: In the 3D view the canvas-drawn '3D Perspective View' box sits exactly where the HTML toolbar (clock, status, follow dropdown) is, so the title is hidden and the text overlaps the pills.
findings.evidence: Canvas: 'ctx.roundRect(10,10,245,72,10)' plus fillText at (22,32). DOM: '.toolbar{position:absolute;z-index:4;top:10px;left:10px;...}'. Screenshot shows the title cut by the '00:00 / Running / A1' pills.
findings.suggested_fix: Move the canvas caption below the toolbar (y>=54) or delete it since the footer already describes the controls.

findings.title: Aircraft progress is stored as arc length, so any route edit or the 'Fly rounded turns' toggle teleports all aircraft
findings.user_impact: Dragging a point, editing a coordinate, changing turn radius or toggling 'Fly rounded turns' while the sim is running changes route length, and every aircraft jumps to the new point at the same distance from the start.
findings.evidence: a.prog is in feet along navSegs(route). PAT1 length is 156,924 ft with rounding and 162,728 ft without, so toggling the checkbox moves an aircraft near the end of the lap by about 5,800 ft.
findings.suggested_fix: Store progress as (segment index, fraction) or re-project the aircraft onto the edited route (closestProg) after edits, or pause the sim while dragging.

findings.title: '+ Entry' / '+ Split' assume the 6-point default pattern and always attach to the first pattern
findings.user_impact: The generated entry merges at pattern point index 5 and the split starts at index 3, which are 'Final Entry' and 'Crosswind' only in the 6-point generator pattern. On the shipped 13-point pattern they land on unnamed 'New Point' waypoints. '+ Entry'/'+ Split' attach to the first pattern even when another pattern is selected.
findings.evidence: defaultEntry: 'mi=Math.min(5,...)'; defaultSplit: 'si=Math.min(3,...)'; addEntry: "pat=routes.find(r=>r.kind==='pattern')?.id".
findings.suggested_fix: Attach to the selected pattern and choose merge/split points by label or by nearest vertex; or let the user pick them in the dialog.

findings.title: Sim clock shows mm:ss only and wraps after one hour; whole right panel is rebuilt every frame
findings.user_impact: At 8x speed one hour of sim time is about 7.5 minutes, after which the clock restarts at 00:00. updatePanels() rewrites three innerHTML blocks (readout, conflicts, the static Leg Distances table) 60 times per second, even while paused, so text in those cards cannot be selected or copied.
findings.evidence: '$('clock').textContent=new Date(t*1000).toISOString().substr(14,5)' gives '02:05' for t=3725 (verified). step() always ends with 'draw();updatePanels();requestAnimationFrame(step)'.
findings.suggested_fix: Format as h:mm:ss, update only changed cells, and refresh Leg Distances on edit only.

findings.title: Esri/ArcGIS imagery is used without attribution
findings.user_impact: The satellite tiles from server.arcgisonline.com are drawn with no credit line. Esri's terms for World_Imagery require attribution (Esri, Maxar, Earthstar Geographics and the GIS User Community).
findings.evidence: tileUrl points at 'https://server.arcgisonline.com/ArcGIS/rest/services/World_Imagery/MapServer/tile/...' and no attribution text is drawn in drawSatellite or the footer.
findings.suggested_fix: Draw a small attribution string on the map whenever the overlay is on.

findings.note: init builds routes then discards them
findings.title: init() builds two patterns and four aircraft that are discarded at startup
findings.user_impact: Every page load builds the old two-pattern demo (PAT1/PAT2, ENT1/ENT2, SPL1, A1-A4), then applyProfile(EMBEDDED_DEFAULT_PROFILE) replaces it. Only one built-in pattern (PAT1 plus 4 entries and 4 splits) exists, not the 'few default patterns' the owner wants. reset() (239-241) and resetAircraftToStarts() (411-424) duplicate each other and disagree about resetting a.landed.
findings.evidence: 'init(){routes=[defaultPattern('PAT1',...),defaultPattern('PAT2',...,14000,...)];...refreshAll();reset()}' followed at 617 by 'applyProfile(EMBEDDED_DEFAULT_PROFILE)' whose routes are PAT1, ENT1-4, SPL1-4.
findings.suggested_fix: Load the built-in patterns from a data file (one entry per pattern, for example overhead, straight-in, VFR rectangle) and drop init()'s demo build. Share one reset function.

findings.note: 1236 arms auto aircraft; 1525 lead gate returns false until #1 turns, so aircraft planned before #1 wait (flight math)
findings.title: Auto timing holds every aircraft that should turn before #1 until #1 has started, so the planned sequence is not flown
findings.user_impact: With Turn trigger = 'Auto timing', the outside aircraft that is supposed to start first (for example #2 in 4312 turning right, or #4/#3 turning left) does not turn at t=0. It waits until #1 begins turning, so #1 and the 'first' aircraft (and in left turns #1, #3 and #4 together) roll in at the same instant. The trainee sees a wrong turn sequence and the wrong rollout geometry, while the status pill claims 'Timing: AUTO'.
findings.evidence: setupTurnStartsFor arms every non-lead aircraft for auto: `a.cueArmed=(trigger!=='time' && (man==='delayed90away'||man==='delayed45away') && a.id!==1);`. cueSatisfied then applies the legacy lead gate to auto as well: `const lead=list.find(x=>x.id===1); if(!lead || !lead.done && lead.turnAccum<=0) return false;` before it reaches `return t>=a.turnStart`. Ran the real code headless (stubbed DOM): weighted, right, auto: planned turnStart 1:25.4 2:0.0 3:50.8 4:76.1 but first-active times were 1:25.45 2:25.45 3:50.85 4:76.2. weighted, left, auto: planned 4:0.0 3:25.4 1:50.8 but actual 4:50.85 3:50.85 1:50.85. offsetBox, left, auto: planned #2 at 0.0, actual 25.45. Time-delay mode is correct (2:0.05 1:16.05 3:32.05 4:48.1).
findings.suggested_fix: In cueSatisfied only apply the lead gate to the legacy triggers (leadHeading/range/bearing), or do not set cueArmed for trigger==='auto' so it falls through to `t>=a.turnStart`. Add a test that pins planned vs actual start times for both turn directions and both line-abreast presets before touching it.

findings.note: delayStep=spacing*theta(rad)/v gives 25.4 s vs s/v 16.2 s that the time-mode harness shows gives a clean line; flight math, needs Dad
findings.title: Auto timing delay step (spacing x turn angle / speed) is 1.57x too long for a 90 degree delayed turn and rolls out wide and staggered
findings.user_impact: Even once the sequencing bug is fixed, 'Auto timing / equal track' at the defaults (6000 ft, 220 kt, 90 deg) sets a 25.4 s step instead of the 16.2 s that actually produces 6000 ft line abreast. Aircraft would roll out about 9,400 ft apart with about 3,400 ft fore/aft stagger while the tool claims to have solved for the desired spacing.
findings.evidence: `const delayStep=Math.max(0, (Math.abs(spacing) * Math.abs(theta)) / v);` (theta in radians, so 90 deg gives 1.571*s/v = 25.38 s). Comment says 'delay step ~ lateral spacing x turn angle / groundspeed' but no derivation or test. Ran the sim in time mode (weighted, right, delayed 90, spacing 6000): base 16.16 s (= s/v) gives rollout relative to lead (fwd,left) #2 (15,-6015) #3 (3,5997) #4 (6,11994), i.e. perfect line abreast at 6000 ft; base 25.38 s (the auto value) gives #2 (3431,-9431) #3 (-3431,9431) #4 (-6844,18844). The old optimiser that scored the rollout (simulateAutoTimingCandidate, line 1333) is dead code, so nothing checks the closed form. NOTE: verify intent with the owner ('equal track' may mean something else) but the numbers disagree with the tool's own Desired spacing.
findings.suggested_fix: Do not change flight math without a pinning test (project rule): first write a test that records the current 25.38 s / rollout numbers, then decide with the owner whether the intended rule is s/v (90 deg) or another closed form, and re-derive for 45 deg. Alternatively re-enable the simulate-and-score search that already exists.

findings.note: same as turnsim-b#18; save/restoreAutoTimingState defined once, never called
findings.title: Switching to Auto timing overwrites the user's Base delay input and it is never restored
findings.user_impact: After trying Auto, going back to 'Time delay' leaves Base delay at 25.38 instead of the 16 s the user had typed, and that value also goes into 'Save as default'. Users will think the manual timing is wrong.
findings.evidence: `$('baseDelay').value=delayStep.toFixed(2);` runs on every play in auto mode. saveAutoTimingState/restoreAutoTimingState (1323-1332) exist to undo this but are never called (grep finds only their definitions). Harness: baseDelay 16 -> 25.38 after an auto run.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the auto step in its own variable/readout instead of writing into #baseDelay, or restore the manual value when the trigger is changed away from auto.

findings.note: 1104 side>0 is target on LEFT (hdg+90 in y-up) but mapped to right turn; toward/away inverted
findings.title: Per-aircraft 'Toward cue aircraft' / 'Away from cue aircraft' turn logic does the opposite of its label
findings.user_impact: Choosing 'Toward cue aircraft' for a wingman makes it turn away from the cue aircraft, and 'Away from' turns it toward. Any 4-ship visual-turn scenario that uses these options shows the wrong turn direction.
findings.evidence: World is y-up (worldToScreen uses `sim.height/2-(y+pan.y)*zoom`), heading is a CCW math angle, and a positive turnDir increases heading, i.e. turns LEFT. sideOfAircraftFrom() returns +1 when the target is on the aircraft's LEFT (vector at hdg+90deg). turnDirFromLogic then does `const toward=side>0 ? -1 : 1; // target right -> right turn, target left -> left turn` : the comment assumes side>0 means right. Harness: #2 (y=+6000, flying east) with lead on its right: turnLogic 'toward' returned +1 (left turn, away), 'away' returned -1 (right turn, toward).
findings.suggested_fix: Swap to `const toward=side>0 ? 1 : -1;` and pin with a test of a left/right target for both options. Same root cause as the 'right' vector naming problem (see the mirrored-label finding).

findings.note: 907-913 wide adds along one fixed vector, so aircraft on the other side of lead get tighter
findings.title: 'Wide' / 'Tight' position error is applied in a fixed direction, so it is inverted for every aircraft on the negative-lateral side of lead
findings.user_impact: For #3 and #4 in 4312, and #2/#3/#4 in Offset Box and Two-ship, entering 'Wide 1000 ft' moves the aircraft 1000 ft CLOSER to lead and 'Tight' moves it away. The position-error training scenarios (and the debrief error labels built from them) are backwards for most wingmen.
findings.evidence: `const lat=(a.latDir==='wide'?1:a.latDir==='tight'?-1:0)*(+a.latMag||0);` then applyErrors adds `right.x*a.tight` along the fixed +90deg vector regardless of which side of lead the aircraft sits. Harness, weighted, all wingmen 'Wide 1000': lateral distance from lead #2 6000->7000 (wider) but #3 6000->5000 and #4 12000->11000 (tighter). Offset box: #2 nominal -7000 -> -6000 (tighter). The same `wide=+1` convention is copied for the KML error panel at line 2145.
findings.suggested_fix: Compute the outward direction per aircraft as sign of its nominal lateral offset from lead (wide = away from lead, tight = toward lead); use it in both the Turn Sim and the KML error panel and add a per-preset test.

findings.title: 'Clock tolerance deg' input is never read
findings.user_impact: Changing Clock tolerance (deg) has no effect; the cue always uses 4 degrees.
findings.evidence: `const tol=+$('clockCueTol')||4;` unary plus on the element (not `.value`) gives NaN, so `||4` always wins. `clockCueTol` appears nowhere else (grep: lines 585 and 1498 only).
findings.suggested_fix: Use `+($('clockCueTol')?.value)||4`.

findings.note: clockCueSequence referenced once; autoClockTargetId path bypasses selectors per 1520; not run
findings.title: Clock-cue target selectors ('Clock cue aircraft', per-aircraft 'Clock target', 'Clock cue sequence: Manual targets', per-aircraft 'Turn logic') do nothing in clock mode
findings.user_impact: Users can pick a different cue aircraft, a per-aircraft cue target, 'Manual targets', or a per-aircraft turn direction rule and nothing changes: the outside-in cascade always decides who waits on whom, and every aircraft turns in the top-level direction. The status line also always prints the global clock position even when an aircraft has its own clockPos override.
findings.evidence: clockMode forces `dir=clockSelectedDir` and `cueTarget=cascadeOrder[idx-1]`, stored in a.autoClockTargetId; cueSatisfied uses `a.autoClockTargetId ? list.find(...) : cueTargetForAircraft(a,list)` and unarmed aircraft return before reaching it, so cueTargetForAircraft/clockCueAircraft/a.clockTarget are never used for triggering (the global select only feeds toward/away). `clockCueSequence` occurs once in the whole file (its <select>, line 586). Harness: cascade printed identical '1<-2 2<-start 3<-1 4<-3' regardless of selectors. updateClockCueStatus (1277) prints the global `clockCuePos` text for every aircraft.
findings.suggested_fix: Either implement 'manual' (use a.clockTarget/global cue aircraft when sequence==='manual') or remove the three selectors; honour per-aircraft turnLogic or hide it while trigger=clock; show each aircraft's own clockPos in the status line.

findings.title: 'Shackle rollback delay' input does nothing and the promised hold before the reverse turn never happens
findings.user_impact: Changing 'Shackle rollback delay' has no effect. The shackle reverses immediately after 45 degrees even though the maneuver note says 'hold for the rollback delay'.
findings.evidence: `shackleDelay` is only listed in the change-listener array (2017) and SETTING_IDS (2047), never read. moveAircraftList tests `t < (a.shackleHoldUntil||0)` (1585) but shackleHoldUntil is assigned nowhere, so the hold branch is dead. Note text at 2038: 'Shackle: aircraft turn 45 deg into each other, hold for the rollback delay, then reverse back to original heading.'
findings.suggested_fix: Set `a.shackleHoldUntil=t+ +$('shackleDelay').value` when phase 0 completes (1594-1597), or remove the input and the note text.

findings.note: 1238 overwrites lead shackle dir with selectedDir; wingmen get dir=side (left=+1=left turn), i.e. away
findings.title: Shackle turn directions do not match the on-screen description ('into each other'); lead's shackle direction is overwritten
findings.user_impact: In a two-ship shackle both aircraft end up turning the same way (set by the top Direction dropdown) rather than toward each other; in a 4-ship, wingmen turn away from lead. The reversal then hides the problem in a straight-line replay but the geometry shown is not what the note describes.
findings.evidence: Two-ship branch computes `dir = (a.id===1) ? -side : side;` but line 1238 `if(a.id===1) dir=selectedDir; else dir=turnDirFromLogic(a,list,dir);` immediately overwrites lead's value. Harness twoShip shackle45 right: planned dirs 1:-1 2:-1 (both right, separation stays 6000 ft for the whole run, never changes). 4-ship weighted right: dirs 1:-1 2:+1 3:-1 4:-1 (wingmen use `dir=side`, side>0 is the LEFT of lead, so #2 turns left = away). Owner should confirm whether 'into each other' or 'away' is intended (a real shackle changes sides).
findings.suggested_fix: Decide the intended direction, move the lead override inside the non-shackle branch, and fix either the code or the note; add a test on separation vs time for two-ship.

findings.note: harness-only (clock cue cascade stall in offset box); not reproduced by me
findings.title: Offset Box with Clock-cue trigger: #3 and #4 never turn at the default 5:30 cue
findings.user_impact: Selecting Offset Box + 'Clock position cue' (default 5:30) with Delayed 90/45 leaves #3 and #4 flying straight for the whole run (the sim just ends at the duration with two aircraft off the screen). No message explains why.
findings.evidence: The cascade makes #3 wait on #2 and #4 on #3, each to be at 5:30. An aft aircraft never sees the aircraft ahead of it at 5:30. Harness: offsetBox right and left with clockCuePos 5.5: cascade '1<-start 2<-1 3<-2 4<-3'; only #1/#2 ever become active, at t=150 'all done false', #3/#4 ended 50,000+ ft away. Similar silent stall in 4312 for cue 3 or 12 o'clock (three aircraft never turn).
findings.suggested_fix: Give aft elements a sensible default cue (or fall back to the time plan when the cue cannot be reached), and show a 'cue not reached' warning in the clock status pills when an aircraft is still waiting at the end of the run.

findings.note: chosenTarget/chosenName assigned once and never read (dead solver); #4 geometry numbers harness-only
findings.title: Offset Box #4 timing: default 'LATE' puts #4 about 21,000 ft aft and on the wrong side for left turns; UI says #4 'solves by ground track' but the solver is dead
findings.user_impact: Offset Box, delayed 90 left, #4 LATE (the default) rolls out at about 21,000 ft behind lead and across to the other side instead of 3,000 ft outside #2 (right turn LATE works; left turn needs EARLY). The maneuver note and the box note promise that #4 'solves by ground track to the inner or outer aft side', which the code does not do.
findings.evidence: #4's delay is just `threeDelay +/- base` (1070-1075). The ground-track target computation above it (outerTarget, innerTarget, chosenTarget, chosenName, fourStartsOutside, frontSep, frontSecondDelay) is computed and never used. Harness (offsetBox, base 16, spacing 6000, boxAft 8000): right/LATE #4 (fwd -6988, left 8988) good; left/LATE #4 (-21047, -3047) bad; left/EARLY #4 (-9146, 8854) good; right/EARLY (4913, -2913) bad.
findings.suggested_fix: Either use the computed side targets to pick early/late automatically per direction (as the dead comment at 1045-1048 describes) or default the toggle by direction and correct the notes.
