findings.note: 953 delta=dir*goal flips forward term for right turns; correct only for left
findings.title: simulateDelayedTurnFinalPos predicts the wrong end point for right turns (mirrored through the start point)
findings.user_impact: No visible effect today because the error cancels between aircraft with the same heading in computeOffsetBoxPlan, but any new use of this predictor for a right turn gives a wrong position.
findings.evidence: `const delta = selectedDir*goal;` then `fwd*R*Math.sin(delta) + right*R*(1-Math.cos(delta))`. For selectedDir=-1 the forward term goes negative and the lateral term keeps its sign, i.e. the turn vector is negated. Harness: lead hook right, delay 10 s: actual end (6178,-2496), predicted (1239,2474); left turn: actual (6178,2496), predicted (6187,2474) which is correct. The unit conversions (R=2474 ft at 220 kt / 2 G, bank 60 deg, 8.6 deg/s) all check out.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `R*Math.sin(Math.abs(delta))` for the forward term and `Math.sign(delta)*R*(1-Math.cos(delta))` for the lateral term, with a test for both directions.

findings.note: turnsim-b#17 (confirmed code fact; label question for Dad)
findings.title: Formation preset labels are the mirror image of what is drawn, and the variable called 'right' is actually the pilot's left
findings.user_impact: '4312' draws #2 on the left wing of lead (2 | 1 | 3 | 4 reading left to right facing the direction of flight), '2134' draws 4 | 3 | 1 | 2, and 'Two-ship: 2 | 1' draws #2 on the right; Offset Box puts #2 on the right. An instructor who reads the digits left to right will see the mirror image, and the presets disagree with the offset box preset. The internal logic is consistent with itself (all the turn ordering follows the drawn geometry), which is why the mismatch has survived.
findings.evidence: The world is y-up, so `right={x:Math.cos(h+Math.PI/2),y:Math.sin(h+Math.PI/2)}` (lines 799, 829, 912, 932, 949, 960, 1122, 1412) is the LEFT-hand vector. weighted: `map[2]=s;map[3]=-s;map[4]=-2*s;` => harness at heading 0 (flying east): 1:(0,0) 2:(0,+6000 north = left) 3:(0,-6000) 4:(0,-12000). twoShip: `map[2]=-s` => #2 south = right of an east-flying lead, label says '2 | 1'. Code comments contradict the code: 1126 `// right turn: most negative lateral / outside first` sits above `return turnRight ? lb-la : la-lb;` which sorts most POSITIVE first. Note also inferLineAbreastFormFromCurrentState() (1407-1421) infers the label from ascending lateral, so after a turn the dropdown flips to the mirrored label.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename to leftVec/lateralLeft, decide which reading the labels use (facing-forward left-to-right is the usual one) and flip either the maps or the option labels; centralise the formation offset table in one function and pin the presets with a test before changing any sign.

findings.note: heading is math angle (0=east, CCW); input labelled Start heading default 0
findings.title: Start heading is a math angle (0 = east/screen right, increasing turns LEFT), not a compass heading
findings.user_impact: Typing 090 sends the flight up the screen (north), 270 sends it down; entering a heading expecting 000 = north / 090 = east is wrong, and after 'continue after a completed turn' the Start heading box fills in values like 270 after a right turn from 0. Anyone comparing with a real compass or the KML debrief headings will be confused.
findings.evidence: `a.x+=Math.cos(hdg)*v*stepTime; a.y+=Math.sin(hdg)*v*stepTime;` with `worldToScreen` y flipped (y-up) and turnDir -1 for right turns (`selectedDir=$('dir').value==='right'?-1:1`). The Start heading row is labelled just 'Start heading' with default 0. The turn direction sign convention itself is consistent (right = -1 = clockwise on screen, checked with the harness: dir -1 ends at y<0 when flying east).
findings.suggested_fix: Either convert compass<->math at the input/output boundary (hdg = 90deg - compass) or relabel the field 'Start direction (0 = right, CCW)'. Pin the current behaviour with a test first.

findings.title: Continuing after a completed turn silently rewrites Start heading and the Formation preset
findings.user_impact: After Play/Step is pressed a second time (continuation), the Formation dropdown flips between 4312 and 2134 and Start heading changes to the lead's heading. A later Reset/Reset formation then rebuilds the formation with those new values instead of what the user chose, and 'Save as default' stores them.
findings.evidence: prepareScenarioFromCurrentState calls syncFormationDropdownToCurrentState() (`sel.value=inferred;`) and useLeadHeadingAsStartHeading() (`$('heading').value=(rad2deg(lead.hdg)%360+360)%360`) without any indication in the UI.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep 'current formation/heading' separate from the user's chosen preset, or show a note when it changes.

findings.title: Saved default settings lose per-aircraft position errors (Wide/Tight, Fore/Aft) and 'Enable position error'
findings.user_impact: Saving a setup with position errors and reloading the page/default silently comes back with no errors, even though the saved data contained a tight/acute number.
findings.evidence: getCurrentSettings stores only the derived `tight`/`acute` (2054) not latDir/latMag/foreDir/foreMag/errorOn/clockTarget/clockPos/turnLogic. applySettings restores `a.tight=+rec.tight` then calls resetFormation(), whose applyErrors() runs syncAircraftErrorValues(a) first: `a.tight=lat; a.acute=fore;` recomputed from latDir/latMag, which are back at 'none'/0, so the saved value is overwritten with 0. The UI restore loop (`inp.dataset.k in rec`) only matches delayErr/gErr.
findings.suggested_fix: Save and restore the raw fields (errorOn, latDir, latMag, foreDir, foreMag, clockTarget, clockPos, turnLogic) and rebuild the aircraft control panel from them.

findings.title: Closure-rate graph/CSV divides by the fixed 0.05 s even though playback steps are shorter
findings.user_impact: During normal playback the 'Closure' series is wrong by the ratio of the real step to 0.05 s (about one third at 60 fps 1x), and it jitters between correct and 3x too small at 4x speed. The exported CSV carries the same numbers. Only Step and the solver (fixed 0.05 s) are right. (Outside the 779-1400 range but part of the timing; may duplicate the other agent.)
findings.evidence: `closure=prev?(prev.d13-d13)/dt:0;` uses the constant dt=.05, while loop() calls `const step=Math.min(dt,simTime); stepSim(step);` with simTime = frame time x speed. Harness: same turn at t=20 s: true closure 208.7 ft/s; recordHist gave 208.7 with 0.05 s steps but 69.6 ft/s with 1/60 s steps.
findings.suggested_fix: Store the step with each sample (or compute closure as (prev.d13-d13)/(t-prev.t)); ideally use a fixed-step accumulator in loop() so results do not depend on frame rate.

findings.note: 900 divides by devicePixelRatio though worldToScreen already multiplies by it
findings.title: Initial zoom fit is divided by devicePixelRatio, so the formation is drawn too small on high-DPI screens
findings.user_impact: On retina/phone screens (dpr 2 to 3) the formation fits into only 1/2 to 1/3 of the canvas after Reset.
findings.evidence: `zoom=Math.max(0.01, Math.min(0.1, Math.min(scaleX, scaleY)/devicePixelRatio));` while worldToScreen multiplies by zoom*devicePixelRatio and scaleX/Y are already CSS px per ft, so the extra division is double counting.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove `/devicePixelRatio` (zoom is CSS px per ft) and check the slider range.

findings.note: note text says lead starts first; ordering harness-only
findings.title: Maneuver notes and code comments describe a different start order than the code uses
findings.user_impact: 'Delayed 90: lead starts first, wingmen follow sequentially' is shown to the user, but the outside aircraft turns first (for 4312 right it is #2, then #1). The trainee is told the opposite of what the sim shows.
findings.evidence: tacticalOrderForDelayIn() sorts by displayed outside-in order; harness time mode weighted right: first-active 2:0.05, 1:16.05, 3:32.05, 4:48.1. Note text at 2035/2036 says 'lead starts first'.
findings.suggested_fix: Reword the notes to 'outside aircraft starts first, others follow'.

findings.note: grep count 1 for listed helpers (prepareGhostScenario, desiredFormationRelativeOffsets, geometricInitialAutoStarts, ...)
findings.title: Large amount of dead code in the formation/turn setup layer
findings.user_impact: No visible effect, but it hides the real logic (three competing 'auto timing' implementations) and makes the module hard to refactor.
findings.evidence: Defined and never called (grep count 1): desiredFormationRelativeOffsets, desiredFormationPositionsForHeading, lineAbreastOutsideOrderIds, clockCascadeTargetFor, prepareGhostScenario (so ghostAc is only ever set to [] and never drawn), leadTurnProgress, finalLineAbreastFormForAuto, saveAutoTimingState, restoreAutoTimingState, simulateAutoTimingCandidate, geometricInitialAutoStarts, saveSimState, restoreSimState (only used by the dead simulateAutoTimingCandidate), bestFormationAssignmentError, desiredFormationPositionsForHeadingAndForm (only used by the dead ones). Unreachable branches: formation 'fluid' and 'trail' (no <option>), triggers 'leadHeading'/'range'/'bearing' (hidden inputs headingCue/rangeCue/bearingCue at 580-582, trigger select only has time/clock/auto), correction lag/lead/gfix (the 'Correction Model' card is display:none), unused locals in computeOffsetBoxPlan (outerTarget, innerTarget, chosenTarget, chosenName, fourStartsOutside, frontSep, sideDist, frontSecondDelay).
findings.suggested_fix: Delete after the flight-math tests are in place; keep only the closed-form auto timing (or the simulate-and-score one) and one formation table.

findings.note: formation tables written twice (797-849); hook90/inplace90 share branch
findings.title: Duplicate formation tables and identical maneuvers
findings.user_impact: Maintenance risk: fixing a sign in one place leaves another copy wrong; two dropdown entries do the same thing.
findings.evidence: The preset offsets (weighted/weightedReverse/offsetBox/twoShip) are written twice (desiredFormationAircraft and desiredFormationPositionsForHeadingAndForm) and the right/forward unit vectors are recomputed inline at least 9 times (offsetRightVec/offsetFwdVec exist but are used in only a few places). 'Hook turn' and 'In-place 90' take exactly the same branch: `if(man==='hook90'||man==='inplace90'){ d=0; dir=selectedDir; }` and both notes say 'all aircraft turn together'.
findings.suggested_fix: One formation-offset function returning lateral/aft offsets per preset; drop or differentiate 'In-place 90'.

findings.title: Turn trigger option text is garbled: 'Auto timing / equal track / equal track'
findings.user_impact: Cosmetic: duplicated words in the dropdown label.
findings.evidence: `<option value="auto">Auto timing / equal track / equal track</option>`
findings.suggested_fix: Change to 'Auto timing (equal track)'.

findings.note: 2095/2099 startup default loads settings after resetFormation; verified code
findings.title: Unguarded localStorage read at startup can stop the whole main script (Turn Sim loop, KML viewer, module launcher)
findings.user_impact: In a browser or iframe that blocks site data (strict cookie/site-data policy, some managed workstations, sandboxed embeds), touching window.localStorage throws SecurityError. Line 2099 then aborts before loop() runs, so the Turn Sim never animates. Everything after line 2099 in the same <script> also never executes: the KML viewer IIFE (2103+) and the module launcher click handlers (3297+). The app opens to a dead launcher. This breaks the 'usable by anyone, anywhere' rule.
findings.evidence: `function autoLoadDefaultIfPresent(){const raw=localStorage.getItem(DEFAULT_KEY); if(raw){try{applySettings(...)}catch(e){...}}}` - the getItem call sits outside the try. Line 2099: `...initDefaultsUi();autoLoadDefaultIfPresent();loop();`. Also unguarded: `saveDefaultSettings` (2085), `setProfiles` (2078), `loadDefaultSettings` (2086, JSON.parse also unguarded, so a corrupt entry throws), `factoryResetSettings` (2090), `localStorage.setItem('dadEzLastTab',tab)` (3313, 3351). Quota errors on save also throw silently, and the status text never updates.
findings.suggested_fix: Add one `safeStorage` helper (try/catch around get/set/remove, falling back to an in-memory Map). Use it everywhere, including the launcher. Call loop() before any storage work. Report failures through setStatus.

findings.note: SETTING_IDS/CHECK_IDS (2047-2048) omit clock cue, rear-check, breadcrumb and per-aircraft error dirs; saved tight/acute get recomputed
findings.title: Profiles and 'Save as Default' silently drop most of the setup (per-aircraft errors, clock cues, rear-check, breadcrumbs, view toggles)
findings.user_impact: A saved profile restores only about 25 top-level fields. The whole Aircraft Errors card comes back blank: enable position error, tight/wide/fore/aft direction and feet, per-aircraft clock target, clock position and turn logic. The rear-check card (rearCheck*), clock cue settings (clockCueAircraft/Pos/Tol/Sequence), Offset Box #4 timing, breadcrumbs and interval, Follow lead, Lead 3/9 and Clock marks are also lost. After Load, the scenario differs from what was saved, with no warning.
findings.evidence: SETTING_IDS (2047) and CHECK_IDS=['turnCircleToggle','errorLabelToggle'] (2048) omit those ids. getCurrentSettings saves per-aircraft only `{delayErr,gErr,tight,acute,x,y}` (2054). applySettings restores only inputs whose data-k is in that record (2069) and sets a.tight/a.acute (2071). The next resetFormation() -> applyErrors() -> syncAircraftErrorValues(a) (909) recomputes a.tight/a.acute from latDir/latMag/foreDir/foreMag, which were never saved, and errorOn was never saved either. So the saved tight/acute values are overwritten and x/y are never read back.
findings.suggested_fix: Drive persistence from one schema of {id, kind} entries covering every control, including the #aircraftControls fields by data-id/data-k. Save latDir/latMag/foreDir/foreMag/errorOn/clockTarget/clockPos/turnLogic instead of derived tight/acute/x/y. Add a version check on load.

findings.note: applySettings calls updateManeuverDefaults (resets turnDeg) and resetFormation (refits zoom) after restoring
findings.title: Loading a profile overwrites the saved Turn degrees, and the saved zoom is discarded
findings.user_impact: A profile saved with a custom turn angle (e.g. 60 deg) reloads at the maneuver default (45, 90 or 180). The zoom stored in the profile never takes effect, so the view refits to the formation on every load.
findings.evidence: applySettings sets values, then calls `updateManeuverDefaults()` (2064), which unconditionally does `turnDeg.value=90` (or 45/180). Then `zoom = settings.zoom ...` (2062) is immediately overwritten by `resetFormation()` (2065) -> fitFormationView() (900). 'turnDeg', 'zoomSlider' and settings.zoom are saved for nothing.
findings.suggested_fix: Split `updateManeuverDefaults` into a note update (always) and a turnDeg default (only on a user 'maneuver' change). Skip fitFormationView when loading a saved zoom, or drop zoom from the schema.

findings.note: 2089-2090 no confirm; reload hides status; dadEzLastTab never read
findings.module: Turn Sim - Factory Reset / Save / Load / Delete profile buttons
findings.title: Factory Reset and Delete Profile have no confirmation; Factory Reset reloads the whole app
findings.user_impact: One click on the red 'Factory Reset' or 'Delete Profile' button permanently deletes all named profiles and the startup default. Factory Reset then calls location.reload(), which drops the user back to the splash screen. Any loaded KML tracks, 3D state and SOF state are lost. 'Save Profile' also silently overwrites an existing profile with the same name, and the box is pre-filled with 'NFTC Default'.
findings.evidence: `function factoryResetSettings(){localStorage.removeItem(DEFAULT_KEY); localStorage.removeItem(PROFILE_KEY); refreshProfileList(); setStatus('Factory defaults restored. Reloading baseline settings.'); location.reload();}`. The status message is never seen because the page reloads immediately. 'dadEzLastTab' is written (3313, 3351) but never read, so there is no return to the Turn Sim tab. deleteNamedProfile (2089) has no confirm.
findings.suggested_fix: Add confirm() or an inline 'Are you sure?' step. Factory Reset should snapshot the pristine control values at load and call applySettings(pristine) instead of reloading. Warn before overwriting an existing profile name.

findings.title: 'Shackle rollback delay' input does nothing; shackle never holds
findings.user_impact: The visible 'Shackle rollback delay' field (default 2.0 s) has no effect. The maneuver note promises 'hold for the rollback delay', but the aircraft reverse the moment the 45 deg leg finishes.
findings.evidence: `shackleDelay` appears only in the markup (579), the change-listener list (2017) and SETTING_IDS (2047). It is never read. moveAircraftList tests `t < (a.shackleHoldUntil||0)` (1585), but shackleHoldUntil is never assigned anywhere. The phase switch at 1594-1599 sets `turnPhase=1; turnAccum=0; ...` without setting it.
findings.suggested_fix: Either set `a.shackleHoldUntil=t+ +$('shackleDelay').value` at the phase switch, after pinning the current timing with a test, or delete the field, the dead branch and the note text.

findings.note: 1498 +$('clockCueTol') coerces element to NaN so tol is always 4
findings.title: 'Clock tolerance deg' input is ignored (coerces an element instead of its value)
findings.user_impact: Changing 'Clock tolerance deg' never changes when a clock-cue turn triggers. The tolerance is always 4 deg.
findings.evidence: `const tol=+$('clockCueTol')||4;` - `$()` returns the <input> element, so `+element` is NaN and the `||4` fallback always wins. The correct form is `+$('clockCueTol').value`.
findings.suggested_fix: Read `.value` (keep the 4 fallback). Add a small test that the trigger fires at the configured tolerance.

findings.note: clockWait ids never exist in markup
findings.title: Live status lines for clock cue and rear-element check never update
findings.user_impact: The per-aircraft 'Clock cue: waits on #N @ pos' lines never appear. The rear-check status ('waiting until 40 sec / turning left 20 deg / holding / complete') stays as the static markup text during play, and only changes if the user edits a rear-check control.
findings.evidence: updateClockCueStatus looks up `$('clockWait'+a.id)`. No element with an id starting 'clockWait' exists in the markup or in buildControls, so it returns early every time, but it is called from four places. `updateRearCheckStatus` is called only from the change handler at 4135, never from stepSim, resetFormation or the formation dropdown, so its text is frozen.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the clockWait{n} nodes to buildControls, or delete the function. Call updateRearCheckStatus from updateReadouts and on formation change.

findings.note: resetRearCheckState only in resetFormation and 4135, not the prepareScenario paths
findings.module: Turn Sim - rear element check turn
findings.title: Rear-element check turn: state not reset for the next leg, pre-empts planned #3/#4 turns, and leaves a bad heading if reset mid-check
findings.user_impact: (1) Run a leg with the check turn on, then press Play again to continue. The second leg never performs the rear check, because rearCheckComplete stays true. (2) The check starts at a fixed time (default 40 s) regardless of #3/#4 progress. It suppresses the turn logic while it runs (about 10 s with the defaults), so a planned #3/#4 turn start inside that window is silently postponed. The offset-box plan assumes the original start times. (3) Editing any rear-check control mid-check resets phase to 0 while a.hdg is still offset, so the aircraft keeps the wrong heading and the next check uses that heading as its 'base'.
findings.evidence: prepareScenarioFromCurrentPositions/State (1441-1475) reset trail, turnAccum etc. but never call resetRearCheckState, unlike resetFormation (887). `const rearCheckOverride=useErrorsAndCorrection&&stepRearCheckTurn(a,omega,stepTime); if(!rearCheckOverride && cueSatisfied(a,list) && !a.done){` (1584). Handler 4135: `activeList(ac).forEach(resetRearCheckState)` does not restore rearCheckBaseHdg.
findings.suggested_fix: Call resetRearCheckState in both prepareScenario* functions. Gate the check on the aircraft having finished its own turn, or pause the turn timer while checking. On reset, restore a.hdg=rearCheckBaseHdg if phase is 1-3.

findings.title: Breadcrumbs: not reset for a new leg or after dragging; toggling or changing interval mid-run stacks labels at one spot
findings.user_impact: (a) After a run finishes and the user presses Play again, breadcrumbs stop showing timestamp markers for the whole second leg. The old markers stay on screen and the drawn path mixes two time bases. (b) If the user drags an aircraft before Play, the path and the t=0 dot start at the aircraft's old slot, leaving a stray line to its dragged position. (c) Turning 'Breadcrumbs' on mid-run, or editing the interval, drops a stack of overlapping dots labelled 5, 10, 15... at the aircraft's current position.
findings.evidence: resetBreadcrumbHistory is called only from resetFormation (888) and the toggle/interval handler (4138-4144), never from prepareScenarioFromCurrentPositions/State. So nextBreadcrumbTime stays at its old value (e.g. 80) while t restarts at 0. The handler at 4141 resets `nextBreadcrumbTime=interval` and seeds crumbs at (a.x,a.y) even when t is already 40. The `while(t+1e-6>=a.nextBreadcrumbTime)` catch-up loop (1636) then pushes crumbs at the current position for every missed interval. The mousemove drag handler (2023) moves the aircraft but never touches breadcrumbs.
findings.suggested_fix: Call resetBreadcrumbHistory (using the current t) in prepareScenario* and after a drag. On toggle/interval change, set nextBreadcrumbTime to the next multiple of the interval after t. Skip the catch-up loop.

findings.note: 781 #4 colour is black on dark canvas
findings.title: #4 is drawn in black on a near-black canvas: its turn circle, label, clock marks, breadcrumbs and timestamps are effectively invisible
findings.user_impact: For the fourth aircraft, the turn circle (with its 'G / R' label), clock marks, breadcrumb path, dots and time stamps cannot be seen. The trail survives only because of a white shadow glow. Instructors see three aircraft's aids and no aid for #4, the rear/outside aircraft most relevant to offset-box and rear-check work.
findings.evidence: `const colors={1:'#0066ff',2:'#00cc44',3:'#ff2222',4:'#000000',...}` and the canvas is filled with `#071018` (1805). drawPlane special-cases #4 with a white outline (1751) and the trail adds a white shadow (1828). drawTurnCircles (globalAlpha .24, fillStyle colors[4]), drawClockMarks (alpha .45) and drawAircraftBreadcrumbs (1648-1649, label fill 1679) all use colors[a.id] with no white outline.
findings.suggested_fix: Use one high-contrast draw colour for #4 (or a white outline pass) via a single `aircraftColor(id)` helper shared by every draw function.

findings.note: resetFormation runs while simApp hidden (clientWidth 0) so zoom clamps to 0.01; showApp/switchTab only call fitCanvas
findings.title: First open of the Turn Sim is stuck at minimum zoom because the view was fitted while the tab was hidden
findings.user_impact: On first entry the formation is drawn at the smallest zoom (0.01, 60 px per NM). Aircraft and labels are crowded together, and the 500 ft drag radius is only 5 px. The user must press 'Reset formation' to get a proper fit. Labels, distance text and error text pile onto each other at that zoom.
findings.evidence: simApp starts with class appHidden (`display:none!important`, CSS line 58; markup 525). Line 2099 runs resetFormation() -> fitFormationView() while sim.clientWidth is 0, so `scaleX=sim.clientWidth/worldWidth=0` and `zoom=Math.max(0.01,...)`, which pins zoom to 0.01 and the slider to 10. showApp (3314) and switchTab (2172) call fitCanvas only, which resizes the bitmap and redraws but never refits.
findings.suggested_fix: Call fitFormationView() from fitCanvas when the canvas goes from 0 to a real size (or on first show). Guard fitFormationView against clientWidth===0.

findings.note: .toolbar is position:absolute flex-wrap over canvas (line 14); grid min 1240px
findings.title: Toolbar overlays the sim canvas and eats mouse input; fixed 3-column grid clips the right panel on narrower windows
findings.user_impact: The 14+ toolbar items (Play/Pause/Step/Reset, 4 pills, Export, Speed, Zoom, six toggles, interval, plus an injected 'Auto-hide panels' pill) wrap into 2-6 rows drawn on top of the canvas. Aircraft, labels and turn circles near the top are hidden behind the pills. The empty toolbar area also swallows wheel-zoom and aircraft-drag events. The 'drag aircraft before play' footer text is also absolutely positioned over the canvas. On windows narrower than about 1240 px (330+520+390 columns, body overflow:hidden, no media query for main) the right column with Live Spacing, Formation Error and Summary is clipped and unreachable.
findings.evidence: `.toolbar{position:absolute;top:10px;left:10px;right:10px;display:flex;...flex-wrap:wrap}` and `main{...grid-template-columns:330px minmax(520px,1fr) 390px}` with `body{overflow:hidden}`. fitFormationView() fits to the full canvas height and ignores the toolbar. collapsePanelsScript appends another pill to every .toolbar (3403-3410).
findings.suggested_fix: Make the toolbar a normal flow row above the canvas (grid row) and fit the view to the remaining height. Add a narrow-screen layout that stacks or scrolls the panels. Set `pointer-events:none` on the toolbar container with `auto` on its children.

findings.note: resetFormation and change handler (2017) never set running=false
findings.title: Changing settings, 'Reset formation' or loading a profile does not stop or re-plan a running sim; turn circles and the paused-mid-run plan go stale
findings.user_impact: While the sim is running, editing Formation, Spacing, Aft, Stagger or Start heading, pressing 'Reset formation', or loading a profile snaps the aircraft back to t=0 but leaves `running=true`. The sim keeps flying with the OLD turn plan (turnStart, turnDir, turnGoal, delayIndex, AUTO_TURN_STARTS), which can be wrong for the new formation. While paused mid-run, changing Direction, Maneuver, Turn trigger, Base delay or Turn degrees updates readouts but does nothing to the aircraft. Turn circles use a.turnDir left over from the previous Play, so they show the wrong side after the Direction dropdown changes.
findings.evidence: `$('reset').onclick=()=>{running=false;resetFormation();}; $('resetFormation').onclick=resetFormation;` - only the first stops the sim. The change-listener (2017) calls resetFormation/updateReadouts/draw but never setupTurnStarts. setupTurnStartsFor runs only in prepareScenario* (Play from t=0). `const dir=a.turnDir||($('dir').value==='right'?-1:1)` (1857) uses the stale value once turnDir has been set. resetFormation (885) never clears turnDir/turnStart.
findings.suggested_fix: Make resetFormation set running=false, clear the turn plan and call the same prepare routine. Invalidate the plan (or recompute it) on any change to a plan input. Preview the plan pre-Play. Merge the duplicate Reset / Reset formation buttons.

findings.note: prepareScenarioFromCurrentState is a deliberate 'continue after completed turn'; UX note only (silently rewrites Start heading)
findings.title: Play or Step after the turn is finished silently starts a new leg (time resets, Start heading and formation dropdown are rewritten)
findings.user_impact: Pause after everyone has rolled out, then press Play to resume, or press Step to look one more frame: t jumps to 0 and every aircraft begins another turn from the current heading, wiping the trail and history. The 'Start heading' box and, in line-abreast, the 4312/2134 dropdown are silently changed. A later Reset builds a different formation than the user chose, and a saved profile stores the drifted heading.
findings.evidence: `if(t===0||hist.length===0){prepareScenarioFromCurrentPositions();} else if(t>=+$('duration').value || allAircraftFinishedTurn()){prepareScenarioFromCurrentState();}` in both Play (2002) and Step (2011). prepareScenarioFromCurrentState calls useLeadHeadingAsStartHeading() (1463) and syncFormationDropdownToCurrentState() (1462).
findings.suggested_fix: Use an explicit 'Next turn' button for the continue-leg feature. Play/Step should only resume until duration. Do not write back into user inputs (keep the inferred heading/formation in state).

findings.note: 1695 divides by constant dt=.05 while loop steps min(dt,frame)
findings.title: Closure-rate column (and hidden graph) is wrong by the ratio of frame time to 0.05 s
findings.user_impact: 'closure_13_fps' in the exported CSV is about 3x too large at 60 fps and 1x speed (steps are about 0.0167 s), about 12x at 0.25x, and correct only after the Step button. Anyone using the closure numbers for debrief gets wrong values that depend on frame rate and playback speed.
findings.evidence: recordHist: `closure=prev?(prev.d13-d13)/dt:0` divides by the constant dt=.05. loop() steps by `Math.min(dt,simTime)`, so with about 16.7 ms frames each hist sample is one variable-length step. hist already holds t for each sample.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `(prev.d13-d13)/(t-prev.t)` and add a test pinning closure for a known geometry. Better, run the sim on a fixed-timestep accumulator (see the frame-rate finding).

findings.note: trail cap 800, hist cap 2000 samples; two-ship NaN.toFixed gives NaN in CSV
findings.module: Turn Sim - stepping loop / Export CSV
findings.title: Trail and history caps are in samples, not seconds; CSV export and trail lose most of a run and depend on frame rate; two-ship CSV contains 'NaN'
findings.user_impact: With one step per frame, a 75 s default run makes about 4500 history samples, but only the last 2000 are kept. Export CSV therefore omits the first 40 s or so. The coloured trail behind each aircraft keeps only 800 points: about 13 s at 60 fps, about 3 s at 0.25x speed, about 5 s on a 144 Hz display. In two-ship mode the CSV d13/d14/d34/closure columns contain the text 'NaN'.
findings.evidence: `a.trail.push([a.x,a.y]); if(a.trail.length>800)a.trail.shift();` (1611). `hist.push({...}); if(hist.length>2000)hist.shift();` (1697). loop uses `const step=Math.min(dt,simTime); stepSim(step);` (1978). exportCsv calls `r.d13.toFixed(1)` on NaN (2097).
findings.suggested_fix: Sample history/trail on sim time (e.g. every 0.1 s) with a cap in seconds. Write empty cells for NaN.

findings.note: Euler step with end-of-step heading; flight math, pin before touching
findings.title: Aircraft integration uses the end-of-step heading and a frame-length step, so results vary a few feet with refresh rate and Play vs Step
findings.user_impact: The same scenario ends a few feet different at 60 Hz, 144 Hz, different playback speeds, and Step (dt=0.05). The path is shifted by about half a step of travel (roughly 3 ft at 60 fps, 9 ft at dt=0.05 at 220 KTAS). Small next to 6000 ft spacing, but it makes results non-reproducible and gets in the way of pinning behaviour in tests.
findings.evidence: `a.hdg+=(a.turnDir||1)*dth; ... a.x+=Math.cos(hdg)*v*stepTime;` uses the heading after the update. Step length is `Math.min(dt,simTime)`, i.e. frame time.
findings.suggested_fix: Run the sim on a fixed timestep with an accumulator and use the mid-step heading (or exact arc). Do this only after adding a test that pins the current numbers, per the repo rule.

findings.note: 'right' vector h+90deg points LEFT in y-up world while turn dir uses right=-1 (correct). Weighted '4312' draws 2-1-3-4 left to right. Needs Dad to confirm intended picture
findings.module: Turn Sim - formation geometry / error classification
findings.title: Possible left/right mirroring of the 4312 / 2134 presets (vectors named 'right' point left)
findings.user_impact: If the dropdown label follows the usual left-to-right notation, the sim draws the mirror image: with the world y axis up, #2 appears on the left of #1 for '4312' and #3/#4 on the right. Turn direction, turn circles and rear-check direction use the true clockwise = right convention, so 'right turn' and formation side are handled in opposite handedness. This needs owner confirmation before touching it.
findings.evidence: `right={x:Math.cos(h+Math.PI/2),y:Math.sin(h+Math.PI/2)}` is the LEFT-hand normal in the y-up frame (worldToScreen 1713: `y:sim.height/2-(y+pan.y)...`). weighted maps `map[2]=s; map[3]=-s; map[4]=-2*s` along that vector. inferLineAbreastFormFromCurrentState (1413-1418) sorts ascending along it and calls that '4312'. dir 'right' is -1, i.e. clockwise (1857, 1537).
findings.suggested_fix: Confirm the intended handedness with the owner, add a test pinning the current positions, then either rename the vectors to `left` or flip the sign in one shared `formationAxes` helper.

findings.title: Auto-timing side effects and formula: overwrites the user's Base delay; step formula differs from the manual default
findings.user_impact: Playing once in 'Auto timing' replaces the 'Base delay' box (default 16) with the computed value, and it stays that way after switching back to 'Time delay' or saving a profile. The auto delay step spacing*theta/v gives 25.4 s at 6000 ft, 90 deg and 220 KTAS, while the shipped manual default is 16 s (about spacing/v), so the two 'equal-track' knobs disagree.
findings.evidence: `$('baseDelay').value=delayStep.toFixed(2);` (1397) and `delayStep=Math.max(0,(Math.abs(spacing)*Math.abs(theta))/v)` (1390). computeAutoDelay is only reached when triggerMode==='auto' (1449, 1467), so nothing restores the value.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the auto value in its own read-only display and leave the user's baseDelay alone. Have the owner confirm the s*theta/v rule, then pin it with a test before any change. Remove the console.log (1399-1401).

findings.module: Turn Sim - auto timing / ghost / triggers / hidden cards
findings.title: Dead controls and dead code around auto timing, ghost preview, triggers and hidden panels
findings.user_impact: About 100 lines are never run. The Graph, Solver and Correction Model cards are display:none, yet their code still executes. drawGraph() runs every frame on a hidden 0-width canvas, and the graph paints all four spacing metrics in the same white. Trigger modes 'leadHeading', 'range' and 'bearing' can never be selected. Two visible maneuvers are duplicates.
findings.evidence: Never called: saveSimState, restoreSimState, saveAutoTimingState, restoreAutoTimingState, finalLineAbreastFormForAuto, simulateAutoTimingCandidate, geometricInitialAutoStarts, prepareGhostScenario, runScenario, leadTurnProgress, drawGhostPlane (ghostAc is set but never drawn). The trigger <select> (577) only offers time/clock/auto, and headingCue/rangeCue/bearingCue rows are display:none (580-582). `colors[m]||'#fff'` (1965) has no entry for '12','13','14','34'. The hidden solver scans delay from -5 s (negative delays behave like 0, so a tie reports -5.00) and runs 60 x 1500 stepSim calls, each rebuilding three innerHTML blocks. 'Hook turn' and 'In-place 90' behave identically (1217, 2037, 2040).
findings.suggested_fix: Delete the unused functions and unreachable trigger branches. Either restore the Graph/Solver/Correction panels behind a toggle or remove them. Drop 'In-place 90' or give it distinct behaviour.

findings.title: Offset-box-only controls (and rear-check card) are always shown; duplicate 'Direction' label; typo in Turn trigger option
findings.user_impact: 'Offset Box #4 Timing', the whole 'Rear Element Check Turn' card, 'Offset box aft spacing' and 'Offset box lateral stagger' are visible for every formation even though they do nothing outside Offset Box (the rear-check status says so only in small text). Two different 'Direction' fields (check-turn direction and turn direction) sit near each other. The trigger option reads 'Auto timing / equal track / equal track'.
findings.evidence: No script references offsetBox4TimingRow or rearCheckCard to show or hide them. rearCheckConfig requires `form==='offsetBox'&&...` (1535).
findings.suggested_fix: Show or hide these groups on formation change. Rename 'Direction' to 'Check turn direction'. Fix the duplicated words.

findings.note: applyFollowLeadPan in draw (1804) re-pans every frame during drag
findings.title: 'Follow lead' breaks aircraft dragging (runaway drift)
findings.user_impact: With 'Follow lead' checked, dragging #1 before Play makes it drift away from the pointer, because the view re-centres on the lead on every frame.
findings.evidence: mousemove computes `screenToWorld` with the current pan, sets `drag.x/y`, then draw() calls applyFollowLeadPan(), which sets `pan=-lead` and so shifts the next mouse-to-world mapping. Touch devices are not supported at all (mouse events only, 2022-2024), so tablets cannot drag aircraft.
findings.suggested_fix: Ignore followLead while dragging (or disable dragging when it is on). Use pointer events.

findings.note: TIGHT combos coloured cold (1707) confirmed; label collisions are visual, not checked
findings.title: On-canvas label collisions and understated error colours
findings.user_impact: In 4312/2134 the '#1-#4 distance' label is drawn at the exact midpoint of #1-#4, which is #3's icon. The #1-#3 and #1-#4 dashed lines also overlap. Turn-circle labels, breadcrumb time labels, error labels and distance labels have no collision handling, so they pile up at low zoom or short breadcrumb intervals (min 0.5 s). A combined 'TIGHT / AFT' error is coloured blue ('cold') as if it were mild.
findings.evidence: Pairs `[[0,1],[0,2],[0,3],[2,3]]` with `fillText(...,(pa.x+pb.x)/2,(pa.y+pb.y)/2)` (1830). Colour rule: `c.labels.includes('TIGHT')?'cold':'hot'` (1707, 1953).
findings.suggested_fix: Offset the distance labels perpendicular to their line. Colour by the worst label (hot if any non-TIGHT error). Thin out breadcrumb labels when they would overlap.

findings.title: Hard-coded spacing standards duplicated across readouts, drawing and classification; unused variable
findings.user_impact: The 4000-6000 ft interval, +/-250 ft fore/aft and 7000-9000 ft aft windows are repeated as literals in several places. Changing 'Offset box aft spacing' (boxAft) to anything outside 7000-9000 flags #3 as FORE/AFT from the first frame. `const desired=+$('spacing').value;` (1705) is never used. The G-correction formula exists twice (moveAircraftList and currentAircraftGForCircle), so they can drift apart.
findings.evidence: See the numeric literals at the cited lines; `dist(a,ac[0])-(+$('spacing').value*Math.abs(a.id-1))` appears at 1583 and 1845.
findings.suggested_fix: Move the standards to one STANDARDS constant object, derive the offset-box window from boxAft if that is intended, and share one `aircraftG(a)` helper between the sim and the circle drawing.

findings.note: switchTab never pauses Turn Sim; breadcrumbPath unbounded
findings.title: Sim keeps running (and history/breadcrumb arrays keep growing) while another tab is shown; per-step DOM rebuilds
findings.user_impact: Switching to KML/3D/Turn Fight while the Turn Sim is playing does not pause it, so it keeps stepping and burning CPU in the background and is at a different time when the user returns. updateReadouts() rebuilds three innerHTML blocks on every sim step. breadcrumbPath grows without limit (one point per step, redrawn as one polyline each frame), so very long durations or repeated legs slow the canvas. A script error inside loop() appends a permanent red pill to the toolbar each time.
findings.evidence: stepSim calls updateReadouts every step. `a.breadcrumbPath.push({x:a.x,y:a.y,t:t})` has no cap (breadcrumbs is capped at 2000). switchTab never sets running=false. loop's catch appends `.pill` without removing older ones (1987-1991).
findings.suggested_fix: Pause on tab switch. Update readouts once per frame. Decimate breadcrumbPath by time. Show errors in a single reusable status element.
